Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed addressed old comments from his Twitch-streamer ally Hasan Piker as he appeared on the Sunday show circuit to take his first questions from the national media after winning his Tuesday primary.

El-Sayed narrowly won the Democratic Michigan Senate primary over Rep. Haley Stevens, beating her by a single percentage point after being massively outspent during the race. Ahead of Tuedsay, he faced criticism from Stevens and others for campaigning with Hasan Piker, a far-left Twitch streamer whose stunning remark about the 9/11 terrorist attacks has saddled nearly every politician who has appeared with him or accepted his endorsement.

During a 2019 Twitch broadcast, Piker derisively said that America “deserved 9/11” while arguing that American foreign policy was to blame for the attack by al-Qaeda terrorists. On Sunday, El-Sayed was asked by Meet the Press host Kristen Welker, “Do you disavow those comments?”

The progressive Democrat brushed off his ally’s comments as “dumb” and claimed that even Piker had backed away from them. “Of course. Of course it was a dumb statement. I think Hasan himself would say it was a dumb statement. He disavowed it,” claimed El-Sayed. “So yes, America didn’t deserve 9/11.”

El-Sayed then accused both Welker and his remaining critics on the left, some of whom linger after the vitriolic primary, of playing “gotcha politics” and engaging in “cancel culture,” which is generally a line of argument from those on the right politically.

open image in gallery Abdul El-Sayed appeared Sunday on Meet the Press and was pressed on ally Hasan Piker’s 9/11 comment ( NBC - Meet the Press )

“I want to be held accountable for what I say and do, rather than this idea that we’ve, we’re so stuck in cancel culture that we all agreed was a bad idea back in 2020 but we seem to want to bring back,” said El-Sayed.

His response closely mirrored Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s response when she was asked about Piker on ABC’s This Week. Piker himself noted on a stream Friday that he was “tired” of apologizing for the comment, something he said he’d done repeatedly to total disinterest from his critics.

"Much hay was made about the fact that we lost young men in the last election. Many of the same consultants that are wringing their hands today were the same ones talking about how we have to go on Joe Rogan and not be so willing to engage in cancel culture,” said Ocasio-Cortez.

open image in gallery El-Sayed talks poolside with streamer Hasan Piker at a party for content creators supporting his campaign on Aug. 3 in Detroit ( AP )

Progressive Democratic candidates who find themselves aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America and the party’s left flank have refused to disavow Piker himself, under pressure from their centrist opponents. El-Sayed campaigned with Piker over the weekend immediately preceding his primary victory on Tuesday, and other Democrats have appeared on his stream or been the beneficiary of receiving the spotlight his Twitch stream provides over the course of this cycle.

Piker’s presence in the Michigan Senate race was possibly the greatest political test of the effect a firebrand lefty streamer could have on a candidate’s chances.

Both Stevens and El-Sayed’s other former rival, Mallory McMorrow, attacked his campaign over its association with Hasan Piker, only to face a wave of backlash of their own as progressives declared that the fixation on Piker and insinuations that his criticism of Israel were anti-Semitic were, in fact, rooted in Islamophobia. In the end, McMorrow’s campaign never recovered from the steep decline she began with progressive voters once those attacks began, and she dropped out in June.

El-Sayed is in a different position now, however, as he looks toward the general election.

His task remains to win over skeptical independent voters in a state that Kamala Harris narrowly lost in 2020 and Hillary Clinton similarly lost in 2016; he also bears the task of unifying his party after the particularly bitter primary’s conclusion. Fueled mostly by a massive surge of money from AIPAC, the pro-Israel lobby, Stevens and her allies buried El-Sayed under a massive wave of negative advertising which could make his path to victory in November harder — particularly since AIPAC is likely to spend tens of millions more now in support of Mike Rogers, his Republican opponent.

open image in gallery Like El-Sayed, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez commented on efforts to try to get her and other progressives to disavow Hasan Piker on Sunday ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Former US President and Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump shakes hands with US Senate candidate Mike Rogers ( AFP/Getty )

Those ads accused El-Sayed of being connected to Piker, whom they described as anti-Semitic, and even disparaging Michelle Obama, whose popularity within the Democratic Party and in the majority-Black areas of Detroit and Wayne County remains sky-high. Ads even falsely insinuated that Stevens was endorsed by former President Barack Obama, though he did not weigh in on the race.

On Sunday, El-Sayed said that he’d spoken with the former president and hoped Obama would campaign with him ahead of November. The former president has not yet issued an endorsement, but El-Sayed did pick up an endorsement from another former occupant of the White House this weekend: Vice President Kamala Harris.

“Abdul knows we need bold solutions to the crises facing America’s working families, and he is ready to take on this fight. I proudly stand with him to ensure we win a Democratic Senate majority in November,” wrote Harris in a statement.

Andy Burnham has vowed to tackle “rip-off” subscription traps as part of his blitz of policies to tackle the cost of living crisis and provide “everyday fixes” for rising bills.

The prime minister, who will begin a summer tour of the country on Monday, will accelerate plans to force companies to make it easier to cancel subscriptions and provide more information about costs up-front rather than quietly auto-renewing them at a higher price.

Mr Burnham will travel the country during August where he will ask the public how the government can improve their lives, with officials insisting the PM will be in “listening mode” as he vowed to “pull every single lever we can to provide people with some room to breathe on the cost of living”.

The changes to subscriptions, announced in April under Sir Keir Starmer’s government, had been expected to come into force next spring, but Mr Burnham will bring their introduction forward to January.

open image in gallery The PM will begin a summer tour of the country on Monday ( PA Wire )

He will also launch a consultation on adding deceptive discount offers to the Competition and Markets Authority’s list of banned practices.

This would make it easier for the watchdog to punish firms that artificially inflate prices and then immediately offer a “discount” to make a product look much better value than it is.

The prime minister said: “I know people are sick and tired of rip-off discounts and subscription traps. Westminster has got used to telling people that everyday hassles like this are just part of life.

“I don’t think that’s right, especially when the cost of living continues to weigh heavily on so many people’s lives.”

Dame Clare Moriarty, chief executive of Citizens Advice, welcomed the proposals, saying subscription traps and deceptive discounts were “a widespread problem”.

Citizens Advice has previously found 26 per cent of UK adults had accidentally taken out a subscription in a single year, with the government saying its action could save households £14 per month.

Further announcements are expected over the summer, with the prime minister describing Monday’s proposals as “just the start”.

The upcoming tour, which is expected to inform his 10-year plan for the country, will also see Mr Burnham focus on improving high streets.

A spokesperson for the prime minister added he would be “getting out of Westminster and meeting people where they are”.

But opposition figures have criticised his August plans as a “vanity tour” offering only “tinkering”, and urged him to implement broader tax cuts. Meanwhile, there have also been concerns raised over how Mr Burnham’s cost of living blitz will be funded.

It comes after he announced a swathe of policies to bring down bills in his first week in office, including a 20 per cent business rate cut for pubs, clubs and live music venues, a VAT cut to electricity bills, and bus fares capped to £2 from January.

The business rate cut alone is expected to cost the government around £100m per year – but it is unclear how it will be funded.

Mr Burnham is also facing at least a £4.7bn black hole to fill in Sir Keir’s defence spending plan. But announcing that his first Budget will take place on 28 October, chancellor John Healey vowed it would be “built on fiscal discipline”.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham and chancellor John Healey are trying to bring down the cost of living ( PA Wire )

Last month, the prime minister was warned that he will have to raise taxes or cut spending if he wants to fund his new priorities, in a grim analysis by one of the UK’s leading economic think tanks.

Economists at the National Institute for Economic and Social Research (NIESR) cautioned the prime minister and Mr Healey that “there is no capacity to borrow any more” and that inflation will push up the cost of living much higher than the Bank of England (BoE) is forecasting.

Responding to the latest measures to tackle the cost of living, shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said: “Andy Burnham has already run out of ideas.

“The cost of living didn’t become a problem last week, so you have to ask why it has taken Labour so long to enact legislation passed by the previous government.

“Labour’s tax hikes have sent costs soaring for hardworking families and destroyed jobs. Consultations and reheated measures won’t make up for that.”

A significant blaze involving over 20 fire engines is currently being tackled near the A31 in Hampshire, after a vehicle fire rapidly spread to adjacent heathland, emergency services have confirmed.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service reported receiving more than 160 emergency calls regarding a vehicle ablaze on the eastbound A31 at approximately 5.24pm on Sunday.

A substantial response has been mounted, with twenty-six fire engines, four water carriers, six off-road vehicles and multiple command units deployed to the scene near Ringwood.

The fire service detailed the incident, stating: "The fire spread from the vehicle to the central reservation before progressing into nearby heathland.

open image in gallery Motorists have been urged to avoid the area and use alternative routes whenever possible ( AFP/Getty )

“Crews from across Hampshire, supported by colleagues from Dorset and Wiltshire Fire and Rescue Service, are currently attending the incident."

The A31 is closed between Picket Post and junction two of the M27.

Motorists have been urged to avoid the area and use alternative routes whenever possible.

The fire service added: “Please follow diversion signs, allow extra time for your journey and avoid the area to allow emergency crews to work safely.”

Meanwhile, Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service declared a major incident on Sunday as two large fires in woodland put a strain on resources.

Several wildfires have broken out in the UK over recent weeks, including large blazes at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, Headon Warren on the Isle of Wight, Llanwonno in the Rhondda Valleys, South Wales, and the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland.

Hot weather continued to build on Sunday, with the south and south-eastern parts of England expected to have the highest temperatures.

According to the Fire Severity Index, any wildfires are likely to be exceptionally severe on Sunday in almost all of the east and south-east of England.

“Exceptional” severity is its highest ranking.

The Met Office data includes rainfall, temperature and humidity, and agencies use the index to assess the severity of fire if it starts.

It does not cover the chances of wildfires occurring.

Heatwave conditions will likely return next week, with a high of 36C expected in parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday, according to the Met Office.

So far the extreme weather of summer 2026 has included two record-breaking heatwaves in May and June that led to more than 2,800 excess deaths.

Two more heatwaves in July, the driest July in England and Wales since records began in 1836, have fuelled drought and wildfires.

Highlander star Christopher Lambert has pulled out of a fan convention early after undergoing a sudden medical emergency at the event.

The French actor, 69, was rushed to the hospital Saturday after he reportedly collapsed while signing autographs for fans at Steel City Con, according to TMZ. His representative told the outlet he fell ill because blood sugar was low after not eating much that day.

Steel City Con, which is Pennsylvania’s largest annual comic-con, shared an update that night saying that Lambert had to leave due to a “personal issue.” They assured fans that he would return Sunday for autographs and a photo-op, but would miss his scheduled panel appearance.

However, event organizers announced Sunday that Lambert would not be in attendance, writing on Facebook: “Christopher Lambert is unable to come today. He sends his regrets.”

The Independent has contacted Steel City Con for further comment.

Christopher Lambert has dropped out of a fan convention one day after reportedly collapsing while signing fan autographs Saturday ( Getty )

Before the incident, the Pittsburgh-based convention had shared pictures of Lambert posing with fans at a meet-and-greet at the convention, which is held from Friday to Sunday.

Lambert is known for his iconic role as immortal Connor MacLeod in the cult classic Highlander film series, which began in 1986.

He also starred as Tarzan in 1984 blockbuster Greystroke: The Legend of Tarzan, Lord of the Apes. He went on to appear in the 1995 Mortal Kombat video game-to-film adaptation.

After Saturday’s medical emergency, fans shared their concern for the beloved actor with messages on social media.

One person wrote on Facebook: “Prayers for Mr. Lambert. His health and care comes first no matter what. Even though I didn't get to meet him, I saw him interacting with fans...you could see in his eyes how much fun he was having and he was loving every second of being there.”

“‘Another day, Highlander!’ Hope he recovers soon,” one added. Another eventgoer wrote: “I'm glad I met him Friday hope whatever is going on he feels better maybe he can come back. It seems like he did like Pittsburgh.”

The actor went through a similar situation in March 2025, when he underwent a serious back injury after falling down a flight of stairs at a hotel, forcing him to abruptly cancel his scheduled appearance at the SciFiWorld fan convention in Sweden.

Lambert has other fan event appearances scheduled, including next weekend at Fan Expo in Chicago and the weekend after at Mad Monster Expo in North Carolina.

His representatives did not immediately return The Independent’s request for comment.

News.title: Trump claims he’s ‘low-keying it’ with Iran after report he could walk away without nuclear deal
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Donald Trump is taking a wait-and-see approach to Iran as negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and permanently end the war appear to have once again stalled following reports that the president is reportedly considering walking away from the conflict without securing a nuclear deal.

“We are low keying it,” Trump told Axios on Sunday, claiming the U.S. strategy will eventually “work out.”

“We are only semi-negotiating with them,” he added. “We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

The apparent chill from the U.S. comes despite the president’s repeated insistence a deal is near and Iran is desperate for an off-ramp.

In private, the reverse may be true; the president has reportedly floated the possibility of declaring victory even without a deal regarding his top goal to shut down Iran’s nuclear program — so long as the Strait of Hormuz is reopened, according to The Wall Street Journal.

open image in gallery Donald Trump has reportedly considered declaring victory in the Iran war even if a nuclear deal hasn’t been reached ( AP )

Tehran, meanwhile, has spoken of a similar arms-length strategy to negotiations.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday the two sides are not engaged in direct talks and are instead swapping messages via intermediaries.

Vice President JD Vance has offered a different picture, claiming the “same amount of oil” will eventually return to passing through the Hormuz Strait, while describing a deal as neither close nor far.

“We’re really in the middle of the game here,” Vance told Fox News on Saturday.

“This thing is not over. It’s obviously not at the beginning,” he added. “We’re we’re in the middle of the game, and we’re applying a whole host of tools — diplomatic, economic, military tools — to ensure that we get the best outcome for the American people.”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

open image in gallery Over the weekend, Iran laid out a new series of demands on the US before it would consider opening the Strait of Hormuz, including requests for war damages and the end of the American blockade ( Reuters )

This weekend, Iran laid out new terms on the U.S. before it would agree to a deal on the Strait, including ending the war, lifting the U.S. blockade, paying war damages and unfreezing Iran assets.

U.S. officials have said it is Iran that needs to meet conditions before any U.S. policy towards the war changes.

“Once the deal is announced to restore commercial shipping without impediments, the United States will lift the blockade of Iranian ports,” a U.S. official told Reuters.

Hopes were high earlier this week some kind of deal over the vital oil-shipping lane would emerge from negotiations between Iran and Oman.

“There’s been progress made in those talks [between Iran and Oman], but not finality yet. We’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Tuesday.

The more time goes on, the more pressure Trump faces to end the nearly six-month conflict, which he promised would be a swift U.S. victory.

“The Iranians fully believe Trump wants out and is focused on opening the strait, which is why they are playing hardball,” Gregory Brew, an Iran expert at the Eurasia Group, told The Wall Street Journal on Sunday.

Midterm elections are nearing and gas prices remain above pre-war levels.

Making matters worse, the prolonged conflict has reportedly drained U.S. stockpiles of key weapons, prompting the Pentagon to lean on contractors to ramp up production.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli ‘lined up for shock transfer to European giant after entering final year of contract’
Sports.content:
GABRIEL MARTINELLI could be on his way out of Arsenal this summer, according to reports.

The winger lost his place in the Gunners’ first team to Leandro Trossard last season, while Greek winger Christos Tzolis was signed this summer in a £34million deal from Club Brugge.



It has been widely expected Martinelli, 25, would depart for pastures new this summer, even after Trossard’s own exit to Turkish giants Besiktas.

But Martinelli could be set to follow the Belgian to the Turkish Super Lig.



That’s because, according to talkSPORT, reigning league champions Galatasaray have made an enquiry over his availability.

Galatasaray had been in talks to sign AC Milan outcast Rafael Leao and had earmarked Martinelli as an alternative option.



And they have now made contact with Arsenal over Martinelli’s status after failing to engineer a breakthrough in the Leao talks.

SunSport reported earlier in the window that if Martinelli was sold, he would be expected to depart for higher than the club’s current sale record of £35m paid by Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

Whether Galatasaray are willing to stump up that sort of money remains to be seen, but it’s understood Arsenal will only sanction an exit for Martinelli if they can find a replacement.

The North London club had been in talks to sign Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, but saw that deal collapse when the Brazilian signed a new deal through to 2032.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, SunSport looked at six alternative targets Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta could eye this window.

Among them were Paris Saint-Germain and France winger, Bradley Barcola – wanted by Liverpool but rated at £145m by his club – as well as Manchester United and England forward Marcus Rashford, and Athletic Bilbao and Spanish World Cup winner Nico Williams.

But reports have also suggested that Juventus‘ Kenan Yildiz, Atletico Madrid‘s Julian Alvarez, Everton‘s Iliman Ndiaye and Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi are all on their radar too.

A move for the latter star in that quartet seems very unlikely this summer given he is expected to miss at least four months following foot surgery he had at the end of July.

Arsenal kick off their season with the Community Shield against Manchester City next Sunday, before they host newly-promoted Coventry at the Emirates to start their title defence.

But they have not fared too well in pre-season yet, having lost back-to-back against Real Betis and then Borussia Dortmund.

They have Cesc Fabregas‘ Como in their final friendly on Wednesday before the clash with City at Wembley.

Sports.title: Embattled Gianni Infantino dealt fresh humiliation as local Swiss club snubs chance to back him
Sports.content:
SHAMED footie fatcat Gianni Infantino’s local club have refused to back his leadership of Fifa.

Zug 94, based in the luxury Swiss lakeside town where the embattled £4.8million-a-year chief has a penthouse flat, declined to endorse him.



It comes as Europe’s football governing body, Uefa, considers launching an investigation into his 16-year career there.

Infantino yesterday denied claims made by The Daily Telegraph that Uefa paid off an alleged mistress while he was the organisation’s general secretary.



A Fifa spokesman said he “strongly denies the allegations, and they are categorically untrue”.

It called the allegations part of a “concerted effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president”.

Uefa confirmed a departure payment had been made to the unnamed woman, whose salary was said to have been raised at married father Infantino’s request.

Infantino could be challenged in next March’s Fifa presidential election after Football Associations of several nations, including England and Wales, withdrew their endorsements.

Zug 94, who play in the Swiss fourth division and have an average attendance of 400, also dodged offering its backing.

When asked by The Sun if Zug 94 supported Infantino’s continued leadership, a club spokesman said: “We will refrain from commenting on this matter.”



Infantino switched his tax residency from Zurich to Zug in 2022.

He has a £6,500-a-month penthouse apartment overlooking Lake Zug in the Swiss tax haven.

Fifa pays his rent.

Sports.title: WAGs should be offered counselling by clubs because of struggles with trolls, other women & their partners, study finds
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL clubs should offer counselling to the wives and girlfriends of players, the first study on Wags concludes.

The likes of Becky Vardy and Coleen Rooney might need help because of all they deal with, it is claimed.



Researchers at Leeds Beckett University — who spoke to seven women — found that being a Wag could be an “invasive force that could threaten or harm their identity and self-esteem”.

The Wags, aged between 23 and 34, told of their struggles to deal with online trolls, other women, and their own partners.



One said: “I know girls who sleep with football players and then take their watches or ask for a payout, so they don’t tell their wives.”

Others told of death threats over their appearance.

Another added: “There’s an added pressure of being a partner of a player, 100 per cent.”

They all spoke of their own needs having to “take a back seat” for the men.

The researchers found the Wags played a “critical yet under-recognised role in player well-being and performance”.

However, they said that clubs rarely considered their welfare was important.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton in stunning transfer talks over incredible swap involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE and Everton are in talks over swapping Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Both players are thought to be keen on moving and the deal will not involve a fee.



Toffees winger McNeil, 26, nearly joined the Eagles on a loan-to-buy in February but the switch collapsed.

Johnson, 25, has had a torrid time at Selhurst Park since his £35million arrival from Tottenham in January, failing to score in 26 games.



The Wales wideman did, however, lift the Conference League.

It was his second European title in two years, having scored the winner for Spurs against Manchester United in the Europa League final 12 months earlier.

McNeil has played more than 100 games for Everton following his move from Burnley four years ago.

The Toffees have signed Hayden Hackney and Tyrique George for £24m from Middlesbrough and Chelsea respectively as well as Merlin Rohl from Freiburg for £19m.

The Toffees also saw key figures getting released, like Seamus Coleman and Idrissa Gueye.

Palace, on the other hand, landed free agents Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Former Arsenal defender Tomiyasu, 27, was on trial with the Eagles after playing for Japan at the 2026 World Cup and earned a contract after a recent injury hell.

Pierre Sage also replaced Oliver Glasner, who rolled credits on his glittering two-year stint at Selhurst Park that saw him winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

And Palace sold key defender Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea for £51m.

Sports.title: Aston Villa ‘make stunning transfer move for Real Madrid and Brazil World Cup star Endrick’
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA have made a stunning transfer enquiry for Brazilian wonderkid Endrick, according to reports.

Endrick, 20, is down the pecking order at Real Madrid but needs to gain experience to muscle his way up the squad hierarchy.



He will also be hard-pressed for minutes in the senior team because of new boss Jose Mourinho‘s preference for a shorter squad.

That being said, according to AS, the former Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham manager initially did not want the player to leave, before opening the door for his exit due to the limited minutes available.



And the attacker is now set to go out on loan for the second time, following a successful spell at Lyon, where he scored eight goals and added seven assists in 21 games across all competitions.

The report adds Real want to loan Endrick to a team in the Champions League and somewhere he can play primarily in the No9 role.

Roma and Aston Villa are two such teams who match this criteria and have sent proposals to land the Samba star.

In Villa’s case, they want a striker who can deputise for England star Ollie Watkins.

The 30-year-old was the club’s top scorer last season with 21 goals, while second top scorer Morgan Rogers – also the teams chief creator – left to join Chelsea in a record-breaking £117million transfer.

While Endrick might appear to be a good fit for Unai Emery‘s side, Roma are the front-runners to land him.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Bernabeu outfit, Real, announced in December 2022 they had reached a deal to sign Endrick from Palmeiras, before his full arrival in July 2024 when he turned 18.

The fee paid could reportedly rise to as high as £52m, if bonuses are achieved.

Sports.title: Arsenal fans joke ‘don’t let Mikel Arteta see this’ as star assists goal with incredible SOMERSAULT throw-in routine
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fans were left stunned after seeing an incredible somersault throw-in go viral on social media.

And many joked that set piece enthusiast Mikel Arteta would be taking note.



The somersault throw-in came in a Russian second-tier match between SKA-Khabarovsk and Spartak Kostroma.

Spartak’s Iranian defender Nader Mohammadi went over to take a throw on the right side, with his side 2-1 up late on.



The 29-year-old proceeded to somersault during his run-up as he launched the ball deep into the box.

Mohammadi’s remarkable throw was headed straight in by Amur Kalmykov, making Spartak’s three points safe.



And fans on social media were left flabbergasted by the incredible throw.

One joked: “Don’t let Arteta see this, I’m begging you”.

And a second similarly quipped: “Don’t let Arsenal see this”.

A third begged: “Keep arsenal far away from him”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Another added: “When Arteta catches wind of this strategy on his evening scroll tonight, the Premier League is finished”.

This was not the first time that Mohammadi’s throw has gone viral.

In 2021, the defender won his side a corner with a throw from his own half during an Iranian top flight match.

Despite its prowess, his monster throw has so far not been enough to earn an international call-up.

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘set for bumper pay-day windfall thanks to secret Romelu Lukaku clause as striker nears Fenerbahce transfer’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are set to significantly benefit from Napoli star Romelu Lukaku’s imminent move to Fenerbahce with a massive windfall.

Lukaku, 33, joined the Partenopei from the Blues in 2024 after three years in his second stint at Stamford Bridge that also saw him being loaned out to Inter Milan and Roma.



According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Fener and the Serie A giants are closing in on a deal for the striker.

The same source claims the Belgium international has agreed in principle to join the Turkish giants.



The ex-Manchester United star has agreed a two-year contract worth £8.6million, including bonuses.

Negotiations between the two clubs are now in their final stages and the transfer is expected to be completed within the next 24 hours.



It is said the deal could cost at least £9-10m, which is what Napoli are demanding to let Lukaku go.

And that is very good new for Chelsea, who added a resale value on the Belgian after selling him to Naples two years ago.

Napoli agreed to pay the West Londoners a 40 per cent sell-on share of any future transfer.

The deal would work as a massive boost for Massimiliano Allegri’s side as that would remove the ex-Everton star’s £9m annual salary from the wage bill.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Lukaku would be joining a star-studded Fenerbahce side that also signed Nathan Ake and Vedat Muriqi this summer.

The ex-West Brom star will also be linking up with the likes of Ederson, Milan Skriniar, Caglar Soyuncu, Mert Muldur, Nelson Semedo, N’Golo Kante, Matteo Guendouzi, Fred, Marco Asensio and Kerem Arkturkoglu.

Lukaku amassed a total of 15 goals and two assists in 59 appearances across both stints at Chelsea.

Sports.title: ‘Let another gem down’ – Chelsea fans fume as academy hero Trevoh Chalobah completes shock transfer exit to Como
Sports.content:
CHELSEA fans have fumed at the club for letting academy hero Trevoh Chalobah complete a move to Como.

Chalobah joined the club at the age of eight and worked hard to become a key first team player.



The 27-year-old ended up making 151 appearances for the Blues but the England star clearly wasn’t in Xabi Alonso‘s plans.

The club accepted a £31million bid from Serie A club Como and he has now left in a permanent move.



Some Chelsea supporters aren’t happy that another club prospect has been axed and said Chalobah “doesn’t deserve” to be sold.

The club have already cashed in on Tyrique George this summer, while the likes of Alfie Gilchrist and Carney Chukwuemeka left last year.

One wrote on X: “Chalobah doesn’t deserve to leave Chelsea, man loved the club with his whole heart, even when they sent him on loan and wanted him back, he never hesitated to come back. You let another gem down again.”

Another said the exit was “hard to take” and questioned why he had been sold before Benoit Badiashille and Axel Disasi.

A third added: “Two decades at the club just to get forced out to Como so the board can balance the books. Modern football is completely soulless.”

And a fourth wrote: “He wasn’t treated as he should. This young lad loved this club. You guys just wanted him out. I am not happy with that decision.”



And one commented: “If Chelsea cared about players who have team cultural values they would never sell him. Sad.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Chalobah has already broken his silence on the move as he prepares to link up with boss Cesc Fabregas, an ex-Chelsea Premier League winner.

In an emotional post, he wrote: “After 18 years, it’s time to say goodbye to Chelsea. I arrived as a nine-year-old with a dream, and I leave as a man who’s lived that dream in ways I never imagined.

“This journey tested me, lifted me, and strengthened me. To every teammate, coach, staff member, and supporter, thank you for shaping me.



“I gave everything I had, and I’m proud of the person this club helped me become.

“To the young players: the path won’t always be smooth. But stay ready, stay positive, and keep your faith. God’s timing is always right. Thank you all, truly, with love and gratitude.”

Chelsea added: “Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Trev for his years of loyal service and wish him the very best in his next chapter in Italy.”

It will be the second time Chalobah has played abroad after previously going on loan to Lorient in France for the 2020-21 season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He also spent the 2024-25 campaign with Crystal Palace before returning to Chelsea and playing 47 times in all competitions last season.



Chalobah helped Chelsea win the Uefa Conference League in 2025 and the Club World Cup last summer.

Sports.content:

The latest transfer news from around the Premier League and beyond, including updates on potential deals involving Liverpool, Arsenal, Manchester United and Chelsea

Sports.title: Amanda Staveley eyeing London Stadium purchase in West Ham bid – but faces three-year wait
Sports.content:
Amanda Staveley eyeing London Stadium purchase in West Ham bid – but faces three-year wait

Amanda Staveley is looking to purchase a stake in West Ham and she would also look to buy the London Stadium with the major of London open to its sale

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is looking to buy a stake in West Ham (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Amanda Staveley would look to buy the London Stadium if she won the race to buy a major stake in West Ham with the major of London open to its sale.

‌



The Hammers are preparing for a first season in the Championship for more than a decade but there remains a battle to purchase a 25 per cent stake in the club. Staveley, who masterminded the Saudi takeover of Newcastle, is looking to get involved with West Ham.

‌



Any deal could also see her push for the purchase of the London Stadium, which has been the club's home since 2016. It has proved a controversial move with one of the major issues being they don't own the venue. They do however pay a minimal rent - initially £4.4million which halved after their relegation.

‌



The tax payer are footing the bulk of the bill and Sir Sadiq Khan would be open to moving on the asset - which could be available for as little as £50million. A spokesman told The Times: “The Mayor would welcome any discussions regarding the London Stadium that would deliver greater value for money for Londoners.”

Arsenal star Max Dowman produces telling reaction to Viktor Gyokeres miss in surprise loss READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival READ MORE :

One of the major issues in purchasing the 62,500-seater stadium is its athletic use with UK Athletics still having 40 years left on a concession agreement deal that gives them access to the stadium for events such as the London Diamond League.

Khan has also been key in fronting London's bid for the 2029 World Athletics Championships and any changes to the stadium would have to be delayed until after that date if they were awarded the event.

‌



One of the criticisms of the London Stadium is that it remains tailored to athletic events, given it was built to host the 2012 Olympics. The fan's lack of proximity to the pitch and the atmosphere has long been cited as an issue but West Ham have had their hands tied.

View 2 Images The London Stadium could be available for as little as £50m

Staveley and the consortium she is fronting with her husband, Mehrdad Ghodoussi, would have to see off the challenge of Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who is currently a co-owner of the Hammers.

‌



Fellow co-owner David Sullivan went to the team's first game of the season on Saturday despite advice from the stadium's owner to stay away following allegations of sexual misconduct. He has strongly denied all accusations, while he stood down as joint club chairman.

The 77-year-old saw West Ham beat Portsmouth 3-1 in the Carabao Cup, despite London Stadium officials urging him not to attend over safeguarding issues.

Sports.title: Kyle Walker relishing Championship challenge with Burnley - 'I am not becoming anyone's meme'
Sports.content:
It may be more than 15 years since Kyle Walker last graced the Championship, but his mentality hasn't changed.

The veteran defender has not played in the second tier of English football since the 2010-11 campaign, where he briefly starred in the resolute QPR team that would go on to win the league under Neil Warnock. Back then, at the age of 20, Walker was a young prospect with his whole career ahead of him. He returns to the Championship as one of the most decorated right-back's in English football with 96 caps for his country, six Premier League titles and a Champions League triumph all to his name.

But motivation will not be an issue despite all he has accomplished as he prepares for what will be his first ever full campaign in the Championship following Burnley's relegation.

"I think if I have to get motivated to play football, I should stay in bed in the morning," Walkers says. "It's a job that I'm doing that millions want to do. So if you're not motivated to play football and don't win games, I'm definitely in the wrong job."

‌



Walker turned 36 in May but insists the physical demands of an unforgiving 46-game season in the Championship is no cause for concern. He says his physical powers have not waned, attributing his "genetic gifts" to mum and dad.

Former Premier League star punished under new rule days after completing £20m transfer READ MORE :

After amassing an abundance of accolades in the game, Walker already knows he will be a target for ambitious wingers looking to make a name for themselves. But while Walker accepts he will be a scalp, he is adamant nobody will be turning him into a meme.

"I think they try to create, what is it called, memes now? They’ll try and create memes out of me and I can assure you that I am not becoming anyone’s meme," Walker says.

"So when you come against me, I'll give it 100 percent. If you beat me on the day, you know, you shake hands at the end of the game, and you say it's a good game. I'm not rolling out anything to become a meme."

‌



Walker was earmarked for greatness long before he had a chance to truly get to grips with the relentless cut and thrust of the Championship; Tottenham snapped him up from his boyhood club, Sheffield United, in the summer of 2009 after just a handful of senior appearances.

A return to his beloved Bramall Lane followed in the form of a loan spell but it was his temporary stint at QPR which was the catalyst for the trophy-laden career Walker has gone on to enjoy.

"Playing in the Championship - it grounds you, but it also teaches you. It can be very humbling as well," he adds, referencing the wealth of experience that inhabited said QPR dressing room.

View 4 Images Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last season (Image: Alex Livesey)

‌



"We had a very good team. Neil Warnock took me and I played every game and then I went to Aston Villa for the last part of the season. I fell back in love with football a bit - I wouldn’t say I’d fallen out of love - but I went on loan from Tottenham, got called back and didn't really play as many games as I wanted. And then Harry [Redknapp] let me go back [out] on loan to get some games under my belt.

"I loved it. I probably didn’t want to leave to go to Aston Villa because I was playing football and winning every game, but it was something that I needed to do personally to make that step up to the Premier League."

From there, the Sheffield-born defender never looked back. Months later he won his first senior England cap. He then became a staple in the Tottenham team before a blockbuster transfer to Manchester City, where Walker acquired his taste for silverware.

After eight seasons in sky blue, Walker left City permanently last year with 15 major trophies to his name in order to embark on a new challenge with Burnley; a move which presented Walker with an opportunity to escape the 'noise' that becomes a non-negotiable extra for those who operate at the truly elite level.

‌



He explains: "The scrutiny is not as big, but I think then you probably scrutinise yourself more because you’re so used to achieving and winning a lot more games. You look back at yourself and think ‘What could I have done?’.

"Last season, most of all, it was about the mental game. I can play the game of football; that didn’t stop just because I went to Burnley. But mentally it was different and something that I had to channel into. But then that’s something I can pass onto the younger players now and hopefully give my experience."

View 4 Images Burnley and Wolves will both bid to make an instant return to the Premier League along with West Ham (Image: Matt McNulty)

As Walker alludes to, after almost a decade at a club where success has become almost synonymous, last year was a different experience altogether. The beleaguered Clarets suffered a death by a thousand cuts, winning just four Premier League games all season.

‌



There is an "obligation" for he and those who have stayed at the club to right the wrongs of that chastening campaign, says Walker, who adds that relegation has left a "sour taste" in the mouth.

While some have moved on, he had no qualms about returning to the level that helped truly elevate his career, even if a Championship encore was not on his footballing bucket list.

"It’s our job," he says. "Things aren’t always going to go as planned. This season might not go as planned. It might not be as plain sailing as we all want it to be. But I feel with the quality, what we have in the dressing room, that’s what we should be doing: getting promoted and going back to the Premier League."

Nicky Hayen has been tasked with achieving that feat following a protracted manager search earlier this summer. The Belgian previously impressed with Genk and Walker's first impressions of the 45-year-old have been positive.

‌



"He has been great," says Walker of Hayen. "The information he has given is key, he is very direct and I feel when a manager comes in they can give you sometimes too much information."

Burnley have immediately been installed as one of the favourites for promotion and Hayen will harbour ambitions of emulating the feats overseen by Vincent Kompany. Walker's former Manchester City team-mate masterminded a memorable promotion campaign for Burnley back in 2022-23, losing just three games and racking up an impressive 101 points.

View 4 Images Walker has picked the brains of his former Manchester City team-mate and Burnley manager, Vincent Kompany (Image: Nathan Stirk)

Walker has already picked the brains of the Bayern Munich boss, revealing: "I've spoken to Vinny, I've got words from him. How did he find it after achieving what he’s achieved? He says it’s difficult. It is something that is going to be attached to yourself personally [the expectation to win] but it is also very enjoyable.

‌



"You become a big fish again, and you get a little bit more of the ball, and it's a bit more of the game that I'm used to playing at Manchester City.

"So, hopefully, we can replicate that for when Vinny went up because I think they broke 100 points and kind of tore the Championship apart."

Now in the twilight years of his career, Walker argued that staying up last season would have been equivalent to a seventh Premier League title. That wasn't to be, but a Championship crown would go some way to quenching Walker's insatiable thirst for more achievements.

"There's always losing in football and there's always achieving in football," Walker says. "All the time I've got a football shirt on my back, I'll always give my all and I won't settle for anything less. I've got a bar for myself, but I've also got a bar more importantly for the team, and if anyone falls underneath that, then they will be told that it's not acceptable.

‌



"But hopefully, from what I've seen in pre-season, what I've seen in training, and obviously from the manager and everything like that, we're all going in the same direction — and that's to get this club back to the Premier League."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso steps in as new Chelsea set-piece coach in heated clash with rival

Chelsea were held during pre-season as they drew with Johor Darul Ta'zim but tempers flared on the touchline which saw new Blues coach Austin MacPhee at the centre of the scuffle

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso had to step in to pull apart an incident on the touchline

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was forced to step in and pull one of his coaches away from a brawl as tempers flared during their pre-season friendly with Johor Darul Ta'zim.

‌



The Blues have just hired Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa and he reacted angrily after seeing Chelsea striker Liam Delap on the receiving end of a nasty challenge. With just over an hour on the clock, defender Antonio Glauder went through the back of Delap with a strong tackle.

‌



His Chelsea team-mates were left fuming with the challenge as centre-half Tosin Adarabioyo lead the response. The Blues’ new set piece coach MacPhee was also raging, which saw Alonso having to hold him back after a clash with one of the Johor coaching staff

‌



Delap, who had converted two penalties during the match, was able to continue and Glauder went on to score a late own goal which allowed Chelsea to secure a 3-3 draw.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Chelsea and Real Madrid eye Martin Zubimendi as Arsenal set price after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

The Blues will now head home from their Far East tour with Alonso's side playing Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on Saturday ahead of their Premier League opener, which sees them head to neighbours Fulham on August 24.

MacPhee has been bought in from Aston Villa as Alonso assembles his own staff in west London. MacPhee and his long blonde locks had become a fixture alongside Unai Emery and he was crucial behind the scenes as the Midlands side enjoyed their recent success.

‌



Chelsea are embarking on another season which has them being led by a new manager. The club's owners have not yet stuck with a manager for more than 18 months but none of their hires have had the pedigree of Alonso.

View 2 Images The new Chelsea coach reacted angrily to a challenge on Liam Delap

The Spaniard arrives having led Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen. His spell in Spain was short lived but by no means a disaster and his work in Germany sees him held in high regard. With Leverkusen he won the Bundesliga, ending Bayern Munich's dominance, and also claimed the German Cup.

Article continues below

Chelsea are looking to bounce back from a dire campaign that saw them finish in mid-table and go through three managers as Enzo Maresca, Liam Rosenior and Calum McFarlane all had spells leading the team.

Sports.title: Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'
Sports.content:
Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'

Mikel Arteta has been asked if fans can expect more signings before the transfer window closes with Arsenal still in the market for a new defender

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal are in the market for more signings (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta has admitted that Arsenal are pushing to sign more players before the end of the transfer window.

‌



The Gunners have spent more than £100million on new players this summer. Piero Hincapie's loan move from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent in a £34.5m deal, Christos Tzolis made the £34m switch from Club Brugge, Illan Meslier has signed after his Leeds contract expired, and Bruno Guimaraes has joined for £75m from Newcastle.

‌



But Arsenal, who go into the season as the reigning Premier League champions, are not expected to stop there and want to bolster their squad with more additions in the coming weeks. Indeed, following the Gunners' 3-2 pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, Arteta revealed the club remain active in the summer window.

‌



Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands READ MORE :

Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality READ MORE :

"Well, that's what we're trying to do [sign more players]," Arteta said. "If we have the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal have conceded six goals in their last two pre-season matches; three against Dortmund and then three in the 3-1 defeat to Real Betis last Wednesday. In both matches, the Gunners looked open at the back and in truth Dortmund and Betis could have scored more than three each.

View 2 Images Jurrien Timber and William Saliba are still out (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Although it is just pre-season, concerns have been raised about Arsenal's capabilities in defence without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, with Cristhian Mosquera and Ben White both struggling in the Betis and Dortmund matches. Ezri Konsa has been listed as a top target as the Gunners look to strengthen at the back, though Aston Villa are determined to keep the £35million-rated England international.

When asked if a defender is a position the Gunners are trying to sign, Arteta added: "I wouldn't go there just to put an isolated there. We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"In the way we competed, especially. But that's a very collective responsibility. So, we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve for sure."

Arsenal go up against Como in their fourth pre-season fixture on Wednesday. They then face Manchester City in the Community Shield next Sunday before their Premier League curtain-raiser against Coventry City.

Sports.title: Inside Italy's talks with Pep Guardiola and real reason he snubbed job amid England links
Sports.content:
Inside Italy's talks with Pep Guardiola and real reason he snubbed job amid England links

Italy pursued Pep Guardiola this summer and can close to landing him as their next manager - but the former Man City boss ultimately wanted time away after also saying no to England

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was offered a return to management just weeks after leaving Man City (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Paolo Maldini has claimed that Pep Guardiola was so close to becoming the next Italy boss that he started jotting down possible line-ups on a piece of paper.

‌



Maldini was hired by the Azzurri in the aftermath of their World Cup qualification failure as they looked to rebuild. His remit was to hire a new manager and, after eyeing up Carlo Ancelotti, they turned their attention to Guardiola after his Manchester City exit.

‌



Talks were held with the Catalan, who has ambitions to manage in the international game. Maldini admits that Guardiola's decision to turn down the job was purely based on his desire to take some time out after a decade at the Etihad.

‌



The 55-year-old wasn't motivated by money and Maldini claimed in an interview with Corriere della Sera: "Guardiola told us: 'Give me one euro less than what the last coach was earning and I am ready'."

Roberto Mancini named new Italy manager as Claudio Ranieri makes shock return READ MORE :

Italy in turmoil as legend ready to quit 16 days into job after manager pick blocked READ MORE :

After holding talks with Guardiola in Barcelona Maldini revealed: "With Guardiola we studied the lists of players, starting from the under-17 team and above" and said that he "even began writing out line-ups".

After the ex-City boss and Ancelotti had turned down the role Maldini turned to Andrea Pirlo, one of the players who helped Italy claim the World Cup in 2006. Since retiring he's led the likes of Juventus and was poised to take the role before several of the country's chiefs intervened due to his association with Russian betting firms.

‌



Maldini stepped down from his role with Italy after less than three weeks once Pirlo was denied the chance to lead the national side. Italy have since appointed Roberto Mancini for a second time.

View 2 Images Paolo Maldini thought he had his man when he pursued Pep Guardiola

Guardiola is poised for a period out of management, which is timely given he's been in charge of a club for 13 years in succession. Before City he had three years at Bayern Munich.

‌



Guardiola reportedly had a verbal agreement in place with England before they turned to Thomas Tuchel. He was seen as a successor to Gareth Southgate once he stepped down two years ago, and his hire would've been a major coup for the FA.

When it came to it though Guardiola chose to renew his contract with City midway through the 2024/25 season, spending another 18 months at the Etihad.

Tuchel's position has come under scrutiny following England's collapse against Argentina in the World Cup semi final. But any change is unlikely after the Football Association granted Tuchel a new contract before the tournament began.

Sports.title: Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat
Sports.content:
Arsenal next transfer priority is clear after Vinicius Jr blow and Borussia Dortmund defeat

ARSENAL 2-3 BORUSSIA DORTMUND: Mikel Arteta's Gunners conceded three goals for the second consecutive match on Sunday as they returned home to face BVB in the Emirates Cup

View 3 Images Arsenal looked vulnerable at the back as they were beaten 3-2 by Borussia Dortmund

Don't read too much into pre-season friendlies, unless of course, you are a defensive mess. Less than two weeks out from their Premier League opener against newly-promoted Coventry City, champions Arsenal are still getting warm.

‌



But having now shipped three goals in two consecutive defeats to Real Betis and Borussia Dortmund, it's becoming difficult to decipher whether this is merely ring rust or a glimpse into what life may really look like without William Saliba.

‌



Context is crucial because just over one year ago, the Gunners were stunned 3-2 at home by Villarreal in a similarly sketchy contest.

‌



A clean sheet in a ruthless 3-0 demolition of Athletic Club and one of the most-historic campaigns in the club's illustrious history then followed.

But it can also be true that Arsenal currently look fortunate that none of their direct rivals, outside of Tottenham, have drastically strengthened to date.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands READ MORE :

While they remain firm favourites to retain their crown, their backline just isn't clicking in the absence of imperious Frenchman Saliba and there's an alarming lack of defensive depth.

‌



Ben White, who managed just 12 top-flight appearances last term is back following his MCL injury but Arsenal are currently placing great faith in his fitness record with Jurrien Timber still sidelined.

The Gunners were sliced apart for BVB's opener inside seven minutes and then exposed again as Konstantinos Karetsas, a prodigy Arsenal tracked last summer, bent home admirably.

Then just moments after Ethan Nwaneri handed Arsenal a lifeline, Arsenal were undone via a messy and chaotic set-piece.

‌



Forget marquee big-name Vinicius Junior alternatives, a versatile defender should now be among Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta's top transfer priorities

It's not time to hit the panic button yet as it's been a slightly odd pre-season all-round this summer, not just for Arsenal.

Another injury and the narrative quickly changes, however. The first expanded 48-team World Cup was gruelling for all parties, on all levels.

‌



View 3 Images Konstantinos Karetsas scored a stunning goal for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal (Image: Justin Setterfield)

The whopping 104-game tournament was brutal on body clocks, a mental slog and that's without even considering the actual physical toll of the participating players' workload on the back of a long domestic campaign.

Arsenal, arguably more so than any other Premier League club, need to manage their stars carefully from here on in.

‌



The champions went deep in all four competitions last term while Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Gabriel Magalhaes and Saliba were all managing varying degrees of pain.

The latter ultimately paid the ultimate price for his bravery but Arteta cannot afford to witness Rice or Gabriel, in particular, break down this season as they are just too important to their Premier League title defence.

View 3 Images Gabriel Magalhaes started for Arsenal but they were still poor defensively

‌



Perhaps it's naive to perceive there will not be consequences somewhere along the line, which underlines the importance of strong recruitment work from Berta.

Bruno Guimaraes' £75million arrival - the Brazilian midfielder was presented to the Emirates Stadium crowd pre-kick-off - will help protect Rice's conditioning.

Sufficient defensive cover is also required and with just over three weeks left of the transfer window, there is still work to do.

‌



Guimaraes, now likely to debut against Como after watching on from the stands, is unquestionably a top acquisition but Arteta's left flank - one key area where there was scope for improvement - is not conclusively better than it was last season despite Christos Tzolis' eye-catching start to life in north London.

Next weekend's Community Shield collision with Manchester City in Cardiff should represent a strong yardstick as to where Arsenal are really at. Losing that fixture would not be ideal preparation for Coventry.

Sports.title: Liverpool show familiar concern as three players shine in Monaco defeat - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool show familiar concern as three players shine in Monaco defeat - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-3 MONACO: The Reds were beaten by the Ligue 1 club in Andoni Iraola's first match at Anfield as their new manager

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola, Manager of Liverpool (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images)

Liverpool suffered a 3-2 defeat to Monaco in Andoni Iraola’s first match as manager at Anfield. The Reds boss will have plenty to ponder after the latest pre-season outing for the club as the Premier League campaign nears.

‌



Alexander Isak opened the scoring for Liverpool in the first half, before Florian Wirtz doubled the home side’s advantage with a finish almost on the goalline.

‌



Monaco then responded with a penalty from Aleksandr Golovin, before Mika Biereth equalised for the Ligue 1 club in the second half and Paris Brunner got the winner in the closing minutes.

‌



Here, Mirror Football takes a look at some of the key talking points from Liverpool’s pre-season friendly against Monaco.

Liverpool given Ronald Araujo transfer update as Hansi Flick makes Barcelona admission READ MORE :

Darwin Nunez has given thumbs up to Liverpool transfer as deal gets seal of approval READ MORE :

Isak clinical

Alexander Isak wouldn’t have wanted to wait long before getting his first goal at Anfield, and it took the Sweden international just 16 minutes to find the back of the net.

Isak had plenty of good link-up play with Florian Wirtz throughout his appearance, and it’s easy to see from the start how important Iraola views the two players.

‌



Liverpool will be hoping that Isak’s goal marks the start of the striker showing the form that earned him his move to Anfield 12 months ago.

View 2 Images Alexander Isak of Liverpool (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Iraola impact

Anfield got its first chance to see an Iraola-Liverpool team, and it wouldn’t have taken long to see the message the 44-year-old is sending to his players.

‌



From the very first kick-off, Liverpool made their intentions clear to get the ball up the pitch as soon as possible to try and attack. While it left the defence open at times, it led to several opportunities, including the goals from Isak and Wirtz.

Wirtz pulling the strings

Wirtz showed before his move to Liverpool why he is regarded as one of the most talented youngsters in Europe, and there was a glimpse of that once again against Monaco.

Most of Liverpool’s attacks went through the Germany international, and he can find himself unlucky not to have found the back of the net on more than one occasion.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ndukwe a gem

Liverpool certainly have a talented youngster on their hands with Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who once again put in an impressive performance during pre-season.

The defender made several important blocks in the first half and looked like he belonged at the heart of the Reds defence alongside club captain Virgil van Dijk.

‌



The teenager will be expected to be loaned out this summer due to not having a work permit to feature for Liverpool, but the Reds definitely have a gem on their hands.

Familiar concerns

Just like they did against Leeds United last week, Liverpool seemed to run out of steam as the game went on and Monaco capitalised.

After scoring twice in the first half, Monaco managed to respond and take the lead after Liverpool began making changes with various substitutions.

Article continues below

Iraola will want Liverpool to be able to put in a consistent performance across the full 90 minutes as soon as possible, particularly with the Premier League season starting in just two weeks’ time.

Sports.title: 'Very pathetic' - Koepka fumes after missing FedExCup playoffs
Sports.content:
Brooks Koepka labelled missing the FedExCup playoffs "pathetic" in a brutally honest assessment of his game after a low finish at the Wyndham Championship.

The five-time major champion, back on the PGA Tour after a four-year hiatus with LIV Golf, posted a final-round 70 at Sedgefield Country Club on Sunday.

Koepka was tied for 70th when his round finished, way short of the fourth-place finish he needed to secure qualification for next week's St Jude Championship.

"I struck the ball great," Koepka explained. "It's just all on the greens. I don't know what the deal is.

"Got zero confidence, can't putt. I don't know. There's going to be a lot of changes here soon."

Asked to sum up his disappointment at missing the playoffs, Koepka didn't hold back, adding: "Pretty disappointed. I think it's pretty pathetic that I can't get through.

"Zero top-10s basically in two years. To be in the prime of my career and be as good as I think I am, I think that's very pathetic, disappointing.

"I just need to go home and completely re-evaluate everything."
