Sports.title: Why Honda only realised the scale of its F1 problems in January
Sports.content:
Heading into Formula 1's major technical overhaul, expectations at Aston Martin were high. With a state-of-the-art factory in Silverstone, legendary designer Adrian Newey and a works partnership with Honda, all the ingredients for success appeared to be in place.

That may still prove to be the case in the longer term, but the start of the new era has proved far more challenging than anticipated. Mike Krack recently admitted that Aston Martin had barely been racing before the summer break, simply because the gap to newcomer Cadillac amounted to around one second.

That changed when the AMR26 received its first major upgrade package in Hungary, although the chassis is naturally only part of the story. Honda has also encountered numerous problems since officially returning to F1, ranging from vibrations that troubled the drivers during the opening weeks of the season to a significant deficit in outright performance.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Autosport, trackside manager and chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the full extent of those problems only became clear in January.

“So, probably at the end of last year, our position was not so bad,” he said. “Still, performance and drivability were in the development stage, but it looked okay.

"But in January, we realised that in some of the areas we found some, not issues, but we realised that performance was always up, down, up, down. So we found some performance, but then we also found some reliability issues."

Shintaro Orihara, Honda Photo by: EYE4images / NurPhoto via Getty Images

Because reliability is always a top priority, Honda had to take a step back on several performance gains to ensure reliability at that performance level. Naturally, that slowed down its overall development.

"In January, we realised that our performance and reliability would not be competitive,” Orihara added. “When we started running in Barcelona, we realised that our performance was definitely poor compared to the other manufacturers. And also, we found some issues on the battery side."

Those battery-related issues made the development process more complex. They cost valuable track time during winter testing, something that was especially painful given Aston Martin and Honda's need to gather data to recover from their deficit.

"So we realised that we were not in good position, maybe at beginning of this year. Last year, at end of last year, we already saw that we were not competitive, but we didn't expect it so bad," Orihara admitted.

What has been Honda's biggest challenge?

Part of the explanation is that Honda's current F1 project is very different from its successful years with Red Bull, something that ties in with the company's philosophy of transferring F1 knowledge to other parts of the company.

Another part of the explanation is, according to Honda, the complexity of the current regulations. Orihara stressed that there has not been one single stumbling block ahead of 2026, but rather the combination of all the changes introduced at the same time.

Honda Power Unit Launch

"It's difficult to say which component of the power unit is most challenging because in this regulation, everything has changed a lot,” said Orihara. “For example, MGU-K power changed from, let's say, [120] to 350 kilowatts. That is a significant change.

"But also on the internal combustion engine side, we have changed the fuel flow rate. So in this regulation, everything has been changed so much. So, a challenging point for Honda is just the combination of a lot of changes happening at the same time."

That means Honda is lacking outright power from its internal combustion engine, something the long-awaited Zandvoort upgrade is specifically designed to address. It is intended to be the first step towards reducing the brand's still significant performance deficit.

On the electrical side of the power unit, the emphasis is on efficiency. However, Orihara explained that the changes there have also had a major impact on drivability – one of the areas that has been a recurring topic for Honda and Aston Martin in the opening months of the season.

"Removing the MGU-H has also been quite challenging on the power unit side,” he said.

“Probably that is the most exciting point for power unit manufacturers. I have always been mentioning drivability. That is, maybe not mainly, but the majority of that is coming from removing the MGU-H.

"So that is a challenging point for us as a power unit supplier, to keep the boost pressure at a target. Again, it's difficult to pick one component that has been most challenging for us, but it has been the combination of all changes at the same time."

Although Honda knows that returning to the competitive level it is targeting will take time - a lot of time - it hopes to make a first step at Zandvoort. That upgrade is focused purely on improving the internal combustion engine and was already tested during a filming day at the Hungaroring.

Sports.title: Why McLaren has been coy about introducing its rotating F1 rear wing
Sports.content:
McLaren will race its version of the so-called 'Macarena' rear-wing concept – but not until an unspecified point in the future, according to team principal Andrea Stella.

It's understood that the reason for not rushing to race the new rear wing is not linked to Red Bull's well-documented issues with its similar design. Instead, McLaren is being cautiously pragmatic, since the rotating rear wing adds to the complexities of managing car behaviour as it moves in and out of Straight Line Mode (SLM).

McLaren planned to test its new wing in Austria but made a late decision to abandon the evaluation. It then waited until Hungary to run it for the first time in FP1 on Oscar Piastri's car, driven by Leonardo Fornaroli, before parking it for the remainder of the event.

Max Verstappen crashed at the Red Bull Ring and Silverstone, prompting his Red Bull team to temporarily shelve its pivoting rear wing based on suspicions that a delay in airflow reattachment when the wing returned to cornering mode made Verstappen's car unstable.

"I have to say it's been a complicated project," Stella told media including Autosport.

"Which was no surprise because when we saw Ferrari introducing the wing in Bahrain test and testing it in China in the first lap, [Lewis] Hamilton spun. And then it took a few more events to actually being in condition to race it.

"We knew it was going to be a complex project, so I have to say that our engineering department has delivered this project in a way that looks well-behaved – like the wing in terms of mechanical actuation, times of the actuation, because there's some limitations by the regulations, not only for aerodynamic reasons.

Ferrari was the first team to run its rotating rear wing, which operates differently to the McLaren and Red Bull examples Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"And then the overall behaviour from an aerodynamic point of view, reattachment – so the time it takes for the car to regain the load, not only the load on the wing, the load on the entire car as driven from the wing.

"All this I have to say has been pretty consistent with expectation, so it's been a positive sign off of this concept and we look forward now to introducing this concept at some future events."

These concepts are a classic example of thinking-outside-the-box creative engineering that is possible for the first time this season because the regulations are relatively open. F1 first adopted the principle of legally shedding drag in a straight line with the Drag Reduction System (DRS) in 2011, which permitted the upper rear wing plane to flatten in prescribed areas of the track.

The speed and actuation procedure for this was clearly defined, along with the dimensions of the wing planes themselves. But under the new ruleset introduced this season, in which front and rear wing flaps can open in specified Straight Line Mode zones, the speed of transition from one state to the other is defined (within 0.4s), but not the means by which it moves between open and closed.

McLaren's pivoting rear wing is closer to Red Bull's than Ferrari's, in that it uses a central actuator to manage the rotation rather than having a mechanism built into the endplates. Also like Red Bull's, it pivots forwards rather than backwards.

The means of actuation gives it an element of air braking as it closes. The trade-off between the two concepts is that Red Bull and McLaren accept a degree of aerodynamic blockage from the actuator and its shroud in exchange for having a wider space between the upper and lower planes when SLM is active.

Ferrari's also has to take a longer path between open and closed because of the angle of rotation.

Verstappen shunted in qualifying in Austria, and a delay in airflow reattachment to the rear wing was cited as one possible contributory factor Photo by: Getty Images

One of the less predictable effects of the new regulations has been the shift in tyre loading during the transition between SLM being on and off. This is because the airflow doesn't reattach to the wing planes instantly, but takes fractions of a second to re-establish its path.

Teams knew ahead of the season that this would be a significant performance factor, but were unable to measure it accurately with simulation tools such as the wind tunnel and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD).

The true extent of the shifts in loadings, and their effect on car behaviour, could only be measured at the track.

This also applies to the theoretical benefits of the rotating rear wings. The airflow around the rear of an F1 car is tremendously busy because of the interaction between the car's aerodynamic surfaces and the turbulent wake of the rear wheels.

Simulating this with great accuracy is very difficult in the wind tunnel, where model size is capped at 60% scale and the wind is generally blowing in one direction. Historically it is difficult to access a car's aerodynamic performance when it's in a state of yaw (i.e. turning), or facing different wind directions. The different deflection properties of the model tyres, as well as their smaller size, also has a tendency to skew results.

Hence McLaren has done a lot of FP1 running with large aero rakes fitted behind the rear wheels to validate substantial bodywork changes such as the latest-spec floor, introduced in Hungary, as well as its pivoting wing. Practical measurements trackside are the real proof (or otherwise) of any theoretical gains.

"There was a question about comparison with Red Bull, but I don't think the wind tunnel is a major factor in terms of determining the aerodynamic behaviour in reattachment," Stella said.

"I think you can use some other tools for that, and then the most important tool, especially when you have this sort of complicated project, even from an aerodynamic point of view, remains what you observe at the track. So it was important for us to acquire data here trackside, because you would have never relied on a wind tunnel only for such a delicate project."

Sports.title: Why the FIA couldn't intervene sooner over F1's 2026 rules
Sports.content:
With the first Formula 1 season under the new technical regulations approaching its halfway point, the summer break provides a good opportunity to take stock. The 2026 rules, with their much greater emphasis on electric power, have sparked considerable debate both in and outside the paddock.

F1 insists that fan ratings – for example in its own Formula 1 Fan Voice programme – have been largely positive, but drivers have been far more critical.

Max Verstappen described the power unit regulations as "Formula E on steroids" during winter testing in Bahrain, while Oscar Piastri spoke at Spa-Francorchamps about the "self-learning elements" of the power units and "qualifying grids being decided by computers behaving or misbehaving".

Asked by Autosport whether the criticism from drivers over the past few months had been stronger than the FIA expected, Tombazis responded: "I think drivers are, by definition, quite demanding clients. I don't think we expected them to have a sugarcoat or to not speak their minds. So to say that it's been more than expected, no, I wouldn't say so."

The complaints from drivers about energy management, super clipping and algorithms were also in line with what the FIA had anticipated, according to its single-seater director.

"We did anticipate a lot of these things that they have complained about in the two years before the launch of the season. We did try to make some adjustments, but we failed with the governance that was in place," Tombazis said. "So I think it was realistically only to be expected."

Energy-starved circuits such as Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps have highlighted the shortcomings of the 2026 regulations Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

FIA tried to listen to F1 drivers' criticism in build-up to 2026

If it had been up to Tombazis, the changes to the regulations that have now been agreed for 2027 and 2028 – to gradually move to a 60-40 split – would ideally have been introduced much earlier.

"I think it's a bit of a shame that we had to wait until we discussed things in May and get to a package for 2027 and for 2028. I think we could have ideally done that a couple of years before and then there wouldn't have been all of this discussion," Tombazis said.

Several drivers warned about potential problems with the new engine regulations before 2026. Verstappen was the first to do so publicly during the 2023 Austrian Grand Prix, when Autosport asked him about his initial simulator runs with the new engine formula.

That has perhaps created the impression that drivers were not listened to in the years leading up to 2026, but Tombazis insists the reality is different. According to him, the initial feedback was taken seriously, but the governance framework meant the regulations could not be significantly revised.

"When OEMs decide to participate as PU manufacturers, they sign a governance agreement that is binding towards all parties, so the FIA, FOM and the PU manufacturers. It's similar to what the Concorde Agreement does for the team side of things," Tombazis explained.

"And there was a separate governance agreement signed in 2022 in order to basically outline the requirements for the PU manufacturers during the years of 2023, 2024 and 2025. That is before the championship started because there's such things like financial regulations for the first time."

The FIA states that governance, even with new manufacturers such as Audi, has made intervention impossible Photo by: Pirelli

Among other things, that agreement stipulated that new entrants would not be allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to develop their 2026 power units.

"If a PU manufacturer who was not participating in Formula 1, let's say Audi, they still had to be bound by regulations and not come to us and say, well, we're not participating, hence we can spend five times the money. That would be unfair," he said.

"So that's why there was a governance agreement that on the one hand forced them to be bound by the regulations, including the financial and operational rules and all of that."

At the same time, that document made it much harder for the FIA to reopen the regulations in the years leading up to 2026 without securing a supermajority.

"On the other hand it put limitations as to how much we could change things unilaterally as the FIA. And therefore any change had to be approved by a significant number of the PU manufacturers," Tombazis explained.

"So for the sort of changes we did [in May], we needed at least four of them to agree. And quite simply, four of them did not agree during the years when we discussed some adjustments."

Tombazis had hoped that the changes for the coming years could have been implemented sooner Photo by: Lars Baron / Getty Images

Challenges known since 2022, but races still entertaining

Part of the reason for that was that the reality of the automotive industry looked very different at the time, with manufacturers placing a much greater emphasis on electrification.

"Overall, it was always a challenging target to have a close to 50-50 power split between the two units," Tombazis said.

"But that was a very important position for the OEMs participating, and frankly having to decide whether they want to be in Formula 1 or not. Don't forget that if we didn't have them in, we would have just two power units in Formula 1, which I think would have been a bit of an issue. So that requirement to have a much stronger electrical part did create these difficulties."

Tombazis explained that the FIA had already become aware of these challenges in 2022, a year before Verstappen publicly voiced his concerns, but by then it was simply too late to fundamentally alter the regulations.

"As simulations came in back in 2022 or so, we knew there were these issues, but we were a bit too far down the line there to change things and some people had committed too much resource," he said. "So that left us slightly on the back foot at the start of the season, discussing that."

Tombazis concluded by stressing that, despite all of this, the races themselves have still provided good entertainment during the first half of the season.

Tombazis feels despite the problems with the F1 regulations, the racing has been exciting Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

"Now with that said, I think most races have been pretty exciting, I would say. There's been quite a lot of fighting," he said.

"I would even say that currently we still have, I don't know if I would go quite as far as to call it domination, but we do have a clear advantage for one manufacturer. And in the past when we've had that at the early start of the regulations, races have been very processional.

"Now I think, even despite the fact that Mercedes have been doing most of the winning, I think the races have nonetheless been quite exciting with quite a lot of changes and so on."

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Which of Antonelli’s rivals is his biggest threat for the championship this year? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s strong position in the lead of the championship standings at the summer break is remarkable enough already for a driver in his second season in Formula 1.

But what makes his position all the more impressive is that, arguably, no single driver has yet emerged as his clear rival. Antonelli has won six of the 11 rounds so far, more than the rest put together, and only his team mate George Russell has taken multiple wins.

Despite that, Russell is not Antonelli’s closest rival in the standings: Lewis Hamilton is leading a resurgent Ferrari. Plus, the final round before the summer break saw McLaren claim their first victory of the season. Three of the last five grands prix were won by teams other than Mercedes – could Antonelli biggest threat come from one of them?

Lewis Hamilton

50 points behind

The possibility of Hamilton fighting for the championship against the driver who took the Mercedes seat he vacated last year is a compelling narrative. But is it a likely outcome? Hamilton is Antonelli’s closest rival in the points but has missed opportunities due to penalties in recent races.

George Russell

59 points behind

Russell should be Antonelli’s closest rival for the championship but various factors have left him well behind including unreliability (not that Antonelli has been immune), some misfortune and his risky first-lap lunge at Spa. He’s also on course to incur a power unit change penalty before his team mate. Still, Russell should have the equipment and the experience to put Antonelli under pressure.

Charles Leclerc

81 points behind

Hamilton may be closer to Antonelli in the standings but Charles Leclerc has arguably looked more competitive. Providing he avoids a repeat of the dip he fell into around Spain and Monaco, he could emerge as Antonelli’s biggest threat.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Lando Norris

91 points behind

Like Mercedes, unreliability has dogged McLaren this year. They often haven’t been quick enough either, though Norris has now won both a grand prix and a sprint race. The MCL40’s Hungaroring upgrade clearly paid off, and may prove enough to bring the McLarens into regular contention. The reigning world champion is a long way behind, though.

Max Verstappen

110 points behind

If last year demonstrated anything, it is unwise to write off Max Verstappen if he is not mathematically out of contention. Having been 104 points off the lead with 249 remaining, he eventually lost by the narrowest margin in F1 history (relatively). But lying 110 points behind in a car which hasn’t won a grand prix yet may be too much even for him.

Oscar Piastri

127 points behind

Oscar Piastri has proved a close match on pace for his team mate as usual but he’s even further behind in the standings. He went into the final round of last season with a shot at the championship but that doesn’t look likely to happen this year.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Isack Hadjar

151 points behind

Isack Hadjar has impressed with the quality of his performances alongside Verstappen and may yet recover the points he dropped after losing his podium finish in Monaco. But his points deficit to Antonelli is surely too large and the Red Bull not competitive enough yet for him to be a realistic title contender.

I say

Hamilton may be closest in the points but Russell surely has the better combination of opportunity and equipment at the moment. If he can stop the rot in the second half of the season I would back him to put Antonelli under pressure for the title.

Sports.title: Domenicali resists Briatore’s call for sprint races at every round | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali will not move to add sprint races at every round next season, but still plans to hold more than the current six.

Alpine consultant Flavio Briatore recently argued for F1 to hold sprint races every week and, as is done in Moto GP.

Speaking in Liberty Media’s latest earnings update call for investors, Domenicali said limiting the number of sprint rounds gives them scarcity value.

“Sprint races is an opportunity that, first of all, started because we wanted to produce something that could create action on the track, creating leverage for the promoter and ourselves to create action on the tracks starting for the weekend,” he said. “We’re going to have more sprint races next year, yes. We’ll inform when we will announce the calendar, how many.

“The principle is very simple. This is also an opportunity to increment the revenue stream, for sure. This is an opportunity for us to have new deals, as we have already seen, and moving in this direction will be our future. We want to do in the right way because, of course, this will allow us also to make sure that the scarcity is a value.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Antonelli says he ‘let pressure destroy me’ in mid-season slump last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he succumbed to pressure when he suffered a slump in form during the middle of his debut season last year.

The Mercedes driver went through a seven-round spell when he finished in the points just once – albeit on the podium. His dip in form coincided with changes to Mercedes’ car which he struggled to get to grips with.

“I had a good start to the season, then I had a difficult period,” said Antonelli in a recent interview. “In the European season I really struggled and in that moment I let the pressure kind of destroy me as well during that period.

“I felt like I was letting down so many people who had believed in me. Of course especially Toto [Wolff, Mercedes team principal], because he was the main one who took the decision [to promote him].

“Obviously I didn’t feel good in that period. I wasn’t doing well. But then I had a big meeting with the team after the European season and it kind of allowed me to reset and just start again.

“Then I slowly found my way back. I had a good second half of the season and that gave me confidence, being able to overcome those difficult moments and gave me the confidence ahead of this year. It also made me learn a lot about myself, not only as a driver, but as a person as well.”

Antonelli said the experience taught him useful lessons about coping with adversity. “Obviously [during] that European season, I think probably most of the things I did, didn’t help me at all,” he said.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But also I learned about how my body responds to those moments, how my brain responds, what helps me to get back into the right focus, the right mindset, what helps me to stay 100% in terms of energy during the whole weekend. So how to manage myself with events, obviously the driving and everything. So I’ve learned a lot about myself and how as well to respond to difficult moments.”

Mercedes promoted Antonelli directly to their top team, in the seat formerly occupied by Lewis Hamilton, at the age of 18. Antonelli said making his F1 debut with a front-running team left him feeling depleted by the end of the 24-round championship.

“I was so drained at the end of the year,” he said. “Obviously the team did an incredible job in trying to protect me. But the learning curve – I think I’ve learned much more than if I would have done in a smaller team.

“The learning curve was incredible, it was like doing three years at once. It was overwhelming, physically, mentally, because I’ve made so many new experiences as well.

“Also, doing a full F1 season for the first time, you don’t really know where you’re going, what you’re about to face. Obviously the year prior to F1, I’ve been doing race shadowing and everything, but it’s not the same.

“When I was doing shadowing, I was watching, I wasn’t there on track doing the job. So I felt very overwhelmed at the end of the year. And it was good to have a bit of a break to just have a little bit of time to analyse and reflect on the year and understand what were the good things and why and why some things went not in the right way.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Having become the youngest driver to lead the world championship, Antonelli says he is trying to enjoy the position and the attention which comes with it, particularly in his home country.

“It’s like in any sport at the highest level, there’s always pressure and of course, being Italian, Italy has been missing an Italian driver for quite a long time and obviously also knowing myself because I’m Italian.

“We know how as Italians we can get very excited about things and how expectations can get over the moon. But obviously that comes with a bit of a extra pressure. But I’ve been enjoying, I have been enjoying. I think what I’ve been trying to do as well is to embrace the pressure and trying to actually shine under pressure.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Norris vs Piastri: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The super-close contest between the McLaren team mates last year would have made for a thrilling world championship fight even if Max Verstappen hadn’t got involved.

Now in their fourth season as team mates, with a completely different type of McLaren to get used to, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have been fairly well-matched on the whole. However in individual races their relative performance has varied, most notably in Hungary last weekend, where Norris was clearly much quicker.

Norris has been on a strong run lately, out-qualifying his team mate for the last five rounds in a row. Though it bears pointing out that Piastri missed first practice at the last round and was badly baulked by Lewis Hamilton when he began his final run.

It took Piastri until the third round of the season merely to start a grand prix, suffering a mortifying pre-race crash at home, then retiring before the start along with Norris in Shanghai. He rebounded magnificently at Suzuka and might have won had it not been for the timing of a Safety Car period.

McLaren have had further technical trouble since then: Norris had back-to-back failures while Piastri’s retirement in Hungary capped a frustrating race where a wayward backmarker had already cost him the lead. Piastri had a rough race in Canada as well, where both McLaren drivers paid the price for a tactical gamble which backfired.

It was therefore fitting that Norris delivered the team’s first win as F1 headed into the summer break. His 36-point lead over Piastri looks like a fair reflection of their relative performances given the various setbacks both drivers have suffered. The world champion holds the upper hand so far but Piastri is keeping him honest as always.

Sports.title: On This Day: Button becomes a grand prix winner with Honda in Hungary | Brief
Sports.content: The Formula 1 world championship began in 1950 and is considered the world’s leading form of single-seater motorsport. The 2025 F1 season is the 75th time the championship has been held. [caption id="attachment_530322" align="alignright" width="470"] The 2025 Formula 1 season started in Australia[/caption]A world drivers’ champion has been crowned every year since the series began. Since 1958 a world constructors’ championship title has also been awarded. The most successful F1 drivers in history are seven-times world champions Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. In 2021 the former became the first and so far only driver to date to win 100 grands prix. While Schumacher retired from F1 at the end of 2012, Hamilton continues to race. His rival world champions in the series are Max Verstappen and Fernando Alonso. There are 10 teams active in the championship, each of which field cars for two drivers. Each team is required to design and build the majority of its cars but may source some parts including engines, gearboxes and certain other components. Ferrari has won the F1 constructors’ championship more times than any other team, with 16 titles. It is also the only team which has competed in every championship since the first…

Sports.title: Hamilton vs Leclerc: 2026 F1 team mates’ head-to-head scores at summer break | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Does Lewis Hamilton have an eighth world championship in him? Has he not recovered from the blow of 2021 or did he simply never gel with the ‘ground effect’ cars of 2022-25?

Those hoping to see the seven-times world champion fight for another title will have drawn great encouragement from what they have seen so far in 2026. Last year, in his first season at Ferrari, he came off badly in comparison to Charles Leclerc , taking a 19-5 pasting in qualifying and making zero podium appearances to his team mate’s seven.

Hamilton has given full credit to team principal Frederic Vasseur for implementing the changes he needed to make a success of his transition to Ferrari, whether that has involved different brake material or swerving the simulator. On the face of it, it has paid off, and Ferrari now have two A-list drivers performing at their peak.

Leclerc is still shading Hamilton on average in qualifying, but the fight between the two has been much closer. Hamilton has delivered more consistently on race day, including that breakthrough victory in Spain.

Both drivers have misfired at times. Leclerc had a spate of errors including costly crashes in qualifying at the Circuit de Catalunya and during his home race.

Hamilton, meanwhile, has picked up a bad habit of incurring the stewards’ wrath, collecting a series of needless penalties in recent races. Though some may not have been his fault or were debatable calls, many others were straightforward, and he was fortunate to avoid a worse penalty for his yellow flag slip in Silverstone.

For all that, Hamilton is Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest rival in the championship at the summer break. “Has the time finally come for Hamilton to hang up his helmet?” we asked in May, in what already looks like one of the most poorly-timed polls ever featured on RaceFans.

Sports.title: Bobby Czyz Pitches 12-Round Shutout Against Bash Ali
Sports.content:
Ali brought an unusual story into the title fight. The Nigerian-born challenger, also known as Bashiru Lawrence Ali and “Mr. President,” talked openly about eventually running for president of Nigeria. He claimed a world championship would increase his stature and help finance those political ambitions.

Winning the belt proved considerably more difficult.

Controlling Ali from the opening bell with a steady jab, Czyz repeatedly followed it with hard right hands, uppercuts and combinations. Ali was naturally strong at cruiserweight and possessed an excellent chin, but his durability became his primary asset as the rounds accumulated.

There were opportunities for the champion to finish him. Ali’s face began showing the effects of the punishment, particularly around the eyes, while Czyz remained largely untouched. When Czyz opened up, Ali frequently responded by tying him up rather than exchanging.

Broadcast punch statistics illustrated the scale of the beating, crediting Czyz with landing 435 of 733 punches, an extraordinary 59 percent. Ali connected at approximately 28 percent.

The knockout that might have transformed an otherwise methodical defense into a spectacular one never came.

By the championship rounds, the outcome had long since been decided. Judges John Potera, Vinny Rainone and Phil Newman each scored the fight 120-108, giving Czyz a clean sweep on the cards. Steve Smoger served as referee.

The performance kept alive talk of a lucrative fight with Thomas Hearns, although that matchup never materialized. Czyz instead defended his WBA championship against Donny Lalonde in May 1992, winning another 12-round decision.

The Nigerian challenger left Atlantic City without the belt, though his reputation for toughness remained intact. He continued fighting for years afterward, while his political ambitions and attempts to stage a record-setting boxing event eventually became major stories in Nigeria.

The night was less about drama than complete control: 36 minutes, 12 rounds and every one of them belonging to Czyz.

Ali landed his share of big shots throughout the fight, but Czyz took them without giving ground and repeatedly came back with harder punches of his own. The 120-108 cards told the story of who won the exchanges.

Sports.title: Boots Ennis Prepares To Raid Josh Kelly For The IBF Title
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn mentioned matching them prior to Kelly’s July 25 defense against Caoimhin Agyarko. His comments came last month, rather than being a new development surrounding the fight.

“There’s a very good chance that Josh Kelly will fight Boots in November,” Hearn told iFL TV in July. “In America. Not Newcastle.”

The British challenger took care of his end by defeating Agyarko, leaving Matchroom with an in-house three-belt unification that makes plenty of sense for Ennis.

The attraction for Boots is obvious. He can pick up the IBF title in one fight and move within a single belt of becoming undisputed champion at 154 pounds.

This matchup also gives Matchroom a marketable opponent without requiring Ennis to wait for another promoter to cooperate. Hearn controls the pieces and has already floated bringing Kelly to America for the fight.

The bigger question is how competitive the contest would be.

While the British titleholder possesses sharp movement along with solid experience to make Boots work, Ennis brings superior speed, heavy power, and deep offensive variety. Kelly would likely need to produce the best performance of his career to keep Ennis from eventually taking control.

That doesn’t make the fight unappealing. Boots needs meaningful fights in the weight class, and collecting another world title is considerably more useful than taking a stay-busy defense while waiting for the division’s remaining belt.

If Hearn still intends to make the fight late this year, the path remains clear. Kelly gives Ennis his cleanest route to owning three of the four belts at 154 pounds.

Sports.title: Sebastian Hernandez Reyes Blasts Out Jose Lopez in Two
Sports.content:
There was some rust early Saturday, but once the 25-year-old began letting his hands go, Lopez had no way to contain his pressure.

Hernandez Reyes took over in the second round, pushing Lopez toward the ropes and unloading combinations from close range. Lopez had little room to escape and couldn’t produce enough offense to slow him down.

Lopez tried covering up as Hernandez Reyes continued pouring punches through and around his guard. The sustained attack left Lopez bloodied, and the referee eventually stepped between them to halt the scheduled 10-round super bantamweight contest.

It was a strong return for a fighter eager to move past the Nakatani result. Hernandez Reyes did not spend Saturday trying to box cautiously or simply collect rounds; he stayed aggressive and broke down an opponent who could not keep pace.

The stoppage gave Hernandez Reyes his 19th knockout in 22 professional fights. More importantly, he came through without jeopardizing a quick turnaround. Hernandez Reyes is scheduled to fight Kyonosuke Kameda (16-5-2) on September 23 in Osaka, Japan.

Kameda should provide considerably more resistance than Lopez offered. The trip to Osaka gives Hernandez Reyes a chance to build on Saturday’s quick finish and continue working his way toward another major fight.

Sports.title: Gradus Kraus Decimates Sean Hemphill in 63 Seconds
Sports.content:
The 25-year-old connected with a straight right before launching a barrage against his pinned opponent. Referee John Latham stepped in, stopping the scheduled 10-rounder at 1:03 of the opening round.

It proved a surprisingly easy night against an opponent who looked capable of making him work.

Hemphill (19-4, 11 KOs) had previously shown he could compete against respectable opposition. The New Orleans native defeated Mark Jeffers by majority decision in England and went the distance with former IBF super middleweight champion William Scull last year. None of that experience helped him Saturday.

Kraus overwhelmed him before the fight had time to develop, recording his fifth first-round stoppage while continuing a destructive start to his professional career. Eleven of his 12 opponents have failed to hear the final bell.

Now Kraus needs tougher competition. At 6-foot-2 with size, aggression and serious power at 175 pounds, Kraus has moved beyond opponents brought in primarily to give him rounds. Hemphill was supposed to test him and lasted barely a minute.

Kraus made it clear afterward that he wants a more difficult opponent next.

“There should be a better guy opposite me,” Kraus said.

After what happened in Leeds, his handlers should give him exactly that.

Sports.title: Foreman Destroyed Norton, Then Caracas Wouldn’t Let Him Leave
Sports.content:
Foreman had destroyed Joe Frazier in two rounds to become heavyweight champion and stopped José Roman in the first round of his initial defense. His record had reached 39-0 with 36 knockouts, making Norton approximately a 3-1 underdog.

Ali, working at ringside, gave the challenger a better chance than most. Having survived 24 rounds against him, Ali questioned the assumption that Foreman would simply run through a fighter who had caused him so much difficulty.

Trouble Before the Bell

The fight nearly encountered problems before either heavyweight reached the ring. Foreman’s camp wanted an American referee, while Venezuelan officials favored a local official. Jimmy Rondeau eventually received the assignment.

Around fight day, reports surfaced that Foreman had developed a knee problem described as either a sprain or pinched nerve, creating uncertainty about the championship fight proceeding. The issue ceased being an obstacle once the referee dispute was settled.

There was another unusual element hanging over the promotion. Don King was already working toward a Foreman-Ali fight, provided Foreman defeated Norton. Norton therefore had a chance to wreck plans for one of boxing’s biggest possible events, though he never came close.

The first round gave Norton some room to box, but the champion began trapping him more effectively as the fight progressed. The game plan depended upon movement and avoiding prolonged exchanges.

Early in the second round, that strategy completely collapsed. Foreman trapped Norton near the ropes and hammered him with a series of clubbing power shots. The ropes kept Norton upright during part of the assault before he went down repeatedly.

Norton’s corner signaled that it had seen enough, prompting Rondeau to stop the fight at 2:00 of the second round. A fighter who had gone 24 competitive rounds with Ali had lasted less than five minutes with Foreman.

Purses and the Caracas Caper

Financial figures showed Foreman reportedly earning approximately $700,000, while Norton received around $200,000. The story did not end when the purses were distributed.

The promotion had been brought to Venezuela partly through assurances involving tax exemptions. Venezuelan authorities subsequently demanded approximately 18 percent of the fighters’ earnings.

Both men were prevented from simply leaving the country while the dispute was unresolved. Norton settled his situation and departed around March 29, but Foreman remained for several additional days as negotiations continued with American diplomatic officials becoming involved in what became known as the “Caracas Caper.”

The bout was staged at Caracas’ Poliedro arena. Historical accounts differ on the attendance, while the financial dispute surrounding the promotion soon attracted nearly as much attention as the gate itself.

Inside the ring, there was little ambiguity. Foreman had destroyed Frazier, Roman, and Norton in consecutive heavyweight title fights, needing only six combined rounds. Norton’s success against Ali suddenly provided an irresistible comparison: Ali had needed 24 rounds against Norton and lost once; Foreman had required less than two.

Seven months later, Ali would travel to Zaire and attempt to solve the heavyweight champion Norton could not survive.

Sports.title: Dina Thorslund Dominates Cherneka Johnson, Claims Undisputed Crown
Sports.content:
Constant pressure, relentless volume and clean combinations set the tempo early. The defending champion found no answers to slow the pace or mount a meaningful counterattack.

By the second half, Johnson needed something significant to change the direction of the fight. She never found it. Thorslund remained in command through the closing bell, completing a remarkably one-sided championship performance.

Johnson never established enough distance to disrupt Thorslund’s pressure, allowing the Dane to dictate exchanges throughout the fight.

The victory unified the WBA, WBC, IBF and WBO titles under Thorslund.

Her return to the top follows a difficult period outside the ring. Thorslund previously held the WBC and WBO bantamweight titles before vacating them in June 2025 after announcing her pregnancy. She later suffered a miscarriage.

A return in January 2026 brought Thorslund the WBC interim featherweight title before she moved back down to 118 pounds to challenge Johnson.

Johnson had collected the belts that became available during Thorslund’s absence and came into Saturday night as the undisputed champion. That reign ended decisively.

Emotional celebrations followed the verdict, with Thorslund sharing the moment inside the ring with her son after completing her return to the top of the bantamweight division.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Campaigns For Jake Paul Fight
Sports.content:
Berlanga posted the poster on his X account with little explanation, creating the impression of a fight promotion without a date or venue. There has been no corresponding announcement from Jake Paul, Most Valuable Promotions or Netflix.

That makes the graphic look less like fight news and more like Berlanga advertising himself for one of boxing’s biggest paydays.

The idea isn’t new. Berlanga has previously pursued Paul and called for a contract when Paul was searching for opponents in late 2025. Paul ultimately went in another direction, fighting Anthony Joshua in December.

Berlanga remains one of the names associated with Paul’s next appearance, although a Tommy Fury rematch has received greater attention. Chris Eubank Jr. and Ryan Garcia have been mentioned as other possibilities.

Financially, it isn’t difficult to understand Berlanga’s interest. A Paul fight would offer considerably more exposure and potentially more money than most of the fights available to him in the super middleweight division.

Berlanga returned on July 26 with a stoppage of Steven Butler at Madison Square Garden. Rather than waiting for Paul’s side to come calling, he now seems intent on selling the matchup himself.

The poster may be fiction. The interest behind it probably isn’t.

Sports.title: Tamm Thibeault Dominates Robinson, Captures Three Middleweight Belts
Sports.content:
Thibeault used her height, reach, and quicker hands to control the action from distance. She consistently landed the cleaner punches while forcing the Australian champion to work through incoming fire to get close enough to attack.

Robinson pressed continuously, turning portions of the bout into a physical battle. Both women finished bloodied, with the new champion suffering a heavy nosebleed after a clash of heads.

Blood streaming down her face created a dramatic scene in the later rounds, but it did little to change the fight. Robinson absorbed punishment while continuing to press, yet she never found a sustained answer for Thibeault’s southpaw boxing.

The shutout win moves Thibeault to 5-0 with three knockouts. Her amateur career included a world championship, Pan American titles, Commonwealth gold, plus two Olympic appearances.

Emotion ran high afterward as Thibeault held her newly won belts while still covered in blood, sharing a respectful moment with Robinson, who dropped to 12-4.

Thibeault now controls one half of the middleweight championship picture. Kaye Scott owns the WBA and WBC belts and faces Claressa Shields on August 15 in Atlanta.

If Shields wins, an undisputed championship fight with Thibeault becomes an obvious possibility. The bigger question is timing. Five professional fights is very little preparation for someone with Shields’ championship experience, leaving MVP to decide how quickly it wants to make that jump.

Ghana News.title: Armwrestling: Golden Arms set for World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's national armwrestling team, the Golden Arms, will represent the country at the World Armwrestling Championship scheduled for October 26 to November 7, 2026, in New Delhi, India, as the Ghana Armwrestling Federation (GAF) steps up preparations for another major international assignment.

The championship, organised under the auspices of the World Armwrestling Federation (WAF), is expected to attract about 1,500 of the world's leading armwrestlers, providing the Golden Arms with an opportunity to compete against some of the strongest and most technically accomplished pullers from across the globe.

The Golden Arms will enter the competition with a team of nine pullers with growing confidence following Ghana's impressive showing at the 15th Africa Armwrestling Championship in Accra, where the country demonstrated its strength and depth in the sport.

The team will feature some of Ghana's most accomplished pullers, including world champion Grace Minta, world championship medallists Mabel Yeboah and Blessed Abeka Nunoo, and African champion Daniel Acquah. They bring a combination of world-class experience, continental success and emerging talent as Ghana seeks to make another strong statement on the international stage.

Mabel Yeboah

As part of preparations for the New Delhi championship, the Golden Arms will commence a national camping programme to bring together selected athletes for intensive preparation. The camp will focus on physical conditioning, strength development, technical and tactical work, recovery, discipline and mental preparation ahead of the championship.

The camping programme will also provide the technical team, led by coaches Husseini Akueteh Addy and Nii Otu Larkyne, with an opportunity to assess the athletes and fine-tune the final squad for the various weight categories. Particular attention will be given to international competition standards as the Ghanaian team seeks to translate its continental dominance into strong performances against the world's best.

President of the Ghana Armwrestling Federation, Charles Osei Asibey, has reiterated the federation's commitment to providing Ghanaian athletes with regular opportunities to compete at the highest level. The World Championship forms part of the federation's broader strategy of developing elite athletes capable of winning medals at continental and global competitions.

The New Delhi championship will therefore serve as both a medal opportunity and an important test of Ghana's progress in armwrestling. Beyond the quest for podium finishes, participation will expose the Golden Arms to different techniques, styles and levels of competition, while providing valuable experience for the athletes and technical team.

The Ghana Armwrestling Federation is calling on corporate organisations and state institutions for travel support, with preparations now gathering momentum and camping set to commence ahead of the October championship in New Delhi.

The team's objective at the 2026 World Armwrestling Championship will be to compete strongly, challenge for medals and further establish Ghana as a force in world armwrestling.

Ghana News.title: NPP government supported comedians more than NDC – Lekzy DeComic
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian comedian Lekzy DeComic says the previous NPP government paid more attention to comedians than the current administration.

He made the statement during the ninth edition of Joy FM’s Showbiz Roundtable, held on Saturday, 8 August 2026.

“When the NPP was in power, I drew the attention of one of their executives to the fact that anytime they did stuff for the entertainment industry, they trivialised comedy. The moment I mentioned it, he drew the attention of the GTA boss Akwasi Agyemang to it. Since then, anytime we had a comedy show, they would call you and ask how the GTA could support our show, whether in kind or whichever form. They would try and come through for you,” he said.

Lekzy noted that it was through the previous government that some comedians had the opportunity to travel to the USA to be part of the Ghana Week celebration in Washington, DC.

“But with this current government, it appears we don’t even exist in their books. Last year, I invited two South African comedians to come to Ghana to help me do my show and I went to see their acting Ambassador and he asked how he could help us. He was ready to do everything for us to have a successful show,” he said.

According to the award-winning comedian, he also got a call from somebody from Blackstar Experience who told him they had a collaboration with the South African government and had seen that he had an upcoming event with some of the comedians from that country, so they needed him to send some footage so they could add it to their proposal.

“…and I asked them how I would benefit from it because I was initiating it myself. That was the last time I heard from him. And I even called somebody to reach out to Mr Rex Omar. It was a three-way call. He said we would hear from him and that was it. If it was the previous government that call would have changed something for me. And till date, I have not heard from them. Nothing. Zero effort. And we are still here, making time. So when Kojo Preko Dankwah said he would score them zero percent for work done so far, I support him hundred percent,” he said.

Lekzy further indicated that his biggest disappointment with the current government stems from the fact that it has the highest number of creatives appointed to various leadership positions.

Themed “Assessing 20 Months of Government’s Impact on Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts”, the ninth Showbiz Roundtable examined the government’s commitments to the sector, assessed the level of implementation, measured the impact of policies and explored the road ahead for Ghana’s creative economy.

The discussion featured industry figures including Chief Operating Officer of Maestro Africa Group, Francis Doku; Lead Consultant at Jesse Agyepong and Associates, Jesse Agyepong; pop culture journalist Olele Salvador; and Joy FM broadcaster Ken Addy.

Also in attendance were comedians Lekzy DeComic, Kojo Pjay, Percy Obrempong, James Brown and Jacinta. Others were broadcasters Austine Woode and Kojo Preko Dankwah, while tourism professional Emmanuel Frimpong was also present.

The discussion was moderated by broadcaster and arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie. It was produced by Philip Nai, with support from Anita Teye and Idah Lamaire.

Ghana News.title: GANRAP will build reserves to cushion Ghana against future shocks — Sammy Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says the government is using the Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP) to build a strong financial buffer capable of protecting Ghana against future economic shocks and external disruptions.

He said the policy would enable the country to accumulate sufficient reserves through its gold resources instead of relying heavily on borrowing to shore up its foreign exchange position.

GANRAP targets an increase in Ghana’s gross international reserves to the equivalent of 15 months of import cover by the end of 2028.

The policy seeks to raise reserve cover from 5.7 months currently to 8.6 months by the end of 2026 and 11.8 months by 2027 before reaching the 15-month target in 2028.

The programme is expected to add an average of US$9.5 billion to Ghana’s gross international reserves annually through the purchase of about 3.02 tonnes of gold per week.

GoldBod will acquire gold from the small-scale mining sector, while government will also exercise its pre-emptive right to purchase 20 per cent of gold produced by large-scale mining companies.

Speaking on Twitter Spaces on Sunday, August 9, Mr Gyamfi said, “Government is using GANRAP to build enough reserves to deal with future exogenous factors and external shocks.”

He further argued that the benefits of the policy would extend beyond government finances, describing the reserve accumulation as something that could be regarded as a public good.

“GANRAP can also be factored as a public good,” he added.

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, in presenting the policy to Parliament, said GANRAP represented a shift from the previous approach of using expensive swaps and Eurobond borrowing to build reserves.

He described the initiative as an effort to build an “economic war-chest” to help Ghana withstand global economic shocks, safeguard macroeconomic stability and sustain the economic gains achieved.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Jazz Orchestra inauguration set for Sept. 5
Ghana News.content:
Its first public appearance last April was described as a "soft opening", but the time has come for the Ghana Jazz Orchestra to make a full entrance. This will happen on September 5, 2026, at the +233 Jazz Bar & Grill in Accra.

Directed by Bernard Ayisa and conducted by Victor Dey Jr., the orchestra comprises five saxophonists, four trumpeters, four trombonists, a clarinettist and a vocalist. It also includes a pianist, bassist, drummer and percussionist.

"Everyone is really working hard towards the inaugural concert," says the orchestra's director.

"We don't have an outfit like that in this country at the moment. So it's great education for the young players, some of whom have never been in a situation where there are four trumpets, for instance, and they have to play and blend as a unit."

The Ghana Jazz Orchestra was formed following the visit of renowned American trumpeter Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra (JLCO) to Ghana in October 2025.

Bernard Ayisa is director of the orchestra

The Ghana Jazz Foundation, working closely with the Accra Jazz Academy, felt there were players with enough flair to establish something like the JLCO in Ghana. Auditions were held, and the result will be unveiled on September 5.

Also scheduled to perform on the night is Lisa Simone, an American singer, composer, actress and Grammy-nominated recording artiste. She is the daughter of renowned musician and civil rights activist Nina Simone.

The GHJazz Collective will also perform at the concert, which starts at 8:00 p.m.

“We are all looking forward to a night of admirable connection between the musicians and a happy audience. Reception was good at the ‘soft opening’ in April and we trust we would present another impressive show on September 5,” the orchestra’s director remarked.

Ghana News.title: African governments must back African multinationals – Dr Ishmael Yamson
Ghana News.content:
The Board Chairman of MTN Ghana, Dr Ishmael Yamson, has urged African governments to provide stronger support for home-grown multinational companies, arguing that empowering African businesses is critical to accelerating regional integration and strengthening the continent's global competitiveness.

Speaking on The Y'ello Chair – Episode 8, MTN's vodcast platform that connects African leaders and changemakers to discuss the continent's future, Dr Yamson said Africa must create a more enabling environment for indigenous multinational companies to expand and thrive across the continent.

According to him, one of the biggest challenges facing African businesses is the lack of harmonised regulations across countries, forcing companies operating in multiple markets to navigate different legal and regulatory systems.

"Today, literally every country you go to, the regulatory environment is different. We are operating in 19 countries, and we are dealing with 19 different regulatory environments. That is tough," he said.

Dr Yamson called for greater harmonisation of laws and regulations, particularly among Africa's largest economies, to make it easier for businesses to operate across borders and contribute to the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

"It's important that we set the idea of harmonising our laws and regulations across the continent, especially between the big economies, to make sure that businesses can flow from one country to another without great difficulty," he noted.

He also observed that African governments often appear more comfortable engaging with foreign multinational companies than African-owned businesses, a mindset he believes must change.

"Companies like MTN and other African multinationals need the support of African governments. Unfortunately, African governments find it easier to deal with non-African multinationals than dealing with African multinationals," he said.

Explaining why this situation persists, Dr Yamson suggested that perceptions and attitudes have contributed to the challenge.

"It's very simple. Why should I be dictated to by my other Black brother? And that's a mindset that should change," he remarked.

He stressed that stronger African companies are essential if the continent is to increase its influence in the global economy, noting that Africa currently contributes only a small share of global innovation while continuing to import technologies and innovations developed elsewhere.

"We need to understand that together we'll be bigger. If we continue to operate as small countries and build only small companies, we're not going to make any meaningful impact anywhere," he said.

Dr Yamson further called for African governments and the private sector to establish regular platforms for dialogue to address common challenges and develop policies that promote business growth and continental development.

"I think that has been the missing link. We need to bring the African private sector and African governments together and have a forum where we can have the difficult conversations, but at the end of the day, we see what will be beneficial to both parties," he said.

He maintained that stronger partnerships between governments and African multinationals would not only support business growth but also advance economic integration, job creation and sustainable development across the continent.

Ghana News.title: WAFCON 2026: Black Queens miss out on automatic 2027 World Cup qualification
Ghana News.content:
Ghana missed out on automatic qualification to the 2027 Women's World Cup following their defeat to Malawi in the quarterfinals of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON).

A late Rose Kadzere goal broke the hearts of the Black Queens as they lost 2-1 at the Al Madina Stadium in Rabat on Sunday, August 9.

Kim Lars Bjorkegren made no changes to the starting lineup that drew in the final group game against Mali, with Evelyn Badu and Comfort Yeboah keeping their places in the team.

Ghana came into the fixture as runners-up in Group D after finishing behind Cameroon, while Malawi finished ahead of Nigeria and Zambia in Group C.

Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah opened the scoring for Ghana after only six minutes, scoring from a rebound to give the Black Queens the lead.

Evelyn Badu should have made it two for the Black Queens, but her header after Alice Kusi's cross went just wide of the post.

However, the lead lasted just minutes as Temwa Chawinga scored from a wicked deflection off Grace Asantewaa to level proceedings.

Doris Boaduwaa came close to restoring Ghana's lead, but her shot from just outside the box was saved by the Malawian goalkeeper.

Cynthia Konlan made a good save to keep out a Malawi header just before the break.

The two teams went into recess with the scoreline 1-1.

After the recess, Boaduwaa thought she had restored the lead for Ghana, but her goal was chopped off for an offside in the buildup.

Jennifer Cudjoe headed from a Ghanaian corner, but it also wasn't enough to threaten.

Malawi scored in the 79th minute to take the lead for the first time in the game after a great spell of possession.

Cynthia kept Ghana in the game with a good save to deny Temwa Chawinga.

Despite their late fight, Ghana were unable to draw level as they missed out on a place in the semifinals as well as automatic qualification to the 2027 Women's World Cup.

Malawi will face Algeria in the semifinals of the competition on Wednesday, August 12, at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat.

The Black Queens will, however, face Cote d'Ivoire in a playoff in Casablanca to keep their World Cup qualification hopes alive.

Ghana News.title: No one can claim GoldBod has made a loss, not even IMF – Sammy Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has strongly defended the financial performance of the institution, insisting that there is no basis for claims that it has made a loss.

He said GoldBod’s financial position could be verified through its audited financial statements and expressed confidence that the institution’s performance would withstand scrutiny from both local and international institutions.

Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was being managed with prudence and that its operations had remained financially sound since it assumed its expanded mandate in Ghana’s gold sector.

Speaking on Twitter Spaces on Sunday, August 9, Mr Gyamfi said, “Nobody can ever say that GoldBod has made a loss, including the IMF.”

He added, “Those who wish us doom will be put to shame,” insisting that the institution’s financial records would ultimately settle claims about its performance.

Mr Gyamfi had earlier stated that GoldBod had never made a loss and that its audited financial statements were available on its website.

He also maintained that the institution was being managed with “modesty and prudence” as it takes on greater responsibility for Ghana’s gold trade.

Chief Executive Officer of GoldBod, Sammy Gyamfi

The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, says the institution is being managed with caution, discipline and prudent financial management to ensure its long-term sustainability.

He said GoldBod’s approach to its operations is guided by the need to protect public resources while maximising the economic benefits Ghana derives from its gold resources.

Mr Gyamfi said the institution had adopted a measured approach to its spending and operations, insisting that its financial management was not driven by excessive expenditure or unnecessary commitments.

He said the approach was also consistent with GoldBod’s broader objective of building a financially sustainable institution capable of playing a central role in Ghana’s gold sector and supporting the country’s foreign exchange reserves.

Speaking on Twitter Spaces on Sunday, August 9, Mr Gyamfi said, “We are managing GoldBod with modesty and prudence.”

He stressed that the institution’s financial position should be assessed based on its records and audited financial statements rather than speculation.

“GoldBod has never made a loss and our audited financial statement is on our site, and GoldBod is very financially sound,” he added.

Mr Gyamfi’s comments come amid discussions about GoldBod’s financial performance and its expanded mandate to oversee the buying and selling of gold in Ghana.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
