World.title: Taking personal responsibility for your desired rest (2), By Ayo Akerele
World.content:
God provides the raw materials, but man must build the structure. God gives the seed, but man must till the ground, sow the seed, protect the field from pests, and harvest the crop. Passivity is an insult to the grace of God, because true grace does not make a man lazy; it empowers him to labour more abundantly (1 Corinthians 15:10).

Examples of Believers taking Responsibility in their Professional Fields

To understand how supernatural rest applies to our contemporary lives, we must look at how the principle of responsibility manifests within specific professional fields. The workplace is not separate from our spiritual walk; it is the ultimate arena where our spiritual authority is tested and demonstrated.

Here are six profiles of believers across various sectors who took strategic, faith-driven responsibility and triggered their professional and personal rest.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Healthcare: Luke, the Beloved Physician (Structural Excellence)

Luke was a highly educated medical practitioner in the ancient Greco-Roman world. When he became a believer, he did not abandon his analytical mind; instead, he sanctified it for the service of the Kingdom. Luke took the responsibility of conducting meticulous, historical investigations to document the life of Jesus and the movements of the early church.

In a professional landscape often driven by commercial gain and pagan superstition, Luke brought a standard of clinical accuracy and spiritual depth. He travelled extensively with Paul, providing medical support during demanding missionary journeys. By taking responsibility for documenting the gospel narrative with medical precision (as seen in his descriptions of hematidrosis, Jesus sweating blood, and various healings), Luke brought a sense of intellectual and theological rest to the early church. His work provided an unshakeable defense of the faith, ensuring that believers could rest secure in the historical certainty of the things they had been taught.

Law and Governance: Daniel in Babylon (Ethical Integrity)

Daniel operated at the absolute pinnacle of civil service and legal administration across multiple world empires (Babylonian and Medo-Persian). The professional environment of Babylon was notorious for corrupt conspiracies, bureaucratic backstabbing, and political occultism. Daniel could have easily compromised to survive. Instead, he took absolute responsibility for his spiritual discipline and professional competence.

He refused to defile himself with the king’s rich food, committed to a lifestyle of prayer three times a day, and maintained an unblemished standard of professional excellence. The scriptures record that his detractors searched for any flaw or corruption in his administration but found none, because he was faithful and errortless (Daniel 6:4). When he was thrown into the lions’ den for his uncompromising stance, God shut the mouths of the lions. Daniel’s refusal to bend triggered a massive systemic shift: the king issued a decree commanding the entire empire to fear the God of Daniel. Daniel entered into a profound era of administrative rest, prospering through the reigns of Darius and Cyrus.

Education and Social Reform: Ezra the Scribe (Sacrificial Investment)

Ezra was a professional academic, lawyer, and educator living in exile. When the opportunity arose to return to Jerusalem, he recognised that a nation cannot be rebuilt without an educational and moral foundation. Ezra took the responsibility to study, practice, and teach the laws of God to a generation that had lost its cultural identity (Ezra 7:10).

The educational system of his day was fragmented, and the people were slipping into spiritual illiteracy. Ezra did not wait for the government to fund religious schools; he organised massive public literacy campaigns, reconstructed the sacred texts, and stood on wooden platforms for hours explaining the scriptures to the populace. His commitment to educational reform broke the back of generational ignorance. By restoring intellectual clarity and moral order, Ezra brought an institutional rest to Israel, stabilising the society and preserving their heritage for generations to come.

Corporate Leadership and Economics: Joseph in Egypt (Prophetic Insight)

Joseph’s corporate promotion from a prison cell to the position of Chief Operating Officer of Egypt is an extraordinary study in economic responsibility. When presented with Pharaoh’s dream concerning an impending global depression, Joseph did not merely provide an abstract spiritual interpretation. He immediately presented a comprehensive fiscal and agricultural strategy.

He took responsibility for the survival of the entire civilised world by designing a national grain storage network, implementing a 20 per cent tax model during the years of abundance, and managing the distribution supply chain during the famine. Joseph worked tirelessly during the seven years of plenty to ensure the infrastructure was sound. Because he took strategic responsibility, Egypt became the economic capital of the world during the crisis. Joseph didn’t just survive the famine; he controlled the wealth of nations, bringing an unprecedented season of financial security and rest to his employer (Pharaoh) and his biological family.

Technology, Engineering, and Architecture: Nehemiah (Uncompromising Standards)

Nehemiah was a high-ranking corporate executive (cupbearer to the king) who transitioned into the role of a structural engineer and project manager. When he heard that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and the gates burnt with fire, he understood that the city’s lack of physical security meant its inhabitants lived in constant vulnerability and unrest. He took personal responsibility for the civil engineering project.

Nehemiah secured the political permits, raised the capital, organised the labour force into specialised teams, and managed an intense 52-day construction timeline. When external adversaries threatened military intervention, Nehemiah did not tell the workers to drop their tools and start a round-the-clock prayer meeting. Instead, he implemented a dual-strategy framework: every builder worked with a trowel in one hand and a sword in the other. He blended high-level security protocols with architectural efficiency. By executing this project with precise tactical responsibility, the wall was completed, the enemies were demoralised, and the citizens of Jerusalem finally experienced safety and civic rest.

Arts, Media, and Entertainment: David the Psalmist (Purified Conviction)

David was a brilliant musical artist, poet, and cultural influencer long before he ascended the throne of Israel. In his youth, the creative arts were often weaponised for pagan worship or shallow entertainment. David took responsibility for his artistic gift by anchoring it in deep spiritual intimacy. He spent years in the wilderness perfecting his skill on the harp and composing songs that captured the character of God.

When King Saul was tormented by a distressing spirit, David was summoned to court because of his reputation for musical excellence and spiritual authority. David did not treat his art as an empty performance; he understood it as a spiritual weapon. As he played, the demonic atmosphere dissipated, Saul was refreshed, and peace filled the palace. By taking responsibility for his creative output, David brought psychological and spiritual rest to a tormented leader, establishing a standard for using music as a vehicle for divine restoration.

Expanding the Teaching on Supernatural Rest

To fully grasp the depth of this doctrine, we must explore the dual dynamics of rest: the tragic consequences of passivity and the transformative power of proactive alignment.

The Illusion of Passivity: The Danger of Misunderstanding Grace

Many well-meaning believers fall into a spiritual trap that can be termed entitlement theology. This is the erroneous belief that because Jesus paid for our peace, health, and prosperity, the believer has no further role to play in their manifestation. This misunderstanding of grace breeds passivity, turning vibrant children of God into professional beggars who wait for sovereign interventions to fix situations that require practical action.

When you look at the architecture of the tabernacle of Moses, the operating model of the priesthood, and the parables of Jesus, you discover that the kingdom of God does not reward laziness. As found in Matthew 25, the servant who hid his talent in the earth, claiming he was waiting for the master’s return, was not comforted; he was cast into outer darkness as a “wicked and slothful servant.”

God provides the raw materials, but man must build the structure. God gives the seed, but man must till the ground, sow the seed, protect the field from pests, and harvest the crop. Passivity is an insult to the grace of God, because true grace does not make a man lazy; it empowers him to labour more abundantly (1 Corinthians 15:10).

Ayo Akerele is the senior pastor of Rhema Assembly and the founder of the Voice of the Watchmen Ministries in Ontario, Canada. He can be reached through [email protected]. World.title: ‘P-Square destroyed Africa’s biggest music brand’ – Daddy Showkey claims
World.content:
Veteran Nigerian galala singer John “Daddy Showkey” Asiemo has expressed disappointment over the long-running feud between P-Square singers Peter and Paul Okoye and their elder brother and former manager, Jude Okoye.

Daddy Showkey made the remarks during a viral interview with Goldmyne TV, where he said the brothers’ feud had destroyed what he described as “Africa’s biggest music group.”

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the family had remained in the news for days following a fresh round of accusations between the brothers.

Peter, known as Mr P, sparked the latest controversy after releasing a series of videos detailing his version of P-Square’s history, financial dealings, and the circumstances surrounding the group’s repeated break-ups.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The 56-year-old said, “I will tell them this, they destroyed the biggest brand that Africa has ever produced. They destroyed the biggest brand that Africa produced. You see, P-Square is not for them alone. As an entertainer, you are not for yourself anymore. Today I’m celebrating 56 years.

“I would have locked myself in my room to celebrate it. I’m celebrating because it is the people who made me Daddy Showkey. You understand? So if the people have made you, you are not considering the people. You are thinking about what you people are making or what.”

Future

Furthermore, the “Fire Fire” crooner urged the brothers to stop dragging each other and consider their future.

He also urged them to find a way to resolve their differences for the sake of their children.

“Dragging yourselves like this, the future will tell. No matter what, you guys are brothers. No matter what, you should look for a place to resolve this thing because you have children. Tomorrow you will carry this beef to your children,” Daddy Showkey said.

Example

Additionally, the singer urged Peter, Paul and Jude to use him as an example, adding that he had gone through the same experience.

“I’ve gone through almost the same thing they are going through. And I just decided that I’m not quarrelling with anybody because I don’t quarrel with people. You understand? So they should look for a way to address that issue and settle it as brothers.

“Because if the time comes, they will say, one time we were. God will not let it be like that for them. God will not let it. So they should try to resolve it.”

Peter and Paul formed P-Square and went on to become one of Africa’s most successful music duos before their first split in 2017. Although the brothers reconciled in 2021, they parted ways again in 2024 after fresh disagreements over the group’s finances and management.

The dispute later prompted an investigation by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and a court case involving Jude, who has denied any wrongdoing.

Jude has since responded publicly to Peter’s allegations, rejecting claims of financial misconduct and accusing his younger brother of distorting the facts surrounding P-Square’s finances and their family disagreements.

The family feud escalated on Saturday after their eldest brother, Henry, accused Jude of fuelling the prolonged dispute.

World.title: When pulpit confronts power, By Wole Olaoye
World.content:
The overwhelming majority of social media commentators are in support of Cardinal Onaiyekan, which shows that he was, in fact, doing his country a good turn by speaking truth to power. There is a rich history of the interactions — sometimes tepid, other times spirited — between the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria and various Nigerian leaders over the years. Patriots who want the best for their country must always support their leaders with candid advice.

John Cardinal Onaiyekan has been known as a temperate, sagacious, and even-handed man for all his 82 years on earth. Anyone now trying to cast him in the mould of a rabble-rouser does so in vain.

President Tinubu, in his own case, has always been a straight-shooting, wily exponent of ‘political wiseness.’ The convivial smokescreen accompanying his famed braggadocio is but a booby trap to ensnare anyone presumptuous enough to underestimate him.

Sharing Ideas

When the pulpit confronts the palace, perspicacious observers know that it is a solemn moment for truth-telling and cross-fertilisation of ideas, rather than an opportunity to create a tempest in a teapot.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

What was the recent hoopla all about? A delegation from the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) met privately with President Bola Tinubu at the Presidential Villa. The clerics presented a document detailing widespread economic hardship, security challenges, and social distress, which they urged the president to address.

Shortly after, Cardinal Onaiyekan discussed details of the meeting on Arise TV, stating that President Tinubu insisted that the economy was improving and appeared displeased with the bishops’ stance. Onaiyekan suggested that the aides around the president might not be giving him an accurate picture of what ordinary Nigerians are going through in their daily struggles. Brutally frank, but not disrespectful.

The clips of President Tinubu’s response to the bishops showed that he manned his corner gamely. He drew the attention of his visitors to the macroeconomic gains achieved by his administration and downplayed the microeconomic challenges. Being Tinubu the politician, he couldn’t help reminding the clerics that politics and morality are worlds apart.

I thought that engagement was one of the more salutary interactions between the pulpit and power in the current democratic dispensation. It was as robust as you could have it in any other democratic country in the world.

We ought to be proud of the fact that our Catholic bishops could go into the palace and tell the king that he wasn’t exactly regally robed. And the king, in equal measure, told his side of the story and explained why a pulpit wasn’t a required furniture item in the palace where the buck stops.

Compare Tinubu’s response to Donald Trump’s diatribe against Pope Leo XIV when the Catholic pontiff spoke against endless wars. I don’t know why we insist on beating ourselves up over matters that, all things considered, show that we have something to teach the rest of the world.

Attack Dogs

Unfortunately, instead of playing up the positive side of the visit, some presidential aides went berserk with puerile attacks against the bishops. One aide, Temitope Ajayi, said Onaiyekan’s interview at Arise News was an “abuse of clerical privilege.” (Pray, what does that mean?)

The comments attributed to Dr Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser on Policy, were, however, even more odious. He claimed that Cardinal Onaiyekan spoke strictly from a Catholic perspective, rather than on behalf of the entire Nigerian Christian community and that the cleric was “more political than spiritual.” He accused sections of the Catholic leadership of partisan alignment with opposition figures, especially Peter Obi of the NDC.

Bwala was proof, if any was needed, that Onaiyekan was right in saying that the president’s aides might not be giving him an accurate picture of what ordinary Nigerians are going through in their daily struggles.

Bwala’s characterisation of the Cardinal drew pushback from political figures, civil rights bodies, and interfaith leaders. Reverend Joseph John Hayab cautioned against attempting to divide the Christian community along denominational lines.

The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) criticised the presidential aides, maintaining that high-ranking clerics like Cardinal Onaiyekan have a civic and moral responsibility to highlight grassroots realities to public officials.

The Anglican Archbishop of Enugu North, Most Reverend Sosthenes Eze, said Onaiyekan was speaking on behalf of all Christians, indeed all Nigerians. “The Catholic Church has spoken the mind of all Nigerians,” he said. He described Bwala as the type of aide who misleads his principal in order to appear loyal.

Unfortunately, the attack dog model deployed by presidential aides is counterproductive on the eve of a presidential election. There are about 38 million Catholics in Nigeria. You don’t alienate that kind of constituency so thoughtlessly. The damage control done by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, was, however, wise and timely.

The overwhelming majority of social media commentators are in support of Cardinal Onaiyekan, which shows that he was, in fact, doing his country a good turn by speaking truth to power. There is a rich history of the interactions — sometimes tepid, other times spirited — between the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria and various Nigerian leaders over the years. Patriots who want the best for their country must always support their leaders with candid advice.

Sophocles’ Antigone

Ancient history taught us that lesson in Sophocles’ Antigone (441 BCE), a classic Greek tragedy that chronicles a fierce battle of wills between a young woman, Antigone, and her uncle, King Creon, over the burial of her brother.

Both of Antigone’s brothers are killed in a brutal civil war. The first brother, Eteocles, fought for the city and is granted a hero’s burial. The other, Polynices, fought against the city, and King Creon decreed that Polynices’ body must be left in the open fields to rot and be scavenged by birds. Anyone who attempts to bury or mourn him will be executed by public stoning. Creon views his decree as an essential demonstration of state power, political order, and legal absolute authority.

But his cousin, Antigone, refuses to obey, believing that the laws of the state cannot overrule the unwritten, eternal laws of justice, divine order, and human dignity. So, under cover of darkness, she sneaks outside the city walls and gives her late brother a proper burial.

When the guards capture her and bring her before Creon, Antigone defiantly delivers one of the most famous stands against political tyranny in Western literature.

“I did not think your edicts had such force that they, given by a mere mortal, could override the unwritten and unfailing laws of heaven. These are not of today or yesterday but live forever…”

An enraged King Creon sentences her to be sealed alive in a subterranean stone tomb. Antigone was stubborn to the end, choosing death over moral compromise. However, her fearless speech sets off a tragic domino effect. The blind prophet, Tiresias, warns Creon that the gods are furious at his refusal to honour natural law.

Eventually, an agitated Creon relents and orders that the tomb be opened. Sadly, Antigone has hanged herself. Her fiancé, Creon’s son Haemon, kills himself in grief, followed immediately by his mother, Queen Eurydice.

In one fell swoop, Creon lost the three people he loved most — his cousin, his son, and his wife.

And from that mythical time, every king has prayed the gods to grant him the humility to listen to the Antigone fate sends to him, no matter the guise.

Did you ask why? Because power without feedback is dangerous!

World.title: Abiodun seeks stronger government -church partnership as Egba Anglican Diocese clocks 50
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has called for a stronger partnership between government and the Church to raise disciplined, cultured and responsible young people capable of providing the leadership needed to drive Nigeria’s future development.

Governor Abiodun made the call on Sunday at the Golden Jubilee Thanksgiving Service of the Egba Anglican Diocese, held at Saint Peter’s Cathedral, Ake, Abeokuta.

The governor said while government has the responsibility to provide infrastructure, quality education and economic opportunities, the Church and other faith-based institutions have a critical role to play in building character, strengthening families and instilling sound moral values in the younger generation.

He noted that the 50th anniversary of the Egba Anglican Diocese, coming in the same year Ogun State marks its own golden jubilee, was a significant opportunity to reflect on the journey so far and renew the collective commitment to building a peaceful, prosperous and united society.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Abiodun stressed that true development must go beyond roads, bridges and physical infrastructure to include deliberate investment in human capital and character.

He warned that the rapid advancement of technology and artificial intelligence must not come at the expense of truth, wisdom, conscience and moral intelligence.

“The future we seek to build must be a future where technological advancement is matched by moral advancement; where artificial intelligence does not replace human wisdom, conscience and responsibility,” he said.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to religious harmony and peaceful coexistence, noting that the mutual respect among the various faith communities in Ogun had remained a major strength of the state.

He assured religious leaders that his administration would continue to partner with them in promoting peace, unity, responsible citizenship and values that strengthen the family and society.

As part of the anniversary activities, Governor Abiodun unveiled the commemorative plaque of the six-floor Cathedral Tower, praying that generations yet unborn would see the edifice as a symbol of a generation that believed in God, invested in His work and prepared responsibly for the future.

In his sermon, titled, “The Call Like Moses and the Strength Like Caleb,” the Archbishop, Metropolitan and Primate of All Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Most Reverend Henry C Ndukuba, urged Christians to respond to God’s call with renewed commitment, courage and strength.

Primate Ndukuba described the golden jubilee as a celebration of God’s faithfulness, while commending the Anglican Church for its enduring contributions to education, enlightenment and societal development.

The thanksgiving service attracted prominent dignitaries, including the Speaker of the Ogun State House of Assembly, Hon Oludaisi Elemide; Secretary to the State Government, Mr Tokunbo Talabi; former Chief of Staff, Toyin Taiwo; and the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, among others.

A major highlight of the celebration was the presentation of the Distinguished Benefactor of Egba Anglican Diocese Award to Governor Abiodun in recognition of his support and contributions to the Diocese.

Presenting the Jubilee Award, the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Michael Aremu Gbadebo, commended Governor Abiodun for his contributions to the development of Ogun State, declaring that his administration had surpassed previous administrations in housing delivery and industrialisation.

The monarch also commended the transformation of Abeokuta under the Abiodun administration, noting the significant development witnessed across the state capital and other parts of Ogun.

The governor’s participation in the jubilee celebration further underscored his administration’s commitment to building strong partnerships with religious institutions as part of its broader agenda of securing Ogun’s future through infrastructure, education, human capital development, peace and responsible citizenship.

World.title: Police probe death of Law School Student in Lagos hostel
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS—The Lagos State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the death of a 23-year-old female student of the Nigerian Law School at the institution’s hostel in Victoria Island, Lagos.

The incident reportedly occurred in the early hours of Friday, August 7, 2026, when the student, identified as Alayande Faith Ajoke, was found unresponsive within the hostel premises.

According to police sources, the Chief Matron of the Nigerian Law School, Mrs Igbokwe Juliana, reported the incident at the Victoria Island Police Division at about 6:30 a.m.

The report indicated that at about 4:30 a.m., another student, Ojo Abisoye Tinuola, who had recently completed her internship, alerted the matron after discovering her roommate in distress.

The matron reportedly proceeded to the scene, where she found the student lying on the ground within the hostel premises.

Preliminary observations suggested that the student may have fallen from the rooftop of the four-storey hostel building.

Police sources further disclosed that preliminary investigation indicated that the deceased may have left behind two notes addressed to her stepfather and roommate.

Following the report, detectives from the Victoria Island Police Division visited the scene, documented the area and took photographs as part of the investigation.

The remains were subsequently evacuated to the Mainland General Hospital Mortuary, Yaba, for preservation and autopsy.

The police said investigation was ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the student’s death.

World.title: Criminal Hideouts Clampdown: RRS nabs over 30 in Lagos
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS—Operatives of the Lagos State Rapid Response Squad, RRS, have arrested more than 30 suspected miscreants during a midnight enforcement operation along the Lekki-Ajah Expressway.

The operation, conducted on Sunday, was targeted at individuals allegedly causing disturbances and posing security concerns to motorists and other road users along the axis.

The State Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed the development on his Facebook page on Sunday.

According to Wahab, the operation focused on individuals allegedly involved in harassing and intimidating motorists, demanding money from them and, in some instances, damaging vehicles when their demands were not met.

He said the enforcement operation was part of ongoing efforts to improve safety and security along major roads in the state.

Wahab said the RRS would sustain intelligence-led operations and enforcement actions against activities capable of threatening public safety and disrupting the free movement of people and vehicles across Lagos State.

World.title: Super Falcons to face South Africa in World Cup play-off – date, time confirmed
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons will face South Africa’s Banyana Banyana in a crucial play-off as both teams battle for a route to the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

The highly anticipated encounter is scheduled for Thursday, August 13, 2026, with kick-off set for 9pm Nigeria time.

The match will be a major test for Nigeria after the Super Falcons lost 1-0 to Cameroon in their WAFCON quarter-final, a result that ended their hopes of securing an automatic ticket to the 2027 World Cup.

South Africa will now stand between Nigeria and a place in the next stage of the qualification process.

Nigeria vs South Africa

Match: Nigeria vs South Africa

Competition: 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup qualifying play-off

Date: Thursday, August 13, 2026

Time: 9pm Nigeria time

Teams: Super Falcons vs Banyana Banyana

The Super Falcons must win the encounter to keep their hopes of reaching the World Cup in Brazil alive.

Nigeria’s defeat to Cameroon meant they missed out on the four direct World Cup tickets available through the WAFCON semi-final places.

The play-off route therefore represents Nigeria’s second opportunity to qualify for the global tournament, but the Super Falcons can no longer afford another setback.

A victory over South Africa would move Nigeria closer to the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 qualifying play-offs and keep their hopes of featuring in Brazil alive.

Vanguard News

World.title: FG sends Passport intervention team to UK to clear pending applications
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Federal Government has deployed a dedicated Passport Intervention Team from the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS Headquarters to the United Kingdom, as part of ongoing efforts to ease and streamline passport applications for Nigerians in the diaspora.

According to the Service, Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, gave the directive to the Comptroller General of Immigration, Kemi Nandap.

The statement said the Intervention Team is scheduled to arrive in the United Kingdom on 10th August, 2026, and will work in collaboration with the Nigerian High Commission to facilitate the processing and issuance of pending, new and renewal passport applications.

“As part of the exercise, the intervention team will visit designated cities across the United Kingdom to conduct passport enrolment and processing, thereby enabling eligible applicants in different parts of the country to access the exercise,” the statement read.

According to the NIS, the intervention is open to applicants with pending passport applications, new applicants, and holders of passports with less than one year remaining before expiry who wish to apply for renewal. Applicants are to present their completed application forms and proof of payment during enrolment.

The Service said the detailed schedule for the intervention, including designated cities, dates, venues and enrolment times, would be announced separately, and advised applicants not to attend any location until the relevant schedule has been officially communicated.

“Applicants are therefore advised not to attend any location until the relevant schedule has been officially communicated and to monitor the official communication channels of the Nigerian High Commission in the United Kingdom for further details,” the statement said.

The NIS provided an email address, [email protected], and a WhatsApp-only line, +234 916 087 8000, for enquiries or complaints regarding the exercise.

The Service added that all its digital passport application channels, including the Contactless Passport Application System, would remain fully operational during the intervention exercise, alongside the existing home delivery service.

“The Nigeria Immigration Service remains committed to efficient, transparent and responsive passport service delivery to Nigerians at home and in the diaspora,” the statement added.

World.title: Burkina Faso thrash Flying Eagles 4-1, end Nigeria’s World Cup hopes
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flying Eagles have been knocked out of the race for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup after suffering a heavy 4-1 defeat to Burkina Faso in the final of the 2026 WAFU Zone B U-20 Championship.

The defeat at the Stade Charles Konan Banny in Yamoussoukro, Côte d’Ivoire, also ended Nigeria’s hopes of qualifying for the 2027 U-20 Africa Cup of Nations.

The WAFU Zone B final carried added importance, as the winner was guaranteed a place at the 2027 U-20 AFCON, which will serve as the qualifying tournament for the FIFA U-20 World Cup.

With Burkina Faso emerging victorious, the Young Stallions secured the region’s ticket, while Nigeria’s hopes of returning to the global youth tournament came to an end.

Burkina Faso took control of the final from the opening whistle, scoring three goals within the first 15 minutes and leaving the Flying Eagles with a huge task.

Nigeria struggled to contain the Young Stallings’ attacking pressure and could not recover from the early setback before the break.

Coach Abdu Maikaba’s side attempted to fight back after the interval but failed to produce the response required to turn the game around.

Burkina Faso eventually added another goal to complete a convincing 4-1 victory, while Nigeria’s consolation effort was not enough to change the outcome.

The result was particularly painful for the Flying Eagles after Burkina Faso had already defeated them 2-0 during the group stage.

Nigeria had hoped to avenge that earlier loss in the final but instead suffered another defeat to the Young Stallions when the stakes were highest.

The Flying Eagles had reached the final after overcoming Côte d’Ivoire in a dramatic semi-final.

The match ended 2-2 after regulation time before Nigeria prevailed 4-3 on penalties to book their place in the championship decider.

Burkina Faso, meanwhile, reached the final unbeaten after defeating Niger 2-0 in their semi-final.

The Young Stallions then completed an impressive campaign by defeating Nigeria 4-1 to claim the WAFU Zone B title and secure their place at the 2027 U-20 AFCON.

For Nigeria, the defeat means the seven-time U-20 AFCON champions will miss the 2027 continental tournament and the chance to qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup through the competition.

Vanguard News

World.title: 147 structures to be affected by coastal highway service lane
World.content:
A total of 147 structures in Lagos will be affected by the construction of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway service lane.

President Bola Tinubu made this known on Sunday at a stakeholder engagement and flag-off of repair works on Eko Bridge and Marine Bridge in Lagos, and the flooded section of Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The president said that, of the 147 structures, five would be cut fully and the others minimally.

Tinubu was represented by Lagos State Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu.

The President noted that Eko Bridge was one of the oldest bridges constructed after Nigeria’s independence, adding that Marine Bridge provided access to the seaports in Lagos State.

He urged the Lagos State Government to remain on a trajectory of irreversible development in every nook and cranny of this state.

”Today, in particular, is a day on which we have had extensive stakeholder engagement. We are truly happy with the turnout,” he said.

Tinubu said that the Federal Government had undertaken extensive renovation works in Lagos State.

“As a government, we must acknowledge and appreciate the efforts that have been made. This is about recognising the real work on the ground.”

He thanked the stakeholders, saying they had always turned out to discuss with the government anytime needed.

Tinubu praised the Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, for his efforts in road infrastructure development.

“For all of us to enjoy the full benefit of infrastructure, we have to shift a bit, so that it becomes an asset that will outlive all of us.”

He said that the stakeholder engagement was aimed at seeking the support of the people toward the implementation of the projects.

He gave the assurance that the Federal Government would make compensations where necessary.

“It will be given to you at the right time.

”There are days when we accept criticism for us to do better, but there are days when things have been done, and they have been done right, and we need to give recognition and support where it is most deserving.

“It is my honour to flag off all of these projects to the benefit of mankind, to our citizens in Lagos, to the benefit of all our people across the country,” Tinubu said.

World.title: FG deploys special guards to protect Lagos-Calabar highway
World.content:
Appoints retired Gen Shodunke to lead team

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — The Federal Government has inaugurated a dedicated security team, Coastal Highway Guards, to protect the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway against vandalism and other unauthorised activities.

The initiative was launched on Sunday by the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, with an initial deployment of 40 officers.

The development was announced in a statement posted on X by the Senior Special Assistant on New Media to the Lagos State Governor, Jubril Gawat.

The 750-kilometre, 10-lane Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is designed to connect Lagos to Cross River through Ogun, Ondo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers and Akwa Ibom states.

The project is being executed by Hitech Construction Company Limited under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Works.

According to Gawat, the special guards will maintain a security presence along the highway, report suspicious activities, monitor and report vandalism, and prevent hawking, the use of tricycles and motorcycles, as well as loitering along the road.

He said the team would be led by retired General Adekunle Shodunke and would work with other security agencies in Lagos State.

Quoting Umahi, Gawat said the initiative was a full-time security assignment aimed at protecting national assets.

“The Hon. Minister says this is not an ‘empowerment programme’. It is a full-time job to protect national assets of the government and in line with the Renewed Hope of Mr President, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR,” he quoted the minister as saying.

Earlier on Sunday, Umahi expressed concern over the removal of construction materials and unauthorised occupation of sections of the highway.

“We have had very terrible, unpatriotic elements removing the blocks, breaking the fence, removing the rods and treading on the highway. This must stop,” he said.

The minister directed the Federal Controller of Works in Lagos to ensure that motorcycles, tricycles, hawkers and other unauthorised users were kept off the coastal road.

“Their job is that no keke on the coastal highway, no motorcycle on the coastal highway, and no loitering. There is no superhighway all over the country where you see people loitering,” he added.

Umahi said that during an inspection of the project with members of the National Assembly at about 11 p.m., people were found sleeping on the highway.

“Last night, we were there with the National Assembly members by 11 pm; people were sleeping on the coastal highway. It must stop. No hawking, no occupation illegally along the entire coast,” he said.

He also called on the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, to strengthen the protection of strategic national infrastructure.

The minister further disclosed that the Ministry of Works had opened its ongoing projects to scrutiny by anti-corruption agencies.

World.title: FRSC confirms 15 dead, 25 injured in Niger road crash
World.content:
The scene of the accident. Credit: FRSC

The Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps in Niger, Aishatu Sa’adu, has confirmed the killing of 15 travellers with 25 others hospitalised following a fatal road crash along Enagi-Mokwa Road.

Speaking with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Minna, the Sector Commander said the accident involved two buses coming from the same direction.

According to her, 15 people were burnt to death when the buses were engulfed in flames after the head-on collision on the evening of Saturday.

She added that 25 other travellers, who sustained injuries, were evacuated to the Federal Medical Centre in Bida and General Hospital in Kutigi.

Sa’adu attributed the accident to wrongfully overtaking at a bend and overspeeding.

“The accident was as a result of overspeeding and wrongfully overtaking.

“I advise motorists to always maintain a good speed limit and avoid wrongful overtaking,” she said.

World.title: NAF Air Interdiction Kills ISWAP Commander, Eight Other Extremists in Borno
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) yesterday revealed that the Air Component of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, eliminated a key ISWAP commander and eight other extremist fighters during a coordinated air interdiction operation in Borno State.

The Service said those killed were reportedly responsible for facilitating the movement and protection of high-value members of the group.

The Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists have continued to attack soft targets in Borno and other North-East states in an apparent attempt to disguise their imminent defeat.

Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have continued to repel attacks on communities and military formations while intensifying their onslaught against the extremists within their areas of responsibility, leading to the surrender of multiple terrorist fighters and their families.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the successful operation was conducted following credible intelligence on the activities and movements of suspected terrorists within the Sambisa Forest area.

“Acting on the intelligence, the NAF deployed a Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA) to conduct persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), enabling the identification and tracking of a group of terrorists as they moved towards a suspected hideout. Following the positive identification and confirmation of the target, the NAF aircraft conducted a precision engagement on the location.

“Subsequent battle damage assessment indicated significant effects on the targeted compound, with several terrorists neutralised. Further intelligence received after the strike confirmed that nine ISWAP fighters were killed, while several others were wounded. Among those reportedly neutralised was Abu Khalid Al Muhajir, described as a prominent ISWAP commander responsible for providing special security escorts for the movement of senior members of the terrorist group,” the statement said.

Air Commodore Ejodame said his elimination represented a significant operational setback for ISWAP, particularly given his reported knowledge of the routes, terrain and tactical movements connecting major terrorist enclaves within the Sambisa Forest and surrounding areas.

He said: “Intelligence further indicated that some of the terrorists affected by the strike were assessed to be linked to elements suspected to have been involved in the recent ambush of Nigerian troops along the Bita–Yamtage axis in Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State. The latest success underscores the growing effectiveness of the NAF’s intelligence-driven air operations, particularly the integration of persistent ISR and precision-strike capabilities to detect, track and neutralise terrorist elements before they can regroup or threaten friendly forces and vulnerable communities. Beyond the immediate casualties, the operation is expected to disrupt ISWAP’s leadership protection arrangements, the movement of high-value personnel and the coordination of activities across its enclaves.”

The Nigerian Air Force, Ejodame said, would continue to sustain intelligence-led and precision air operations in close coordination with surface forces, with the objective of degrading terrorist capabilities, disrupting their freedom of movement and creating a more secure environment for affected communities across the North-East.

World.title: Arise Recounts Role in Establishment of FUOYE
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Former Senator representing Ekiti North Senatorial District, Senator Ayo Arise, has sought to set the record straight on the establishment of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE), recounting how his intervention and engagements with the Federal Government initiated the process that eventually brought the institution to Oye-Ekiti.

Arise, who served in the National Assembly between 2007 and 2011, said recent narratives crediting other individuals with the establishment of the university amounted to a distortion of the history of the institution and a disservice to those who worked to secure its location in Oye-Ekiti.

Addressing journalists in Ado-Ekiti, the former lawmaker said the process began shortly after the then President, Goodluck Jonathan, announced on November 28, 2010, that the Federal Government would establish six new federal universities in states without such institutions.

According to Arise, he acted the following day by writing to the Minister of Education through the ministry’s then Permanent Secretary, Professor Oladapo Afolabi, requesting that one of the proposed universities be established in Oye-Ekiti.

He said Professor Afolabi subsequently directed him to present the request to the then Minister of State for Education, the late Kenneth Gbagi.

Arise recalled that he immediately visited Gbagi’s office, where he met the minister alongside the then Executive Secretary of the National Universities Commission (NUC), Professor Peter Okojie, and Professor Mahmood Yakubu of the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), who later became Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

He said it was during the meeting that Gbagi indicated that Oye-Ekiti had already been identified as one of the locations for the proposed universities, alongside Otuoke.

Arise said his intervention was driven by the conviction that Oye-Ekiti had the facilities and historical connection necessary to accommodate a federal university.

He recalled telling Gbagi that Oye was ready to host the institution, pointing to the existence of a Federal Government teachers’ college established in the community in the 1970s.

The former senator said the subsequent inspection of facilities led to another phase of the process, which eventually generated controversy over whether the university should be located in Oye or Ikole-Ekiti.

He said the controversy intensified after officials visited Ekiti and the then newly sworn-in Governor, Dr Kayode Fayemi, took them to Ikole-Ekiti for an inspection.

According to him, the late Gbagi subsequently declared that he had established a Federal University of Agriculture in Ikole, a development that created tension between the two communities.

Arise, however, said the controversy was eventually resolved through a dual-campus arrangement, with Ikole-Ekiti hosting the Faculty of Agriculture while Oye-Ekiti remained the main campus as approved by the Federal Executive Council.

He disclosed that he met Fayemi on July 31, 2011, for nearly two hours to address the land and Certificate of Occupancy issues surrounding the project.

While acknowledging Fayemi’s role in resolving the location-related challenges, Arise maintained that the initial request for the university to be established in Oye-Ekiti came from him.

He also addressed the role of Dr Femi Ajayi, a former Director-General of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), who he said had been credited in some quarters with securing the university.

Arise described Ajayi as a “decent gentleman” who played a supportive role but was not the initiator of the process.

According to him, Ajayi had a longstanding relationship with President Jonathan, having served with him at Iresi and later occupied several federal positions, including Senior Special Assistant to the President on Diaspora Affairs, Director-General of NDLEA and Executive Secretary of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF).

He said Ajayi was particularly useful to him because he was the person he could most easily reach at the Presidency and who reliably conveyed his messages to President Jonathan.

“Dr. Femi Ajayi was the person I could most easily reach at the Presidency, and he reliably conveyed my messages to Mr. President,” Arise said.

He stressed, however, that Ajayi’s supportive role should not be confused with initiating the establishment process.

“As far as I am concerned, Dr. Femi Ajayi remains a good man,” he said, adding that Ajayi was “one of the contributors that supported me as needed.”

Arise further explained that his relationship with President Jonathan predated the university project, dating back to his tenure as Chairman of the Senate Committee on Privatization in 2007.

He said Jonathan, who was then Vice President and statutory Chairman of the National Council on Privatization, had a working relationship with his committee, which provided him with opportunities to engage directly with the then Vice President.

According to him, the relationship continued after Jonathan became Acting President in February 2010 and President in May of the same year, giving him a direct channel through which he could pursue issues of importance to his constituency.

Arise urged Ekiti people to approach the history of FUOYE with fairness and integrity, rather than allowing political considerations to rewrite the circumstances surrounding its establishment.

He said the sequence of events surrounding the university’s establishment should be properly documented and preserved for future generations.

“I have become aware of recent narratives about the establishment of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti. Some of these accounts appear to be deliberate attempts to diminish my role in the effort that, by God’s grace and with President Jonathan’s approval, led to the university being established in Oye-Ekiti,” he said.

Arise added that while several individuals contributed to the eventual establishment of FUOYE, the role of those who initiated and sustained the process should not be erased from the history of the institution.

World.title: Prof Alfred Kasunmu Dies at 92
World.content:
•Bayo Ojo, Ajogwu, Nwobike, Ajayi, others celebrate legal luminary’s enduring legacy

Wale Igbintade

The Nigerian legal profession has been thrown into mourning following the death of renowned legal scholar, advocate and former Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Lagos State, Professor Alfred Bandele Kasunmu, SAN, who died peacefully in the early hours of Sunday, August 9, 2026. He was 92.

Kasunmu, widely regarded as one of the most distinguished figures of Nigeria’s legal profession and a towering personality of the golden era of Nigerian advocacy, was remembered yesterday by leading members of the Bar as a remarkable scholar, gentleman, mentor and statesman whose contributions profoundly shaped legal education, jurisprudence and legal practice in Nigeria.

Among those who paid glowing tributes to the late legal luminary was former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Chief Bayo Ojo, SAN, who described Kasunmu as a remarkable scholar and gentleman whose influence extended far beyond the classroom and courtroom.

Recalling his personal encounter with the deceased, Ojo said Kasunmu was his Dean at the Faculty of Law of the University of Lagos (UNILAG) in 1974.

“He was my Dean at the Faculty of Law of the University of Lagos in 1974.”

Ojo said learning under Kasunmu left an indelible mark on his career and that of countless other lawyers who passed through his tutelage.

According to him, Kasunmu possessed a rare combination of intellectual brilliance, professional competence, humility and dignity.

Despite his formidable knowledge of the law, Ojo said, the late professor never used his intellectual superiority to intimidate others but deployed it to illuminate difficult legal questions, challenge young minds and encourage his students to think deeply and independently.

Ojo described Kasunmu as a foundational figure in the development of modern Nigerian jurisprudence, noting that his life was devoted not only to the practice of law but also to the advancement of legal knowledge and the training of successive generations of lawyers.

As Dean of the Faculty of Law, UNILAG, between 1973 and 1975, Kasunmu, Ojo noted, played a pivotal role in shaping young legal minds while maintaining high standards of academic discipline and professional excellence.

Also mourning the legal icon, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Dr Joseph Nwobike, SAN, said Kasunmu made invaluable contributions to legal education and practice in Nigeria.

Nwobike noted that Kasunmu was among the early Nigerian academics who ventured into legal practice, bringing to advocacy a depth of scholarship that distinguished him from his contemporaries.

“As one of the early academics who ventured into law practice, his advocacy in courts was very analytical and progressive.

Through the various cases that he handled, he helped to define the Nigerian common law,” Nwobike said.

Although he was not one of Kasunmu’s students, Nwobike said he had the privilege of studying several of the deceased’s learned works during his undergraduate and postgraduate education.

“In the courts, Prof, as we fondly called him with great respect, was brilliant and infectious in his exposition and use of the law to drive home his ideas around the issues of law in the cases that he conducted,” he said.

Nwobike described Kasunmu as “the last of the golden era of Nigerian lawyers,” adding that his death would be deeply felt by the Bar, Bench and the wider legal community.

Another Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Professor Fabian Ajogwu, OFR, SAN, described Kasunmu as “a great Iroko of the Inner Bar” who had taken his final bow.

In a personal tribute, Ajogwu recalled his first encounter with Kasunmu as a young lawyer in the early 1990s at the Lagos High Court.

He said he watched with admiration as Kasunmu addressed the court with remarkable refinement of language and brilliance of advocacy.

“I knew I was in the presence of greatness,” Ajogwu said, adding that Kasunmu’s name would remain synonymous with legal excellence, intellectual rigour and unimpeachable integrity.

According to him, it was only after he had the privilege of knowing Kasunmu beyond his courtroom reputation that he fully appreciated the magnitude of the man’s character and stature.

“Professor Kasunmu was a colossus in the legal profession and a luminous beacon in legal education,” Ajogwu said.

He noted that as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Kasunmu wielded the law as a noble instrument of justice and social transformation through persuasion.

“In the courtroom and classroom, he commanded respect through his wisdom and the quiet dignity of his carriage,” he said.

Ajogwu described the late professor as the “gold standard” and a benchmark against which members of the legal profession could measure their aspirations and professional conduct.

“Prof was a mentor whose footsteps we sought to trace, even when we knew the path was steep and the pace formidable,” he said.

He added that Kasunmu’s dedication to the law, service to humanity and high moral standards had left an enduring imprint on the professional and personal lives of generations of lawyers.

Ajayi: ‘He was a lawyer of all seasons’

Professor Konyinsola Ajayi, SAN, also paid tribute to Kasunmu, describing him as a lawyer who successfully embodied the three principal dimensions of the legal profession — academia, public service and practice.

Reflecting on Kasunmu’s extraordinary career, Ajayi recalled a description of the late professor in his 78th year in 2012 as one of the few lawyers who had attained distinction as an academic, technocrat and practitioner.

Ajayi said Kasunmu’s career exemplified the description of a “lawyer of all seasons”, noting that he had left an enduring imprint on legal education, law and justice.

In a lecture delivered at the Professor A.B. Kasunmu Annual Lecture at the Faculty of Law, University of Lagos, on July 11, 2018, titled “Conflation of Time: Analogue Practice & Digital Reality,” Ajayi described Kasunmu as a “gentle giant of the mind” whose intellectual legacy continued to inspire generations.

He said Kasunmu had succeeded in “leaving a stamp on time” through his contribution to law and justice and his role in producing some of the finest legal minds in Nigeria.

Family announces death

Kasunmu’s death was formally announced by his family, which described him as a beloved father, grandfather and great-grandfather.

“With gratitude to God for a life well spent, we announce the passing of our beloved father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, Professor Alfred Bandele Kasunmu, SAN, who departed peacefully in the early hours of Sunday, 9th August 2026,” the family said.

Born on May 23, 1934, in Lagos to parents from Ilesa, Osun State, Kasunmu received his early education at Elizabeth Fowler Memorial School, Reagan Memorial Baptist School and Baptist Academy, Lagos.

He proceeded to University College London, where he obtained his Bachelor of Laws and Master of Laws degrees.

He was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1964 and began his academic career the same year as one of the pioneer lecturers at the Faculty of Law of the University of Ife, now Obafemi Awolowo University.

In 1971, he joined the University of Lagos as a senior lecturer and was subsequently elevated to the rank of Professor of Law.

He served as Dean of the Faculty of Law, University of Lagos, from 1973 to 1975 before his appointment in 1975 as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Lagos State, a position he held for three years.

His appointment as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria followed on January 25, 1978, placing him among the earliest members of the Inner Bar.

Kasunmu was also a Notary Public of Nigeria and remained active in legal scholarship and advocacy for decades.

A prolific author, he was joint author of several influential legal texts and published numerous scholarly articles covering a wide range of legal subjects.

His legal practice spanned several areas of Nigerian law.

He represented prominent expatriate and domestic clients before courts at various levels and appeared as counsel before arbitration panels in Nigeria and abroad.

Also mourning the legal icon, Professor Taiwo Osipitan, SAN, described Kasunmu as a father, friend, mentor, role model and “lecturer of lecturers” and “professor of professors,” whose influence extended across generations of Nigerian lawyers.

Osipitan said Kasunmu was an amiable and gentle man, a quick-witted scholar blessed with an uncommon photographic memory, and an inspiring leader within the body of Senior Advocates of Nigeria.

According to him, Kasunmu remained faithful to the legal profession throughout his life and was “an advocate of advocates” and a repository of knowledge.

“Prof ABK was our father, friend, mentor, role model, lecturer of lecturers, professor of professors and an amiable leader of the body of Senior Advocates of Nigeria,” Osipitan said.

He added that Kasunmu was not only devoted to the legal profession but also excelled as a family man.

“He was amiable, gentle and quick-witted and blessed with uncommon photographic memory.

He was faithful to the legal profession and was an advocate of advocates, a repository of knowledge and a family person par excellence,” he said.

Osipitan said Kasunmu’s death had created a void that would be difficult to fill, adding that the late legal luminary would be sorely missed by all who knew him.

World.title: UN Youth Office Disowns Fake Agency DG Adeyemi
World.content:
The United Nations has disowned Mr Adeniyi Adeyemi Matthew over his alleged appointment to a position within the UN Youth Office, declaring that he has no appointment, employment or affiliation with the organisation.

The UN Youth Office also stated that Adeyemi was never authorised to represent the office or the United Nations in any capacity.

The clarification was contained in a letter dated July 27, 2026, with reference number UNYO-2026-0017, issued by the United Nations Youth Office and released through Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York.

The letter was written in response to a note from Nigeria’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations dated July 1, 2026, seeking clarification on Adeyemi’s purported appointment and documents allegedly linked to the position.

In the letter, the UN Youth Office stated that Adeyemi “holds no appointment, employment, or affiliation of any kind with the Office” and had never been authorised to represent it in any capacity.

The development was disclosed by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, who said the communication had settled questions surrounding Adeyemi’s alleged appointment and the documents associated with it.

The controversy had also triggered allegations of forgery involving the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, over documents reportedly connected to Adeyemi’s purported appointment.

However, Ibrahim said the clarification from the UN Youth Office effectively cleared Gbajabiamila of the allegation, arguing that the official communication established that Adeyemi had no appointment or formal relationship with the UN Youth Office.

He said the UN position should put the controversy in its proper perspective and end claims portraying Adeyemi as an appointee or representative of the organisation.

Ibrahim urged the media and members of the public to rely on official communications from the United Nations and other competent authorities when reporting issues relating to international appointments.

He warned that reliance on unverified claims could fuel misinformation and cause reputational damage to individuals and institutions.

The envoy stressed that the latest clarification represented the official position of the UN Youth Office on Adeyemi’s alleged appointment.

World.title: Rep Dasuki Urges INEC to Hold 2027 General Election in One Day, Warns of Loophole in Section 63 (2) of Electoral Act
World.content:
Says Section 63 (2) will compromise integrity of election with fake ballot papers

Commends military salary increase, recommends housing for all personnel

Rep Abdussamad Dasuki, Deputy Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to reconsider the staggered arrangement for the 2027 general election and hold the federal and state elections on a single day.

Dasuki also raised concerns over Section 63 (2) of the Electoral Act which, he warned, could potentially compromise the integrity of the 2027 general election by allowing ballot papers without the prescribed official mark of the electoral commission to be counted under certain circumstances.

He said this at the weekend while receiving youths of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), who visited him to congratulate him on his emergence as deputy minority leader.

Addressing the youths, the lawmaker said conducting the 2027 general election on a single day would save the country huge economic losses arising from the disruption of socio-economic activities associated with staggered general election.

He argued that a one-day election would also significantly reduce the financial burden on government, as allowances and other expenses for ad hoc electoral personnel, security agencies and other election-related logistics would be incurred for only one day instead of two separate election days. He said this had become necessary considering the paucity of funds for other needs having direct impact on the welfare of the people.

According to him, combining the elections would equally reduce the number of election-related trips that Nigerians and other participants would have to undertake, particularly in view of the country’s security challenges.

He explained that under the current arrangement, people travelling for election purposes could be required to make one trip in January for the federal elections and another in February for the state elections. A single election day, he said, would mean that such journeys would only have to be made once.

Dasuki urged INEC to merge the federal and state elections and conduct them in either January or February 2027.

He said the combined election would involve five ballot papers covering the presidential, senatorial and House of Representatives elections at the federal level, as well as the governorship and State House of Assembly elections at the state level.

The deputy minority leader maintained that INEC had the capacity to manage the five ballot papers efficiently and effectively if adequate preparations were made ahead of the polls.

He further noted that the existence of eight off-cycle governorship elections would make a single-day election even more practicable, as governorship elections would not be held in 8 states during the 2027 cycle. He added that in those 8 states, the ballot papers would reduce to four.

Dasuki said the arrangement would not only simplify the electoral process but also help reduce the movement of voters, political actors, election officials and security personnel across the country.

“Considering the security situation in Nigeria, participants should not be required to make two separate journeys for elections when the process can be efficiently organised to take place on one day,” he said.

Raising concerns over a provision of the Electoral Act which, he warned, could potentially compromise the integrity of the 2027 general election by allowing ballot papers without the prescribed official mark of the electoral commission to be counted under certain circumstances, Dasuki wants Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act to be expunged.

He argued that the provision could create a loophole capable of facilitating the use of fake or unauthorised ballot papers during elections.

He drew attention to the provisions of Section 63(1) and (2), particularly the apparent contradiction between the two subsections.

Quoting Section 63(1), he said: “Subject to subsection (2), a ballot paper which does not bear official mark prescribed by the commission shall not be counted.”

He, however, expressed concern over the qualification contained in Section 63(2), which provides:

“Where the returning officer is satisfied that a ballot paper which does not bear the official mark was from a book of ballot papers which was furnished to the presiding officer of the polling unit in which the vote was cast for use at the election in question, he or she shall, notwithstanding the absence of the official mark, count the ballot paper.”

Rep Dasuki argued that permitting ballot papers without the prescribed official mark to be counted could expose the electoral process to abuse and make it difficult to distinguish genuine ballot papers from counterfeit ones.

He assured that the minority leaders are working to ensure that it was corrected before the 2027 elections.

The lawmaker also commended the recent increase in the salaries of members of the Armed Forces, describing the measure as a step in the right direction.

He, however, called for further improvements in the welfare of military personnel, particularly in the area of accommodation.

Dasuki stressed that all military personnel should be provided with decent accommodation, noting that improved living conditions were essential to the morale and effectiveness of the Armed Forces.

He also reiterated his earlier call for forfeited properties to be handed over to the military for use as accommodation and other facilities.

The lawmaker said strengthening the welfare of military personnel was particularly important given the demanding security responsibilities they continue to shoulder across the country.

World.title: 2027: APC Completes Upload of All Candidates Ahead of Deadline
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general election, the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has revealed that the party has successfully uploaded into the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) portal all its candidates into all available elective positions.

Yilwatda, in a statement issued Sunday by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, disclosed this at the weekend after the successful completion of the exercise, well ahead of the deadline initially set by INEC.

He added that the successful completion of the upload of the party’s candidates across the country from the state House of Assembly to the president was a demonstration of the APC’s organisational strength, institutional discipline and readiness for the 2027 elections.

The chairman noted that while the APC completed the exercise within the original timeframe, several other political parties were still struggling to meet the deadline and subsequently appealed to INEC for additional time to complete their submissions.

Following these appeals, INEC extended the deadline from Saturday, August 8, 2026, to Tuesday, August 11, 2026, giving political parties an additional three days to conclude their submissions through the commission’s online portal.

Yilwatda described the development as another clear indication that the party has moved beyond the politics of slogans to the politics of structure, planning, systems and execution.

He noted: “The ability of a political party to successfully coordinate the nomination, documentation, verification and electronic submission of thousands of candidates across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory within a prescribed timeline is a serious test of organisational capacity.

“The APC has once again demonstrated that we are prepared for the responsibility of governing Nigeria. We did not wait until the last minute.

“We planned ahead, coordinated our structures and ensured that our candidates were successfully uploaded before the expiration of the original deadline. This is what organisation, discipline and responsible political leadership mean.”

Yilwatda added that the successful completion of the exercise was particularly significant because the 2027 elections would be one of the most consequential electoral contests in the history of Nigeria, requiring political parties to demonstrate not only popularity but also capacity, internal coordination and preparedness.

The national chairman stressed that the APC’s performance should also be viewed against the complexity of managing a nationwide political organisation with structures in every state, senatorial district, federal constituency and local government area.

He explained that the exercise required meticulous coordination between the National Secretariat, state chapters, candidates and other relevant party structures.

The chairman noted that the ability to complete the process ahead of schedule reflected the efficiency of the systems being developed under the current leadership of the party.

Yilwatda further stated that the development sends an important message to Nigerians about the importance of organisational capacity in choosing political parties and leaders.

He cautioned Nigerians against political parties that are quick to make ambitious promises about governing the country but are unable to demonstrate basic organisational competence within their own structures.

The chairman added: “Governance is not an experiment. The management of a country as complex as Nigeria requires planning, coordination, discipline, competence and the ability to deliver within deadlines.

“If a political organisation cannot effectively organise its own internal processes, coordinate its candidates and meet simple statutory and administrative deadlines, Nigerians must ask serious questions about its preparedness to manage the affairs of the nation.

“Political parties seeking the mandate of Nigerians must be judged not only by their campaign rhetoric but also by their internal systems, preparedness, capacity to manage people and resources, and ability to comply with electoral regulations.”

The APC National Chairman said the party’s achievement should therefore not be interpreted merely as the completion of an administrative exercise, but as an important early indicator of its preparedness for the 2027 electoral contest.

He added that having its candidates properly uploaded ahead of the original deadline gives the party greater room to concentrate on the next stages of its electoral preparations, including campaign coordination, candidate engagement, voter mobilisation, grassroots organisation, policy communication and reconciliation across its various structures.

Yilwatda also commended the APC National Working Committee, state party leadership, candidates, election management teams and all party officials who contributed to the successful completion of the exercise.

The chairman said the achievement was a collective victory for the party and another demonstration that the APC remains Nigeria’s most organised and institutionally prepared political movement.

He said: “The work has only begun. Completing the upload ahead of schedule gives us confidence, but it also places a greater responsibility on us. We must remain united, disciplined and focused.

“We must take our message of Renewed Hope to every community and demonstrate to Nigerians that the APC is not only prepared to contest elections; we are prepared to continue providing responsible leadership for Nigeria,” he said.

The APC National Chairman said the party would continue to put in place the necessary structures and systems to ensure that the 2027 elections become another opportunity for Nigerians to make an informed choice based on competence, continuity, stability and national development.

World.title: Women Group Decries Senate’s Confirmation of Fasina As Ambassador
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

Over 300 women’s rights organizations have rejected the Nigerian Senate’s confirmation of Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina as Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, citing alleged disregard for pending sexual harassment cases and due process.

In a petition signed by Co-Convener of Womanifesto, Wumi Asubiaro-Dada, the groups described the Senate’s action as “a charade of shame, travesty of justice and in total oblivion of existing petitions”.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio confirmed Fasina during plenary, citing four reasons: that the nominee is from Lagos State with no opposition, that no petition was submitted against him, the principle of presumption of innocence, and that the police and FUOYE Governing Council had cleared him.

The coalition disputed all four points while insisting that Fasina is from Abeokuta South Local Government Area of Ogun State, despite being educated in Lagos, and not an indigene of Lagos State.

The groups said two petitions dated June 25, 2026 and June 29, 2026, with acknowledged copies, were submitted to the Office of the Senate President and the Chairman, Senate Committee on Foreign Affairs, adding that also attached were details of two suits pending at the National Industrial Court.

According to the petition, “Ambassadorial appointments demand public confidence, ethical credibility and demonstrable respect for accountability processes. Confirming a nominee while multiple judicial proceedings remain pending sends a dangerous signal to survivors of workplace sexual harassment.

“The first, Suit No. NICN/ABJ/201/2025, is a sexual harassment case filed by a FUOYE staffer. The petitioners said it is supported by a 37-minute audio recording allegedly of Prof. Fasina. The second, Suit No. NICN/LA/61/2025, alleges harassment and victimization.

“The complainant claims she was denied promotion and later had her appointment terminated after rejecting alleged advances, in violation of a court order to maintain peace.”

The groups also challenged claims that Fasina had been cleared, arguing that the police lack constitutional powers to give final clearance on sexual harassment allegations and that the FUOYE panel that dismissed the case was composed of university employees under the control of the then vice-chancellor.

On the issue of appearance before the Senate, the CSOs said no invitation was extended to the complainants or civil society groups, contrary to the Senate’s claim that victims “failed to appear”. They cited Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution on the right to fair hearing.

The petition further referenced House of Representatives records indicating that Folasade Adebayo submitted over 100 pages of evidence and travelled to Abuja on May 14, 2025 for a scheduled hearing.

The hearing was postponed indefinitely after Fasina allegedly failed to respond to the committee’s invitation.

The CSOs also stated that the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) commenced an investigation in 2025 into allegations of abuse of office and sexual harassment.

They alleged that Fasina obtained a court order restraining the ICPC and that the matter remained pending.

World.title: ‘Horrified!’: Women For Change on Cameron Waldeck-Cooks’ death
World.content:
Women For Change have acknolwedged the death of Cameron Waldeck-Cooks. Image via Instagram

Anti-gender-based violence (GBV) activists Women For Change have spoken out about the death of Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a St Stithians student who died in an alleged murder-suicide alongside her boyfriend, Ethan Coetzee, this week.

The bodies of the teen couple were discovered at a Sabie game lodge on Monday, 3 August.

According to Ethan’s family, the 17-year-old and the 19-year-old were in a relationship and had finished a hiking expedition.



WOMEN FOR CHANGE

In a social media post, Women For Change, known for their anti-GBV advocacy, paid tribute to Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, whose death occurred during Women’s Month.

The post read: “Women For Change is horrified by yet another devastating femicide case involving a young woman whose life was cut tragically short.

“Our hearts are with Cameron’s family, friends, classmates, and everyone mourning this unimaginable loss.



“We are horrified that this tragedy also involves a young man, highlighting the urgent need to address violence, harmful gender norms, and healthy relationship education among young people and in schools”.

The organisation added: “When is enough, enough?”

In an open letter to President Cyril Ramaphosa, Women For Change founder Sabrina Walter named Cameron Waldeck-Cooks as one of several women who have tragically been murdered during Women’s Month.

She shared: “How many more names will we say before action replaces promises? Women’s Day cannot become another day of flowers, hashtags and speeches while women continue to bury their daughters, mothers, sisters and friends”

WHAT HAPPENED TO CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS AND ETHAN COETZEE?

Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, 17, and Ethan Coetzee, 19, were found dead at a lodge in the Sabie area of Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August. Cameron was a Grade 11 learner at St Stithians Girls College, while Ethan had matriculated in 2025.

Police initially investigated the deaths as an inquest and initially suspected that no foul play was involved.

However, post-mortem findings changed the direction of the investigation.



According to preliminary findings as well as the opinion of an independent forensic pathologist involved, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks died from strangulation/suffocation.

Ethan’s death is believed to be a suicide.

Police have subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death.



No person has been charged with Cameron’s murder, and police have not publicly announced that Ethan was legally determined to be her killer. The investigation continues.
