World.title: Estonia's parties betting on tax cuts, AI and demographics ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
Reviving Estonia's economy, reversing the decline in the birth rate and ensuring national security emerged as the key issues ahead of the 2027 elections at Opinion Festival's party chairmen debate.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) highlighted national defense and revitalizing the economy as his most important goals.

"When I formed the government, I promised two things: first, that Estonia would be firmly defended. To the extent that it is in our hands, it certainly is. We have had to do many different things to fund defense spending, and we are probably now paying a price for that in terms of popularity — there is no doubt about it. But I think that when history looks back, what matters is what you have done, not what people happen to be saying at the moment," the prime minister began.

Michal's second point was economic growth, which he said cannot be credited solely to the government or politicians.

"It is certainly cyclical, and as a small, open economy we are particularly dependent on our partners. But economic growth means that people and businesses have more money on payday. At the beginning of this year, Estonia saw the largest tax cut in its history, which certainly provided this momentum. We want to pursue the same policy — Estonia is defended, the economy grows and the people of Estonia become wealthier," Michal emphasized.

The prime minister's third priority was looking to the future, including a clean natural environment, new technologies and innovation.

"And also a sound set of values. I am under no illusions — I understand that these elections will be a repeat performance by the same old EKRE-IKE band (former coalition of EKRE, Isamaa and the Center Party — ed.) /.../ We want to preserve the same liberal democratic values on which Estonia was built. Estonia has been a forward-looking country, not one that looks to the past for solutions," Michal concluded.

Opinion Festival 2026. Prime Minister Kristen Michal and Eesti 200 head Kristina Kallas. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Isamaa

Urmas Reinsalu, chair of the Isamaa party that currently tops party ratings, said trust needs to be restored in society, starting with the country's economic outlook.

"Generating economic growth cannot simply be a slogan; it has to begin with restoring optimism among investors and entrepreneurs. Isamaa's first message is that, unfortunately, the government has done everything it can to suppress that economic growth. Economic policy cannot be based on simply making the economic outlook more fragile. That has to change fundamentally; we need a fundamentally different approach," Reinsalu said.

Reinsalu's second priority was providing families with a sense of security and restoring the purchasing power of families and individuals, while also giving people the freedom to start families and develop themselves.

"Third is an unconditional commitment to Estonia's national defense. Isamaa has always supported — whether in opposition or in government — the steps necessary to restore and ensure Estonia's military security, internal security and civil protection. We intend to continue doing so unconditionally after the elections," Reinsalu said.

Parempoolsed

Non-parliamentary Parempoolsed chair Lavly Perling said she had been making the same point for four years: words are not enough; they must be turned into action.

"When we talk about defense spending, it cannot be the case that only 27 percent of the taxes collected for it actually get there. Words are not enough; decisions and actions are needed. We have said very clearly that our Estonia is free, prosperous and Estonian-minded. How do we achieve that? Through lower taxes and greater freedom — more freedom, fewer taxes. When we talk about tax increases, we are talking about taking away people's freedom to decide for themselves how to use their own money," Perling said.

Perling said government spending needs to be cut to restore people's sense of security.

"We need to start talking about the fact that our state budget is on an unsustainable course. Everywhere you turn, you are starting to hear what I have called a marketplace of promises. Urmas promises lower taxes and more benefits, while on the other side we once again hear the same kinds of promises we heard four years ago. We are not offering sweet talk; we are saying that we need to start making difficult decisions. We need to do that so the next generation inherits a prosperous and exciting Estonia — that is what drives our decisions," Perling emphasized.

EKRE chair Martin Helme said Estonia's biggest concern is its natural population growth, as well as demographics more broadly.

EKRE

"If we look at what has just happened again in Spain, the immigration crisis that EKRE was talking about 10 or 11 years ago has not gone anywhere. Over the past decade, more than 50 million Africans and Muslims have arrived in Europe. This is no joke. We talk about having an immigration crisis in Estonia, with various illegal immigrants scurrying back and forth; the situation remains critical and is getting increasingly horrific. Addressing immigration at the level of the nation-state and the national border is extremely important. Hiding behind the Schengen border means, quite frankly, abandoning your responsibility for Estonia's security and the safety of its people," Helme said, adding that immigration is only one part of the problem, because if Estonia fails to raise its birth rate, the country has no future.

Opinion Festival 2026. Kristina Kallas and EKRE chair Martin Helme. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"If Estonia has no future, it no longer makes any difference who carries on here — whether Chinese, Arabs or Ukrainians. Everything else, whether tax debates or security debates, becomes irrelevant, because if there are no Estonians left here, all of this becomes someone else's problem. Natural population growth is therefore critically important, and that means family and population policy," Helme explained.

Helme said the coalition had failed on national defense because it had spent large amounts of money without having anything to show for it.

"First you drove the Estonian economy into contraction for 13 consecutive quarters, and now you are crowing because it has posted a small increase for a second quarter in a row. The people who messed things up cannot be the ones to fix them. Donald Trump shows us the way on economic growth: low taxes and little regulation. Of course, if the earlier question was what we should give up, there are some very easy choices. We will give up the green transition, give up Rail Baltica and give up hundreds of millions in foreign aid that, in reality, makes its way back through corrupt channels," Helme concluded.

Eesti 200

Eesti 200 chair Kristina Kallas said Estonia's economic growth problem is low labor productivity.

"That means that, figuratively speaking, in one hour of work an Estonian can make seven table legs, while a German can make 100. Labor productivity is simply low. The countries that can bring technology into their economies quickly and intelligently will be among the winners. I do not think Estonia should be embarrassed about the state helping businesses invest in AI technologies, whether through guarantees or growth funds. Those wishing to invest in artificial intelligence could receive state-backed loan guarantees or other forms of support from funds. I consider this extremely important because that is where the next leap in economic growth will come from," Kallas said.

Responding to Helme, however, Kallas said the greatest problem of the century is instead climate change and the disasters it causes.

"These affect both our economy and our population, including migration. Moving away from fossil fuels and transitioning as quickly as possible to 100 percent renewable energy production is critically important. This is important not only in terms of fuels, but also for the natural environment and biodiversity," Kallas said.

Center Party

Center Party chair Mihhail Kõlvart said the tax system should not be used simply to collect money so that it can later be redistributed. The tax system should regulate the economy, but Kõlvart said no such system exists today.

"When it comes to the economy, the most important aspect is political decisions that do not regulate the economy but steer it — and in my view, that is not a focus at all today. If we compare ourselves with other countries, such as Latvia, Lithuania and Finland, over the past four years there has been an understanding that there need to be priority sectors in which the state invests, where it changes legislation and provides appropriate regulation," Kõlvart said.

Kõlvart also noted that every coalition agreement over the past 20 years has included a pledge to attract investment, but that there has never been any systematic effort to do so.

Opinion Festival 2026. Urmas Reinsalu, Mihhail Kõlvart and Lavly Perling. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"Lithuania shows that it can be done. In a short period of time, 300 financial companies have entered the market there and 8,000 jobs with top-level salaries have been created. All of this has a real impact on the economy, and this is not the only sector. It does not work by simply offering artificial intelligence to the economy and expecting it to solve everything. That requires a little intelligence of our own as well. It often involves risk, but you have to take responsibility and identify the sectors that can drive the economy. Lithuania has made those choices, whether in the chemical industry, financial sector, transport or logistics. The state invests, creates a system and then love follows," Kõlvart joked, adding that middle-aged or older men often talk philosophically about love and demographics, when in reality it is a mathematical problem.

"Over the past 35 years, there has not been a single year in which the fertility rate was 2.1. Four years ago it was 1.4; today it is 1.1 or 1.2. This is a mathematical projection, not some kind of rhetoric. If this continues, in 20 years we will have a demographic hole, but the consequences are already here. This must be our nation's top priority," Kõlvart said.

SDE

Social Democratic Party chair Lauri Läänemets said his party's most important priorities for the next electoral term are, above all, ensuring and improving people's well-being.

"That does not apply only to those who are struggling the most; we always talk about the average Estonian family. You could call it an uncompromising economic focus on investment. First and foremost, that means an uncompromising focus on investing in human capital. We know that regardless of which economic expert we listen to — and many people here today have also talked about this — an aging society needs to keep people in the labor market for as long as possible if it wants long-term economic growth," Läänemets said.

According to Läänemets, talk of taking money away from healthcare actually means taking people out of the labor market, as people become sicker and contribute less. He said this is why investment in healthcare and education is needed, including efforts to curb educational inequality and ensure that tuition-free higher education is accessible to everyone.

"Then there are investment incentives for businesses — not only financial support, but diplomatic assistance and all other forms of support as well. We continue to support investment and business activity without compromise. Ultimately, investment is needed in energy and in modern, accessible electricity generation, because this is currently one of the most significant factors holding back Estonia's economy," Läänemets said.

Läänemets also highlighted security, not only in the military sense, but also internal security and people's sense of security.

"When it comes to that sense of security, I would add something that has already been mentioned here and that I think a large part of today's audience also feels — environmental and climate issues. When we talk about having children, we cannot rely on benefits alone, because the issue is one of security. Can I be certain that a child I bring into the world here will have every opportunity in the future? We cannot deny problems in which climate change is already forcing European nuclear power plants to shut down and causing populations to move. Incidentally, I think Martin Helme is looking in the wrong direction when he looks to Africa in discussing the immigration problem. The first climate refugees will come from Southern Europe," Läänemets said.

According to Läänemets, for example, Germans and French people will move to Northern Europe because of the heat and buy up local real estate for large sums of money, which will in turn drive up property prices.

"All of these things are caused by climate change, and action is needed to ensure families — especially young families — have a sense of security and confidence in their future," Läänemets said.

Opinion Festival 2026 Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Omniva sends packages to different towns to manage high delivery volumes
World.content:
Omniva is redirecting packages dozens of kilometers away to manage the high number of parcels sent from third countries, saying it helps goods reach customers faster.

While the €3 customs duty added to goods ordered from China and other third countries, introduced in July, has significantly reduced the flood of parcels into Estonia, Omniva is still struggling to deliver all the packages.

When a parcel locker is full, parcel companies often redirect a shipment to another nearby locker. Unfortunately, in the name of faster service, Omniva decided this summer, for example, to send a parcel ordered to Tapa to Rakvere, 35 kilometers away, or instead of Treimani village to Häädemeeste, 20 kilometers away.

Lylian Peek, head of Omniva Estonia's distribution and postal network, said the situation has been caused by large volumes and faster service.

"Parcels are actually redirected relatively rarely. If we look at Omniva's volumes during the day, our sorting line sorts about 200,000 parcels a day, and 1 percent of those are redirected. To be more precise, 0.8 is the exact percentage that is redirected. Redirection is done based on the fact that our sorting process runs through an automated sorting line. When a parcel goes onto the sorting line, the sorting line takes as its basis everything that is in the address on the parcel. However, people always have the option of choosing their preferences, a first preference and a second preference, to specify which parcel locker is their favorite," Peek said.

This means around 1,600 Omniva customers a day do not receive their parcel at the location to which it was ordered. Other companies also redirect parcels.

However, DPD Estonia commercial director Janek Kivimurd said making sure the parcel is delivered to the chosen locker is a priority for the company.

"For Estonians, a parcel locker is one of the most preferred delivery options, because it is convenient to order a parcel there. It is open around the clock and is supposed to help save the customer's time in particular, and any additional journey or burden for the customer understandably causes dissatisfaction," he said.

"Sometimes it happens that a parcel locker unexpectedly fills up or has a technical fault. Around 1 percent of DPD's shipments are like this, and in order not to leave the parcel waiting, we deliver it to the nearest parcel locker, and for DPD the nearest parcel locker means up to one and a half kilometers away. There is certainly no situation where it is sent from one end of Tallinn to the other, or from one end of Narva to the other, or from Pärnu to the other end of Pärnu. That is certainly not our aim," Kivimurd said.

While the examples given at the beginning of the story concerned mainly smaller places where the parcel locker network is relatively sparse anyway, a customer can also be in for an unpleasant surprise in the middle of Tallinn.

"I run my business in Telliskivi and I have also had to collect my parcels, for example, from a parcel locker on Sõpruse puiestee. But the last time it was sent to Tallinn Kaubamaja, which was quite a big surprise because Omniva has post offices closer by both in Kristiine and at Arsenal keskus. It was strange having to go looking for it there," said Omniva customer Tarieli Lipartia from North Tallinn.

Lipartia added that he also asked Omniva for an explanation, but the company was unable to give any reason.

World.title: No mercy for corrupt officials as Al-Zaidi widens Iraq crackdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s anti-corruption effort has shown no signs of stopping, with arrests and investigations ranging from senior Oil Ministry officials to MPs, former provincial leaders, and other government figures since he assumed office.

One of the main early instances involved Adnan Al-Jumaili, the former deputy oil minister for refining affairs, whose imprisonment was a key development in the probe.

Statements gathered from Al-Jumaili assisted authorities in expanding their investigation into a larger network of politicians and officials accused of profiting from government contracts and state resources.

That probe culminated in a spectacular operation on June 28, when Iraqi security forces blocked off access to Baghdad’s highly defended Green Zone and conducted coordinated raids on political and government heavyweights.

Iraq’s national news agency first claimed 47 arrests, including 12 current parliamentarians, a former legislator, a former aide to former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, and a top Oil Ministry official.

According to sources inside Iraq’s anti-corruption authorities, there were 67 people held during the first phase of the “Dawn Crackdown”.

Ali Maarij, Iraq’s Deputy Oil Minister for distribution and another key player in the country’s energy industry, was among those held.

According to prosecutors, the larger investigation turned up claims of the misuse of public resources, government contracts, and commissions for personal or political gain.

Authorities also recovered a considerable quantity of assets related to the investigations. Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council said in July that 375 kg of gold had been confiscated as part of the al-Jumaili probe, with more cash and gold found in subsequent operations.

Instead of finishing with the first Green Zone attacks, the campaign lasted all of July.

Between July 20 and July 26, Iraqi police apprehended 31 persons in seven corruption cases, reflecting the government’s escalating enforcement campaign.

So far, August has delivered a slew of high-profile cases.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, was held as authorities investigated claims involving public finances, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court for a separate inquiry.

On Sunday, police detained Hashem al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company, on suspicion of corruption regarding a Ministry of Defense contract.

The specifics of the alleged infractions and the contract’s worth have not yet been released.

The financial impact of the crackdown is becoming significant.

The Eco Iraq Observatory said on Sunday that police had recovered around 482.6 billion Iraqi dinars ($371.6 million) in stolen assets, including cash and gold.

Taken together, the arrests convey an increasingly clear message from Al-Zaidi’s government: senior political ties, legislative standing, or positions inside major ministries should not exclude people from scrutiny.

However, arrests alone will not decide whether Iraq eventually succeeds in combating corruption.

Success will be predicated on transforming the present campaign into long-term institutional transformation via open government contracts, improved audits, digital financial systems, independent investigations, and tighter controls over public funds.

This is especially crucial as Iraq pursues tens of billions of dollars in foreign investment and works to strengthen economic ties with the United States, Europe, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and other Gulf nations.

Investors need to be confident that predictable rules govern contracts and public institutions rather than political interference.

The crackdown has also received backing from key international partners.

During a phone call with French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday, Macron reaffirmed France’s support for Iraq’s anti-corruption drive and economic reforms, as well as continued cooperation on counterterrorism and strengthening the capabilities of the Iraqi armed forces.

But the problem goes beyond financial corruption.

Al-Zaidi has committed to reinforce state power and bring armaments under government control, adding to the administration’s already arduous task of dealing with entrenched political and economic interests.

Iraq’s long-term goal must consequently be greater than capturing people.

Baghdad needs institutions strong enough to prevent corruption and foreign intervention from resurfacing under new political networks, whether sponsored by Iran or another external entity.

If Al-Zaidi can combine rigorous enforcement with due process and institutional change, the campaign might greatly boost trust in the Iraqi government.

Without such institutional improvements, even hundreds of arrests risk becoming a momentary crackdown rather than the long-term transformation Iraq requires.

World.title: Iraq opens its first IMAX cinema in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated its first IMAX theater at the Iraq Mall in Baghdad, introducing the premium large-screen movie format to the nation for the first time.

Sarwa Abdul Wahid, the Acting Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities, formally opened the new Iraqi Cinema branch in the mall, adding to Baghdad’s fast expanding entertainment and leisure sector.

According to IMAX’s official listing, the Iraq Mall site in Baghdad has an IMAX with Laser auditorium and stadium seating.

The launch allows Iraqi consumers to see important worldwide movies in IMAX without having to fly abroad, like Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey.

The film, starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Robert Pattinson, and Lupita Nyong’o, was the first feature film filmed exclusively on IMAX film cameras.

The Odyssey has also emerged as one of 2026’s greatest box office triumphs, earning more over $260 million globally in its first weekend.

Iraqi Cinema is now offering daily IMAX screenings of the film at its Iraq Mall location.

IMAX brings another worldwide entertainment option to Baghdad, as Iraq seeks additional investment in retail malls, restaurants, hotels, theaters, and other leisure developments, while also growing its domestic tourist and entertainment sectors.

World.title: Iraq arrests senior Trade Ministry official Hashem Al-Sudani
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi prosecutors detained Hashem Al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company (GAMCO), on Sunday for suspected embezzlement in a contract with the Ministry of Defense.

The contract’s specifics, including its value and the particular alleged infractions under investigation, have not been released. Al-Sudani’s arrest is part of Iraq’s growing anti-corruption effort, which targets prominent government officials, legislators, and business leaders.

The new arrest comes as Baghdad ramps up the “Dawn Crackdown,” an anti-corruption operation that began on June 28 by Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to probe big crimes involving public contracts and state finances.

The initiative has gained traction among senior and politically connected individuals.

Recently, police arrested former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court as part of a separate inquiry.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and reclaiming public monies, with authorities attempting to show that probes would extend to officials regardless of party or institutional affiliation.

Corruption has long been a major impediment to Iraq’s growth, depleting state resources, degrading public services, and deterring private and international investment.

The ongoing arrests imply Baghdad’s new effort is spreading to official institutions, but anyone arrested or interrogated has not been convicted and is still subject to due process.

World.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region.

The World Health Organization denounced a strike that destroyed a warehouse in Ukraine holding medical supplies.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, both countries are ramping up long-range strikes. The resulting civilian casualties led the United Nations to condemn both sides last week.

Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at Ukraine this week.

“More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he added.

The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, said Zelensky.

Twenty-three people were also wounded, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov, sharing images of a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.

Zelensky said eight people had also been wounded overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.

He condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region that wounded nine people, including four children.

– WHO condemns warehouse strike –

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro had been destroyed in strikes on Friday.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros in a post on X Sunday.

“Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!”

In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.

Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also wounded, he added.

Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, said Shuvaev.

A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.

On the front line, the Russian army said Sunday they had captured two small villages in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. The claim has not yet been independently verified.

One of them, Vasiutynske, is about 10 kilometres (six miles) from the city of Kramatorsk, a Ukrainian urban and logistical hub.

– Zelensky defends strikes –

Zelensky, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s responses to Russia’s attacks — including strikes on oil refineries, air-defence systems and radar stations — as “truly just responses”.

“The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said.

On Thursday, United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned both sides for their repeated attacks on civilian areas.

“Attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are a clear violation of international humanitarian law, and must stop immediately,” he said.

The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

World.title: Como sign England defender Chalobah from Chelsea
World.content:
Milan – Como have completed the signing of England centre-back Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for a reported fee of 30 million euros ($34.5 million), the Serie A club announced Sunday.

The 27-year-old has penned a five-year deal with Cesc Fabregas’s ambitious side, who will play in the Champions League for the first time this season.

“I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans,” said Chalobah, who made 151 appearances for Chelsea.

“I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together.”

Como pipped AC Milan and Juventus to Italy’s fourth and final Champions League place last season.

Scudetto holders Inter Milan had also been heavily linked with a move for Chalobah, before reportedly deciding the asking price was too high.

“Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club,” said Como coach Fabregas, a former Chelsea midfielder.

“He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Chalobah was part of the England squad which finished third at the World Cup last month, after receiving a late call-up as a replacement for the injured Tino Livramento.

He could make his Como debut when they visit Udinese in their Serie A opener on August 22.

World.title: Iraq steps up digital transformation of banking and customs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is speeding up preparations to digitize its financial and customs systems, with Finance Minister Falih Sari and Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasser Hussein considering tighter integration of electronic payments, customs processes, and government financial data.

The conference, which included members from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), aimed to accelerate electronic linkages between Iraq’s customs and payment systems.

Sari urged authorities to speed up implementation as part of measures to modernize financial management, streamline trade processes, and create a more efficient environment for companies and investors.

The talks also focused on increasing cooperation between fiscal and monetary agencies, including digital data interchange and upgrading Iraq’s banking infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability and meeting government financial responsibilities.

The revisions are part of Iraq’s larger transition from cash-heavy and paper-based institutions to a more integrated digital financial infrastructure.

Baghdad sees modernization of banking, payments, and customs as more crucial as the government strives to bring its financial system closer to international norms, increase transparency, and make it simpler for Iraqi and foreign enterprises to do business.

The drive also supports broader banking changes in Iraq, as the government seeks deeper connectivity with the international financial system and encourages private sector development.

World.title: PSG sign France full-back Digne from Villa
World.content:
Paris – Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne has joined Paris Saint-Germain on a three-year deal, the European champions announced Sunday.

The 33-year-old French international, who grew up in the Paris region, returns to PSG, where he played for two seasons between 2013 and 2015.

“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain,” Digne said in a statement on the Ligue 1 champions’ website.

“I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.

“I can’t wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team.”

After PSG, Digne spent time on loan in Serie A with Roma before signing for Spanish giants Barcelona, who were then coached by current PSG boss Luis Enrique.

He moved to the Premier League in 2018, firstly with Everton, then four years later joining Aston Villa.

At Villa Park, he won the Europa League under Unai Emery last season.

Capped 64 times by his country, Digne became France’s first-choice left-back over the course of the 2026 World Cup.

Digne is PSG’s second major signing of the summer transfer window after fellow French international Maghnes Akliouche arrived from Monaco.

He could make his debut for his new club against his former employers Aston Villa on Wednesday in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg.

However, long term it is likely his principal role will be to provide cover for PSG’s starting left-back, Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Former Iraq finance minister Taif Sami summoned in widening corruption probe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami has been officially summoned by a court and put on a judicial wanted list as authorities broaden a corruption probe that has reached high political and government officials, according to sources.

Sami is thought to be outside Iraq and has not been captured.

The alleged court action is part of an inquiry and does not prove misconduct or lead to a conviction.

The revelation comes as Iraq’s new administration steps up its anti-corruption effort, which has already resulted in the detention of important political personalities and bureaucrats.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, often known as Abu Mazen, was detained in Baghdad recently on suspicions of misusing public contract funds.

A close acquaintance was also arrested as part of the inquiry.

The new charges stem from a big operation in Baghdad’s highly protected Green Zone in late June, when Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service detained numerous officials as part of a larger corruption probe.

According to reports at the time, authorities were looking into claims involving government contracts and huge sums of public money.

Sami, the previous administration’s finance minister under former Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammad Shia Al-Sudani, was one of Iraq’s most significant economic leaders, responsible for handling the federal budget, government expenditures, and financial ties between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

The purported summons therefore implies a potentially major extension of the probe against individuals who formerly held top positions inside the Iraqi state.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and improving state institutions as part of its domestic agenda to boost public trust and reassure international investors.

With the arrest of Abu Mazen and the rumored legal proceedings against Sami, Iraq’s anti-corruption campaign is gaining traction among established political players.

However, the claims are still being examined, and individuals who are being arrested have the right to due process.

World.title: ED director Rahul Navin's tenure extended by a year
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rahul Navin has been granted a one-year extension as ED director as his two-year fixed tenure was due to end this month.

The tenure of Navin, a 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service (I-T) officer, as director of enforcement has been extended for a period of one year beyond "13.08.2026 i.e.

up to 13.08.2027, including extension in service beyond the date of his superannuation or until further orders," as per DoPT.

After three years as ED director, he could get two more extensions and serve till August 2029, all through the PM Modi government's tenure, with polls due in April-May 2029.

Navin's tenure as director (in-charge) began on September 15, 2023, and he was appointed as ED director on August 14, 2024, while his service retirement was due on July 31, 2027. He has set a roadmap for officers to complete probes within two years and ensure attached properties are auctioned and restituted to rightful claimants and fraud victims, including banks or individuals.

World.title: 7 of 25 high courts without CJs, collegium recommends names for just four
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At a time when seven of the country's 25 high courts are without regular chief justices, the Supreme Court collegium, headed by CJI Surya Kant, recommended the names of four HC judges to the government for their appointment as CJs of the Bombay, Calcutta, Patna, and Punjab and Haryana HCs.

The collegium recommended appointment of Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, a judge of Allahabad HC, as CJ of Bombay HC; Justice Ravindra V Ghuge, acting CJ of Bombay HC, as CJ of Calcutta HC; Justice V Kameshwar Rao, a judge of Delhi HC, as CJ of Patna HC; and acting CJ Punjab and Haryana HC Justice Ashwini Kumar Mishra - whose parent high court is Allahabad HC - as regular CJ of that HC.

The collegium is yet to decide on selecting judges for appointment as regular CJs to HCs of Rajasthan, J&K and Madhya Pradesh, which are manned by acting CJs - Justices Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, Sanjeev Kumar and Vivek Rusia, respectively.

The five-member collegium comprising CJI Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, BV Nagarathna, MM Sundresh and PS Narasimha met separately to recommend the government the transfer of Orissa HC judges Justices Manas Ranjan Pathan and Krushna Ram Mohapatra to Gujarat and Chhattisgarh high courts, respectively, for better administration of justice.

Orissa HC has a sanctioned strength of 33 judges but at present it has 17 judges, including the CJ.





When these two transfers take effect, the working strength will go down to 15, creating a vacancy of more than 50% of the posts of judges in the HC.

Orissa HC Collegium had suggested eight names - four advocates and four judicial officers - for the consideration and scrutiny by SC Collegium and consequent recommendations for appointment as judges of the HC.

Since the retirement of CJI Deepak Misra on Oct 2, 2018 - whose tenure towards the end was mired by the controversy of four-most senior SC judges led by Justice J Chelameswar holding an unprecedented presser against the sitting CJI - more than 50 judges have been appointed to SC but Orissa HC has not got representation in the last eight years despite successive CJIs advocating regional and state representation in the top court to make it a truly a national court.

World.title: Recent rain has little impact on national monsoon deficit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Good rains in the past one week over Delhi, Haryana and east Rajasthan helped offset the shortfall in these areas, but they did not reduce the overall country-wide monsoon deficit by much.

In this period, India's cumulative rainfall deficit was down by only one percentage point - from 12% on Aug 2 to 11% on Aug 9 - with many agrarian states, including Bihar, Jharkhand, UP, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh, continuing to witness deficient rainfall.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It rained in many parts at a time when sowing of Kharif crops had ended in almost 88% of the country's total sown area. As a result, the acreage deficit could be reduced by only 1% in the past one week, with paddy, the main kharif crop, still reporting 4% less acreage compared to the corresponding period last year.

Aug rains will improve water storage in reservoirs, which is a good augury for hydro-power potential being utilised and a back-up being in place for the next sowing season.

As of Sunday, as many as 12 states have reported high rain deficits of 20% and more.

IMD on Sunday, however, predicted a rise in rainfall activity over Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Bihar from Aug 13 onwards due to possible formation of a low-pressure area over the north Bay of Bengal and Bengal-Bangladesh coasts around Thursday. This may, to some extent, revive sowing of paddy and maize in Bihar and Jharkhand. Region-wise, all regions, except central India, have reported cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit despite 'normal' rains in July and in the first week of August, with east and northeast India recording the highest deficit of 25%, followed by 17% in south peninsular India and 11% in northwest India.

World.content:
INS Kalpeni sailed from Kochi on Saturday night to join the search operation and anchored one nautical mile off Neendakara on Sunday morning (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: A search operation involving the Indian Navy for three fishermen who went missing following separate boat mishaps off Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram coasts will continue on Monday, a defence spokesperson has said.The search operation for Gautam Krishna, John and Shijin -- who went missing in separate fishing boat mishaps at Neendakara (in Kollam), Vizhinjam and Muthalappozhi (in Thiruvananthapuram), respectively, on July 31 -- entered its 10th day on Sunday.On Sunday, Indian Navy divers joined the Coast Police, Coast Guard and Marine Enforcement Wing of the fisheries department to search for the three missing fishermen.INS Kalpeni sailed from Kochi on Saturday night to join the search operation and anchored one nautical mile off Neendakara on Sunday morning, the spokesperson said.The divers are using portable SONAR, which enhances their capability for underwater surveillance and diving operations, the spokesperson said. The Navy initially focused its search on Gautam Krishna, who went missing after his fishing boat capsized off the Neendakara coast. Later in the evening, INS Kalpeni moved to Muthalappozhi harbour to continue the search.

World.title: Police search 26 locations tied to banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Police searched 26 locations across Sopore in north Kashmir on Sunday in a coordinated crackdown on banned Jamaat-e-Islami J&K, seizing documents, literature and electronic devices as part of a probe into its alleged links to terrorist outfits and youth radicalisation.

The search targeted residential and other premises linked to Jamaat-e-Islami J&K members and activists. No arrest was reported till filing of this report. âThe operation was conducted in accordance with due legal procedure and prescribed protocols,â police said.

Police said the seized material was being examined to establish further linkages and activities connected with the proscribed organisation. The operation was part of efforts to dismantle networks linked to banned organisations, separatist activities and terrorist funding.

Distinct from Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, Jamaat-e-Islami J&K has a history tied to regional separatism and has long had a support base in Sopore. Union government first declared it an âunlawful associationâ in Feb 2019 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. In Feb 2024, the ban was extended for five years, with the government saying the organisation continued activities against Indiaâs security, integrity and sovereignty.

World.title: 'Ranchi police fully prepared': Jharkhand braces for students' protest march to Assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Sunday said it was prepared for the planned Assembly march by JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi, assuring protesters that they would not face action if the demonstration remained peaceful.

The assurance came hours after a second round of talks between student representatives and the state government, with the administration agreeing to consider some of their key demands but failing to resolve the issue of a CBI probe into the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination.

Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said adequate security arrangements were being made as a large number of students are expected to participate in Mondayâs âVidhan Sabha gheraoâ.

âPrecautionary force deployment will be carried out effectively; the Ranchi Police is fully prepared. There will be a large number of students. Instructions have been issued to all Ranchi Police personnel that if the protesters conduct themselves peacefully, no inconvenience will be caused to anyone,â Rana said.

âHowever, if anyone attempts to resort to violence, appropriate legal action will be taken against them,â he added.





Rana also clarified a controversy surrounding a viral video that appeared to show security personnel carrying a pellet gun.

âIf a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video - what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, coloured balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun,â he said.

The police officer said any pellet gun, if deployed, would be kept strictly for emergency situations.

Meanwhile, student leader Ravindra Paswan said the government had agreed to consider cancelling three examinations - the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, JPSC Backlog 2023 and JPSC Backlog 2025.

World.title: BSP president Mayawati opposes ‘creamy layer’ idea for SCs, STs, hits out at RSS
World.content:
The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday opposed the ‘creamy layer’ concept in reservations for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs), arguing that affirmative action was linked to their social transformation, economic emancipation and self-respect and criticised the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) for politicising the issue.

“Reservation for the SC, ST and OBC sections of the country’s ‘Bahujan Samaj’, especially for the SC, ST and OBC sections, is a crucial and extremely sensitive issue related to ‘social change and economic liberation’, i.e., their self-respect. For the SC and ST sections, who have been divided, oppressed and marginalised for centuries on the basis of caste, it becomes a crucial issue, especially when caste-based hatred, exploitation, torture, injustice and atrocities show no signs of abating. Therefore, talking about the creamy layer in this regard is not only inappropriate but also against the sacred objectives of the humanitarian Constitution of the revered Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar. However, no one should ignore this, but everyone must implement it with complete honesty and integrity in the interest of the country and the people,” wrote Ms. Mayawati, on X.

The BSP president questioned the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his recent remarks that reservation had been deliberately politicised, creating bitterness in society, and that beneficiaries should voluntarily give up the benefits. Ms. Mayawati described the RSS’s position a reflection of a “casteist mindset”, adding it might serve narrow political interests but would undermine constitutional objectives.

“While the RSS chief recently reiterated his statement that, ‘Reservation has been deliberately politicised, leading to bitterness in society, and that beneficiaries of reservation should voluntarily give up its benefits.’ In reality, this is a casteist mindset that may serve narrow political interests, but undermines constitutional objectives. Reservation is essentially meant to provide the constitutional and legal right to equality on humanitarian grounds to millions of exploited, oppressed, neglected, and despised people who have been victims of the caste system for centuries. This cannot be measured by economic progress at all. Because the sting of casteism continues to bite them in every aspect of life, and this trend continues at every level. Who knows this better than the RSS?,” she wrote on X, questioning RSS stand.

World.title: Protests on Nashik-Pune highway against revised Nashik-Pune railway route
World.content:
Thousands of protesters staged traffic blockades at several locations across Nashik - Pune highway on Sunday (August 9, 2026), urging the government to retain the proposed Nashik-Pune semi-high-speed railway route through Sangamner and Narayangaon instead of the new route via Shirdi.

MLC Satyajeet Tambe, nephew of Congress leader Balasaheb Thorat, was detained by police.

The initial proposal passed through Narayangaon station, 9 km away from the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescopes (GMRT) facility, which had raised concerns of potential interference. An alternative route via Shirdi has subsequently been proposed. According to a press release by Mr. Tambe, a major portion of the land acquisition process for the original Nashik-Pune route has already been completed, with over ₹500 crore disbursed.

This chakka Jam (traffic blockade) protest was staged across Chakan, Khed, Manchar, Narayangaon, Alephata, and Sangamner, as well as Gonde Phata on the Samruddhi Expressway and the Sinnar region.

Addressing protestors before his detention, Mr. Tambe said that “this is not a political stance of any single party” but represented a “mass public movement representing a demand that citizens have held for years”.

“The Nashik-Pune Railway must be executed along the exact original route on which it was proposed. We will not accept any attempt to alter the route under anyone’s pressure or for any reason whatsoever,” he said.

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis constituted a four-member committee, headed by former Atomic Energy Commission chairman Dr. Anil Kakodkar, to study the technical issues concerning the initially proposed Nashik-Pune railway line through Narayangaon. The committee comprises Dr. Kakodkar, along with the Divisional Commissioners of Nashik and Pune and Railway Board officials.

Mr. Tambe said the primary demand of the protestors is that the 60-day deadline granted to this committee must not be extended under any circumstances. “A clear decision must be reached within 60 days,” he said. He also said that the committee should hold public dialogues in every taluka to understand the sentiments of the people.

The GMRT facility, run by the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (NCRA-TIFR), is an array of 30 sensitive radio telescopes used for radio astronomical research using the metrewavelength range of the radio spectrum at Khodad.

World.title: Census 2027: Ladakh to lead Independent India’s first caste enumeration
World.content:
Ladakh, one of the country’s two youngest Union Territories, is set to lead the way in demonstrating how caste will be enumerated for the first time in Independent India. The second phase of the Census—the Population Enumeration (PE)—which starts on August 17 in Ladakh and other snow-bound areas, is likely to ask questions on 40 parameters and provide an open-ended column for caste enumeration.

Open-column methodology

As reported by The Hindu on July 6, the rehearsal, or the “pre-test” for the PE phase, was conducted from July 1 to 20 in 16 States and Union Territories, where respondents, other than Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes, recorded their castes in an “open column”, or the enumerator noted a resident’s caste as declared by them. The methodology is likely to be retained in the final form.

While the ongoing Census is India’s first digital Census, officials are making an exception for Ladakh by printing a sufficient number of paper schedules. The move takes into account the presence of large defence establishments in the region bordering China and Pakistan, whose locations cannot be geo-tagged because of security concerns. The digital Census mandatorily requires enumerators to geo-locate the structures on a mobile App. Respondents who self-enumerate on Census portal are also required to do the same.

Though the questionnaire or the schedule is yet to be notified by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI), preparations have begun in Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand to conduct Population Enumeration—the second phase of Census—from August 17-September 30, ahead of the rest of the country, where the exercise will be conducted in February 2027.

The Directorate of Census Operations, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, has concluded a three-day Master Trainers’ Training Programme for Census 2027 population enumeration, marking the next phase of field preparedness ahead of operations scheduled to begin on August 17 with the self-enumeration phase.

According to Chief Principal Census Officer Amit Sharma, the three-day programme provided comprehensive training on all aspects of Census 2027 population enumeration, covering census concepts, caste and demographic data collection, digital tools, self-enumeration, interviewing techniques and hands-on use of the mobile application.

Ladakh’s case is peculiar as it was not among the 16 States and UTs where a “pre-test” or rehearsal of the questions to be asked during the second phase, was held in July.

A senior government official said that, in the absence of the pre-test, the master-trainers are being trained based on tentative questions, around 40, which are likely to be notified this week.

“The broad contours have been conveyed to us. This time the questions are descriptive and will also include caste. The caste column will be open-ended, and enumerators will record the name of the caste as provided by the respondent,” said the official.

The official added that since the Census envisages counting all structures and buildings, enumerators are being told to exercise caution and record defence structures along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) as “special charges” on paper schedules.

The open-column methodology had resulted in the 2011 Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) returning over 46 lakh different “caste names”, largely owing to the differences in what people understand by caste. Significantly, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government has consistently maintained over the last decade that the 2011 SECC’s caste data was unreliable because of “errors” in data collection.

The total number of castes recorded during the 1931 Census was 4,147. The SECC was conducted as a survey and was outside the purview of the Census Act, 1948, and had no statutory backing. The data was never released by the government.

On August 3, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India notified in the gazette of India that “the conduct of Census of the population shall be undertaken in the Union territory of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, from 1st September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1 October, 2026 to 5th October, 2026”.

An option for self-enumeration will be available from August 17 to 31, before the start of house-to-house population enumeration, the notification said.

World.title: Government data point to uneven implementation of NRTS, with several large States lagging behind
World.content:
More than two-thirds of India’s registered nursing workforce are yet to be brought under the Nurses Registration and Tracking System (NRTS), despite the digital platform having been introduced over seven years ago to create a national registry and streamline registration-related services.

Government data tabled in the Lok Sabha last month show that only 14.24 lakh of the country’s 46.02 lakh registered nursing personnel—comprising Auxiliary Nurse Midwives (ANMs), Registered Nurses and Registered Midwives (RN & RM), and Lady Health Visitors (LHVs)—have been enrolled on the platform, leaving 31.78 lakh outside the national system.

The incomplete rollout has left many nurses waiting months for No Objection Certificates (NOCs) required to change their place of employment, while others seeking overseas employment have encountered delays in credential verification, affecting their career opportunities and livelihoods.

The State-wise figures point to stark disparities in implementation. Karnataka, which has more than 5.58 lakh registered nursing personnel, has enrolled only around 82,000 on the NRTS. Tamil Nadu, with over 4.76 lakh registered nurses and midwives, has enrolled just 57,000, while Andhra Pradesh has brought only 92,000 of its 4.52 lakh registered personnel onto the platform.

Kerala, another State with a sizeable nursing workforce, has enrolled about 1.5 lakh of its 4.2 lakh registered personnel.

The rollout, however, has been relatively successful in a few States. Bihar has enrolled 62,020 of its 62,591 registered nursing personnel on the NRTS, making it one of the best-performing States. Jharkhand has brought 24,640 or 90% of its 27,160 registered personnel under the system, while Odisha has enrolled 78,244 out of 98,194 registered personnel.

Uneven implementation

The figures suggest that implementation has been uneven nationally. Congress MP Anto Antony recently urged Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda to complete the enrolment of all registered nurses and issue National Unique Identity (NUID) cards within six months. In a recent letter to the Health Minister on July 30, the MP said the incomplete implementation of the NRTS had caused considerable hardship to nurses, particularly those seeking NOCs, inter-State registration and verification of credentials for overseas employment.

The NRTS was launched by the Indian Nursing Council (INC) in association with the National Informatics Centre (NIC) to maintain a live national register of nursing personnel and provide a common online platform for primary registration, renewal, reciprocal registration, higher qualification registration and other services.

In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on July 24, the Health Ministry said nurses are enrolled on the NRTS after verification by the respective State Nursing Councils, following which they are issued NUID cards and Nurse Passbooks. It said the INC had conducted meetings with State Nursing Council registrars, organised virtual training programmes, issued online user manuals and established a dedicated helpdesk and technical support system.

Meanwhile, nursing organisations argue that the uneven implementation has undermined the very purpose of creating a centralised digital registry. The Indian Professional Nurses Association (IPNA), which has been pursuing the issue, contends that several State Nursing Registration Councils continue to process registration, renewal and reciprocal registration through their own systems instead of routing them through the NRTS, resulting in delays and duplication.

PIL in Delhi High Court

In a public interest litigation filed before the Delhi High Court in 2025, the association alleged that nurses often had to rely on middlemen and agencies to secure registration-related documents. “The intermediaries exploit them financially. Moreover, often nurses do not receive their documents on time, which affects their ability to work,” the petition said.

In May 2025, the Delhi High Court directed the INC to consider the association’s representation and pass a reasoned order.

In response to IPNA’s representation, the INC said that the responsibility for registration of nurses under the existing legal framework rests with the respective State Nursing Registration Councils. On allegations of delays in registration, renewals and issuance of NOCs, it said it took such concerns seriously.

“While the NRTS is designed to address these issues by offering an online, transparent and time-bound mechanism, its effectiveness depends on consistent adoption and operational discipline by all State Councils,” the Council said.

Speaking to The Hindu, Siju Thomas, Joint Secretary of the IPNA, called the NRTS “the hope of nurses across the country” and alleged that its failure was the result of “mismanagement and lack of accountability” on the part of the INC. He claimed that despite the association pursuing legal action, the Council had failed to take concrete steps to make the portal fully functional.

Mr. Thomas said many nurses who remained outside the NRTS continued to face difficulties in obtaining NOCs and completing overseas verification. Describing it as “a grave injustice to the nurses who form the backbone of our healthcare system”, he urged the Health Ministry to intervene “on a war footing”.

World.title: BJD sees potential opportunity to regain political ground
World.content:
The resignation of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) last month, may have marked a notable development in national politics. In Odisha, however, it appears to have had implications for the political landscape, with the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), one of the country’s strongest regional parties, viewing it as a potential opportunity to regain political ground.

The party’s renewed confidence appears to stem from ground-level conversations that are critical of the pace of development under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government, which is now well past its “honeymoon period” in office. Moreover, the Mohan Charan Majhi Government is yet to clearly articulate a narrative around its governance model.

World.title: Why distance from ‘crime scene’ matters in criminal law
World.content:
A Prayagraj court’s summons to Independent MP Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav for his skit at the Parliament complex over the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple raises the question of territorial jurisdiction, which the judiciary is expected to strictly enforce to prevent “forum-shopping” by unscrupulous litigants as a means to harassment.

The court summons to the MP to reportedly appear before it on August 11 was based on a complaint filed before the court in Prayagraj. Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) begins with the words ‘A Magistrate having jurisdiction’, suggesting that the Magistrate should have territorial competence while taking cognisance of an offence on a complaint.

World.title: Houthi attacks kill 11 in Yemen, target Saudi refinery
World.content:
Strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on Sunday killed at least 11 people in the Yemeni port city of Mokha, after an earlier drone salvo targeted a Saudi oil refinery on the Red Sea coast.

A years-long truce in Yemen’s civil war between the Houthis and the Saudi Arabia-backed, internationally recognised government appeared to collapse last month as fighting between regional allies of the United States and Iran flared.

West Asia war LIVE updates - August 9, 2026

A medical source in Mokha said three civilians and eight military personnel had been killed in the Houthi attacks. Mokha is one of the main ports under Yemen’s internationally recognised government and has been renovated to handle shipping that avoids the Houthi-held port of Hodeida.

Two military sources with the government forces earlier confirmed at least eight troops had been killed in the strikes and more than 40 personnel were injured. They also confirmed that the Houthis attacked Mokha with several waves of missile and drone barrages

The Houthis’ military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted “Saudi enemy” troops and equipment in the area with missiles and drones.

Earlier, Mr. Saree said the Houthis had struck an oil facility on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast after the Gulf kingdom’s Energy Ministry said it had extinguished a fire at the Jazan site.

The Saudi Ministry said relevant authorities were completing procedures to deal ‌with the incident, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day ⁠in southwestern Saudi Arabia. No injuries were reported, it added.

Mr. Saree said that the attack on the facility operated by Saudi Arabia’s state-owned oil firm Aramco was launched in response to incursions by drones from the Gulf monarchy into northwest Yemen. The group had struck Aramco sites before in Jazan and Yanbu on the Red Sea.

The Houthis control vast swathes of Yemen, including the capital Sanaa and areas on the border with Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea provinces. They have announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, hitting Saudi tankers in the Red Sea and the kingdom’s oil infrastructure, in parallel with Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Haryana Power employees announce three-day strike from today after talks fail
World.content:
GURUGRAM

Haryana power employees and engineers on Sunday announced a three-day strike from 10 pm on August 10 after talks with the management of power distribution and transmission companies failed to yield any assurance on their key demands.

The talks between the Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Struggle Front -- both representing the power employees -- and the management were held at Shakti Bhawan under the chairpersonship of Additional Chief Secretary, Energy Department, Ashima Brar.

The Joint Struggle Front leaders said the management failed to provide any concrete assurance on issues including parallel distribution licences, the proposed formation of an Agri distribution company (DISCOM) and smart metering. They also said no assurance was given on the regularisation of contract workers, equal pay for equal work, risk allowance, removal of conditions imposed under the ex-gratia employment scheme and other pending demands.

According to the employees’ leaders, the management maintained that these issues fell under the purview of the State government and could only be considered by it.

The leaders further alleged that the management appeared to have backtracked from assurances given by the Power Minister during an earlier meeting with the Joint Struggle Front. With no agreement reached, the Front announced that it would go ahead with the three-day strike.

Electricity Employees Federation of India, national vice-president, Subhash Lamba, condemned the government’s and management’s approach.

Mr. Lamba said warned that any repressive or punitive action against striking employees would trigger strong nationwide protests.

The proposed creation of a separate Agri DISCOM for agricultural consumers from August 15 remains a major point of contention.

Elected Gram Panchayats from several districts -- Sonipat, Rohtak and Jhajjar -- have also opposed what they described as moves towards privatisation of the electricity sector and extended support to the employees’ strike.

Farmers have separately organised “mahapanchayats” and announced their opposition to the proposed Agri DISCOM, smart metering and parallel distribution licences.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact open to any other country in region, 'purely defensive': DPM Dar
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister said on Sunday that the defence pact signed between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

He also clarified that the agreement was “purely defensive” in nature.

The indication that an expansion of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi city on Friday, was possible came a day after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact.

The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Dar further elaborated on the pact, which he referred to as the Makkah Accord, in a post on X.

“The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement […] reflects the depth of the brotherly relations between the leadership and peoples of the three countries.

“The Makkah Accord is the culmination of years of discussions and coordination, with a common desire to strengthen strategic cooperation in addressing multifarious peace and security challenges and advancing regional peace, stability and prosperity,” he said.

He clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations.

Reiterating that any external armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all under the pact, he said it was consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

Moreover, he said, the accord was “purely defensive” in nature.

“It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.”

“The Makkah Accord remains open to any country in the region willing to uphold its fundamental principles and resolve differences through mutual respect, cooperation and peaceful means,” he said, adding that the pact was consistent with the fundamental pillars of Islamabad’s foreign policy.

“Pakistan looks forward to continuing to work closely with all brotherly countries in the region towards lasting peace and stability. We remain committed to advancing the cause of peaceful resolution of all conflicts and building a more secure, stable and prosperous future for our peoples,” he concluded.

Later in the day, Dar and Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand exchanged views on the regional situation, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Dar informed Anand of the “essence of the agreement and the joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

Egypt likely to join: Turkish FM

Earlier, on Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan also said he believed Egypt could join the pact once several technical issues were resolved.

“Egypt is already our natural partner on all issues. I believe that at the next stage, Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members. There are a few technical issues. Once these are implemented, there is no reason for Egypt not to be part of it,” he told Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu news agency.

Other countries had expressed interest in joining the agreement, but the founding members had debated how the expansion should be handled, he further stated.

Some countries that wanted to join asked not to be named, he said, adding that the preferred model was for Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to remain the three core founding countries, responsible for establishing the principles, standards and long-term structure of the alliance, while other countries could join with the approval of the core members.

“Under our president’s vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow,” Fidan said.

Fidan also said the initiative was broader than the traditional definition of the Middle East because of Pakistan’s participation.

Pakistan’s geographical position meant the initiative went beyond the conventional definition of the Middle East and represented a broader regional perspective.

‘Same as Nato’s Article 5’

Fidan further elaborated on this, saying the pact was technically the same as Nato’s Article 5 mutual defence agreement.

Article 5 of the North Atlantic alliance specifies that an attack on one ​of its members is an attack on all of them. It obliges allies to take action they deem necessary to assist the country under attack, including potentially the use of military force.

While the Makkah defence pact stipulates the same, Fidan explained that its text contained general commitments whose practical implementation would depend on discussions and decisions by relevant bodies.

A country would need to make a request for assistance and would determine the type of support it needs, he said, adding that the requests could be of different kinds, ranging from intelligence and logistics to ammunition or, if necessary, military units, depending on the scale of the threat.

The signatories, he said, would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of ​support they would ask for in the event of an attack, but that no country would be considered a ​threat as long as a member state is not attacked.

Fidan also said that the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support the three signatories’ security.

He further told Anadolu that discussions on the initiative began before the current war environment, when there was no US-Israel war on Iran and other regional countries had also been involved in the talks leading to the agreement.

Fidan said its signatories were countries that did not have expansionist policies. “They are countries concerned with their own borders, their own problems and their development, and, if possible, they want to contribute positively to their environment through good relations and good neighbourliness.“

The three countries, he said, had different styles and capacities, but when brought together, they naturally formed a defence-oriented organisation rather than an offensive one.

“It is not an approach of going on the offensive and saying, ‘Let’s do this or that together.’ Therefore, unless it is attacked by a country, whether from inside or outside the region, this alliance cannot have any dispute with any country. But, of course, the power composition we have put forward will make a constructive contribution to regional stability,” he said.

He termed the pact the “most important step” toward bringing lasting stability to this region.

How will the alliance function?

According to Fidan, the pact would be operational under a political and military committee comprising foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of general staff, similar to Nato structures.

The committee would translate the vision set by the leaders into decisions and carry out related work, while a secretariat would be established to implement those decisions, he explained.

“At the first committee meeting, ministers would likely present proposals to the leaders on the establishment, structure and functioning of the secretariat, as well as its initial tasks,” he said, adding that the pact would cover a broad range of military issues, including interoperability, or the ability of countries with different military structures to operate together. Other areas would include joint training, mutual support, logistics, threat assessments, intelligence sharing and, most importantly, defence industry cooperation.

He said the committee would meet at certain intervals during the year and that a permanent secretariat would be established in Saudi Arabia. The structure, functioning and additional units of the secretariat would be determined in discussions among the members.

Fidan added that joint exercises and training would be necessary to establish the ability of the countries to operate together.

“Because after a while you will see that when you find yourselves in a common combat scenario, how your weapons systems and communications systems will communicate with one another and how they will be compatible are important issues. These are the things that will be done after the secretariat is established,” he said.

He said standards would need to be developed and that analyses and assessments would also be carried out.

‘Support in the Muslim world and the West’

Fidan said the defence agreement had received strong support from countries in the Muslim world, including those that were not members but were nevertheless very pleased with the agreement.

He said there were also supporters in the West who understood the substance of the initiative.

“Especially in the Islamic world, there are many who strongly support this issue. There are also supporters in the West, among those who understand the essence of the matter. The way for the Middle East to cease being a place that produces problems for humanity and the international community and instead become a place that creates added value with everything it possesses is through implementing constructive alliances of this kind,” Fidan said.

Fidan said the leadership of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had created significant regional and global expectations and that officials now had the responsibility to fill those expectations professionally.

“Our responsibility, in the positions we hold, is to recognise that the political will put forward by the leadership of the three countries has created a very significant regional and global expectation. We need to fill that expectation very professionally, move forward step by step and make it work. We have begun doing this, and God willing, we will continue,” he said.

The signing of the accord comes at a time of heightened regional tensions, with Pakistan seeking to balance ties with Middle Eastern and Western partners.

Analysts say many in the region view the development as a step toward Gulf states taking greater responsibility for their own security.

Israel’s increasingly aggressive military posture in recent years has also emerged as an important factor shaping how Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye perceive the regional security environment, they added.

For decades, Saudi Arabia has relied heavily on its strategic relationship with the United States for its security. Experts note the new agreement does not replace Washington, but it does create an additional security pillar.

“The regional states are not seeking to sever ties with Washington, but neither do they want to entrust their security exclusively to American guarantees,” one analyst said.

Additional input from Syed Irfan Raza

World.title: Sindh govt decides judicial commission to probe Mir Raza Ali murder case
World.content:
KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to seek a judicial probe into the killing of 25-year-old businessman Mir Raza Ali, Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Sunday.

Ali’s body was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar last month, a day after he went missing on July 28. While his family is convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide.

However, after injury details from a second postmortem ruled out the possibility of suicide, a murder charge was added to the case on Sunday.

“A decision has been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry into the murder case of Mir Raza Ali Khan,” the Sindh home minister said in a statement issued by his office.

According to the statement, Lanjar, along with Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, visited Ali’s residence to meet his parents. They assured the family that they would be provided complete justice.

Lanjar said the judicial commission would be constituted under the leadership of a Sindh High Court judge on the recommendation of the Sindh chief minister.

During the meeting, Lanjar briefed Ali’s parents in detail about the progress of the case and the investigation, the statement said.

“The investigation team will maintain full contact and cooperation with the deceased’s parents,” the minister was quoted as saying. “A transparent and impartial investigation into the case will be ensured.”

He affirmed that all requirements of justice would be fulfilled and no leniency would be shown to anyone responsible.

Meanwhile, the Karachi mayor noted that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah chaired a four-hour-long meeting during which “all aspects of the incident and the investigation were reviewed in detail”.

The decision of a judicial inquiry comes after Faryal Talpur, the chairperson of Sindh Assembly’s Standing Committee on Home, recommended that CM Murad constitute a judicial commission for a “transparent, impartial and comprehensive investigation” into the case.

Taking notice of Ali’s murder, she said the proposed commission should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

“Legal and disciplinary action should be taken without discrimination against those found responsible in light of the commission’s findings,” Talpur added.
