World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Odesa in summer 2026: Life between sea and war. VIDEO
World.content:
Beaches, bomb-damaged homes and explosions in broad daylight. In the summer of 2026, Odesa is caught between its traditional seaside resort atmosphere and the constant threat of Russian attacks. While some people relax by the sea and stroll through the city centre, others sift through the rubble left by the latest strike.

JAMnews visited Odesa to show what life in the city looks like today.

Odesa and the surrounding region remain frequent targets of Russian strikes. Residential neighbourhoods, critical infrastructure and port facilities have all come under attack.

Russia has carried out combined attacks using drones and missiles, seeking to overwhelm Ukraine‘s air defence systems.

The impact of these attacks is visible across the city. Residential buildings have been damaged, windows blown out and flats destroyed. Strikes have also hit Odesa’s historic centre, including heritage buildings and universities.

Ports in Odesa Region, along with the logistics hubs and warehouses that support them, are also regularly targeted. Attacks on port infrastructure have disrupted Ukraine’s transport network and Black Sea export routes.

The strikes often occur in broad daylight, when the streets are busy, cafés and shops are open, and beaches are filled with residents and visitors. At any moment, the familiar sounds of the city can be interrupted by explosions, air defence fire or the buzz of attack drones.

On several occasions, missiles have been intercepted directly over the coastline while beaches were crowded with people.

Today, it is possible to spend the day at the beach and the night in a bomb shelter.

World.title: “Russia’s annexation of Georgia’s regions would not go unanswered” – embassies on 18th anniversary of August war
World.content:
France, Germany, Italy, Britain: Russia’s annexation of Georgia

France, Germany, Italy and the UK issued a joint statement marking the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russo-Georgian war, reaffirming their support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

18 years after the Russian aggression, we reaffirm our full support to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia within its internationally recognized borders. We welcome Republic of Naoero’s decision to withdraw its recognition of the so-called independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

We urge states that have established diplomatic relations with these entities to follow this example,” the statement said.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia).

The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

France, Germany, Italy and the UK condemned Russia’s military presence in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

ЭWe reiterate our condemnation of Russia’s ongoing military presence in the occupied breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia in violation of international law as well as Russia’s obligations under the six-point agreement of 12 August 2008.

Russia’s ongoing militarization of Georgia’s occupied territories poses a serious threat to the security of Georgia and to regional and European stability,” France, Germany, Italy and the UK said.

The statement also referred to rulings by the European Court of Human Rights.

In October 2025, the court found Russia responsible for a number of violations in the occupied regions, including the use of excessive force, ill-treatment, unlawful detention and restrictions on movement between Georgian-controlled territory and areas occupied by Russia.

“We urge Russia to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights relating to this situation and to fully fulfil the commitments it made on August 12 and September 8, 2008,” the statement said.

The four countries also expressed concern over recent developments in South Ossetia.

They said the so-called “Agreement on Deepening Alliance and Cooperation,” signed by Moscow and the de facto authorities in South Ossetia on May 9, 2026, further violates Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and is incompatible with international law.

“This is a clear violation of international law. This document, as well as the appointment of a Russian citizen to head the region raise concerns on a possible full-fledged annexation of the region, which would not go unanswered,” the statement said.

Support for the Geneva International Discussions, co-chaired by the EU, OSCE and UN, was reaffirmed.

They said it is the only format that allows the parties to work towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

The statement also stressed the importance of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia and said its work would continue to be supported in the future.

News in Georgia

World.title: Carlton fans chant 'we want Fraser', talks on coaching future imminent
World.content:
Carlton fans are chanting Josh Fraser's name and a similar endorsement from the club's hierarchy for the Blues' interim coach to take the reins full time could follow as soon as this week.

Fraser has mounted an irrepressible case to take on the vacant head coach role, having delivered 10 wins and just two losses since stepping up when Michael Voss was sacked in mid-May, with the Blues at 1-8.

Fraser, who earned "we want Fraser" chants from Carlton fans after Sunday night's 44-point win, is yet to officially throw his hat in the ring — but that conversation is imminent.

Loading...

"At some stage this week there'll be an opportunity to have some conversations with the club," Fraser said.

"It'll be sometime this week."

Half-back Adam Cerra joked whether the interim boss should take the reins was the hardest question at the club at the moment.

"Obviously the club's got their processes. We've got full faith in that process and their decision and we'll support whatever they pick. 'Frase' has been great," he said.

"The boys obviously love playing with him. We'll leave that to the club."

Cerra put Carlton's turnaround down to a combination of Fraser's influence and how the playing group lifted him — with experienced players leading from the front and young players expressing themselves.

"Frase has probably allowed a bit of freedom for us to do that, a bit of simplicity in the way we're trying to play," Cerra said.

"It hasn't set too many boundaries on us. It's more trying to explore what our best football looks like and building that week to week.

"These last couple of weeks we've been getting more confidence in our process and our trust and executing."

Fraser was asked whether part of his thinking in holding off on nominating was around managing if he missed out on the job while preparing the team for a potential wildcard match.

Blues plant one foot in the AFL finals as Saints lose star to hamstring Carlton plants one foot in the AFL finals series with a statement victory over the Saints at Docklands.

"It's a fair question, but no, I haven't thought too deeply about that," the 43-year-old said.

"I've just tried to stay as narrow as I can and it's been challenging with a lot of the questioning and different things, but I still feel such a responsibility to this role as interim coach.

"That's what I needed to and have focused all of my energy on — because I would be doing a disservice, not only to our players, but our staff and everyone, if I started to stray away from that.

"Clearly I've had to think through some things, but that hasn't occupied a lot of my thinking and all the hypotheticals haven't either. Most of my energy has been focused on this playing group and footy club."

The Blues sit eight points clear in 10th with games against the Western Bulldogs and Fremantle to come.

"[It's] not about daring to dream, I think the thing that's taking us forward is we are just attaching ourselves to the work that we need to do," Fraser said.

AAP

World.title: Gold hunters fear World Heritage bid could undermine prospecting
World.content:
As Victoria continues to build its case for UNESCO World Heritage status for selected goldfields sites, modern-day prospectors are concerned a successful bid could undermine the very activity that sparked it.

The state's gold rush continues to inspire more than 115,000 prospectors who hold a Victorian miner's right, a permit dating back to the 1850s.

Loading...

But Prospectors and Miners Association of Victoria (PMAV) executive president Jason Cornish said he had been fielding two-hour phone calls from gold hunters anxious about the implications of World Heritage status.

A UNESCO listing has no bearing on local laws, but Mr Cornish said apprehensions it could open the door to further land use restrictions remained widespread.

"Prospectors and miners have always had a distrust of government and over-regulation and bureaucracy," he said.

" We're the descendants of the Eureka Stockade … That's just the way we are, we're pretty much rebels. "

Jason Cornish says much of the criticism on social media is misinformed. (Supplied: Jason Cornish)

An unfolding process

The World Heritage bid for the Victorian goldfields proposes listing a group of selected sites of significance across regional Victoria, such as Castlemaine, Walhalla, and the Great Nuggets landscape.

The proposal is currently on Australia's tentative list, and is spearheaded by 15 local councils, the state government and Heritage Victoria.

Next month, the team will submit its preliminary assessment making the case for "outstanding universal value" to the federal government.

Each year, the federal government can choose just one proposal from its tentative list to put forward to UNESCO.

An Australian government spokesperson said progress was being made on the nomination.

"The Australian government has been working closely with the Victorian government on the Victorian goldfields World Heritage nomination," the spokesperson said.

"The next step in the process is to submit a preliminary assessment request to UNESCO to seek advice on the likelihood of the property to contain outstanding universal value."

Selected Victorian goldfields sites for potential World Heritage listing submitted to Australia's tentative list. (Supplied: Heritage Victoria)

Mr Cornish said open dialogue with the World Heritage bid team had overcome his initial concerns, but some questions remained unanswered.

He said his "optimistic" views were not shared by a significant number of prospectors vehemently opposed to the project.

"There's a lot of people out there that are concerned [about] what's going to happen in the future if the bid is successful, but that's the future," he said.

"If something happens down the track and they actually do start blocking access, well that's just a fight for another day … but so far I haven't seen that."

Chris Bogusis says he is concerned land use is gradually being more restricted. (Supplied: Chris Bogusis)

Digging into history

Wodonga-based prospector Chris Bogusis is one of the PMAV members concerned that platforming the story of the gold rush could have results contrary to its spirit.

"I think World Heritage can be a fantastic thing to have in place for certain areas that certainly show historic significance," he said.

" I worry though that some of these grounds will get locked up to the point where we're not able to utilise them in the same way that they've been utilised since the gold rush. "

He said he felt a strong connection to Victoria's gold rush miners who left traces in historic tunnels.

The Malmsbury viaduct is one of the sites under investigation for World Heritage status. (Supplied: Barry Gamble)

"The scars of their picks and their chisels are still in the walls," he said.

"Then you'll hit a point where modern mining picked up with pneumatic drills and more effective explosives … and you can literally see the boundary line of where the two different workings meet, and they change."

Why Victoria?

Barry Gamble, a strategic adviser to the heritage bid, said the preservation of early mining activity was part of what made Victoria's gold rush stand out above its North American equivalents.

"The fact that … no large corporations were allowed to come in subsequently to mass mine the land through large-scale dredging, large-scale hydraulic mining left the signature of the individual prospectors in their tens of thousands," he said.

A deep lead gold mine in Bright, 1880. (Supplied: State Library Victoria)

Mr Gamble has a 100 per cent success rate on 22 UNESCO World Heritage nominations around the world, including his native mining landscape of Cornwall-West Devon.

He said western Victoria's distinctive volcanic landscape also made the local gold rush unique.

"The lava flows that flowed over the landscape that produced the fertile farmland … also covered ancient rivers of gold," he said.

"For about another 20 years, these ancient lava flows concealed a further hidden treasure which then perpetuated that gold rush for another … two decades."

Barry Gamble can trace seven ancestors to Victoria's gold rush. (Supplied: City of Ballarat)

He said he was confident the Victorian goldfields would get over the line with UNESCO.

"I've looked at gold rush landscapes across the world in the last 20 years and for me, this is the best, most extensive and most coherent landscape of the lot," he said.

"This is a winning horse."

'Zero downside'

Former Victorian premier John Brumby has been pushing for World Heritage status for the goldfields since he was a federal MP in the 1980s.

He said the process for World Heritage had "no impact whatsoever" on land use.

John Brumby (right) is co-patron of the World Heritage bid alongside Dennis Napthine. (ABC Ballarat: Lexie Jeuniewic)

"Those nominations would have no legal status within the Australian, Victorian or relevant local government laws," he said.

"It won't impact any provisions in existing planning schemes… and importantly, there's no impact on the exercise of legal rights under a miner's right."

Mr Brumby said prospectors were an important stakeholder in the process.

"The nomination itself highlights the important historic role of the miner's right and that actually it's a reason why World Heritage inscription is justified," he said.

"It demonstrates the path to democracy and the recognition of the role that diggers played."

The World Heritage bid proposes listing about 10 sites of significance across regional Victoria. (Supplied: Barry Gamble)

Mr Brumby is co-patron of the World Heritage bid alongside former Liberal premier Dennis Napthine.

He said it was a "much more sophisticated proposal" than what was launched in the 1980s, and had brought together an unlikely coalition.

"[It's] almost unprecedented to get 15 councils all united and all supporting this," he said.

" There is absolutely zero downside — it's all upside. "

The earliest the Victorian goldfields could gain World Heritage status is 2030.

If successful, a World Heritage management plan would then be developed for the goldfields.

A Department of Transport and Planning spokesperson said the World Heritage bid would not affect prospectors.

"The proposed World Heritage listing of the Victorian goldfields will not affect prospecting activities," the spokesperson said.

"As the nomination progresses, we'll continue working with councils and communities to plan for the future, so these places can welcome more visitors while protecting what makes them unique."

World.title: Aviation bosses summoned, airport workers stood down after Sydney near-miss
World.content:
Emergency meetings will be held in Canberra as an investigation gets underway into a near-miss involving two passenger planes at Sydney Airport following days of flight disruptions and delays.

Two airport workers were stood down pending the outcome of an official investigation into the near collision, which left a Jetstar crew member injured on Sunday.

Jetstar flight JQ402 was preparing to take off for the Gold Coast and was taxiing to the runway when it was forced to slam on the brakes.

Its flight crew noticed a Qatar Airways plane that was being towed along the tarmac by an aircraft tug and in close proximity.

Both aircraft stopped abruptly, avoiding crashing by mere metres.

Two airport workers involved in Sunday's near-miss have since been stood down. (Supplied)

Describing it as "extremely concerning", federal Transport Minister Catherine King vowed any "systemic issues" to come out of the investigation by the aviation safety watchdog would be addressed.

She also said Airservices Australia "needs to do better" to manage disruptions at the airport, which has grappled with a shortage of air traffic controllers.

Thousands of passengers were affected by lengthy delays to flights over recent days, with some missing flight connections as a result.

"They caused significant challenges to passengers, staff and airlines

"My office has asked for an explanation, and for Airservices to outline a pathway to improve the delivery of its services," Ms King said.

It was understood the organisation's CEO Rob Sharp will meet with her this morning in Canberra.

Airservices Australia, the government-owned body responsible for safely and efficiently managing air traffic, on Sunday said in a statement that Air Traffic Flow Management measures had been put in place following the incident, including departure spacing "to safely manage projected airborne and departure demands".

"Airservices is reviewing the incident and will assist with any safety investigation," it said

'A very stressful environment'

Australian Transport Safety Bureau's Chief Commissioner Angus Mitchell is heading the investigation into yesterday's near collision.

A Jetstar spokesperson said the aircraft had been following air traffic control instructions before its pilots brought to plane to a sudden stop. (ABC News: Peter Garnish)

He said it was too early to confirm the cause with investigators examining all possibilities, including one line of inquiry that the tug pulling the aircraft did not follow Air Traffic Control instructions.

"Now exactly why they came so close is I guess really what we're trying to understand at the moment so we're gathering the evidence we need to make that determination," he said.

"So that will be from both the pilots on board the Jetstar aircraft, those that were controlling the Qatar plane, as well as those in the coordination of air traffic control, to understand what potentially broke down in the coordination or communication.

" Most importantly what we need to do to strengthen the system, so we don't get this happening again at Sydney airport, or any other airport in Australia. "

A shortage air traffic controllers at Sydney Airport is affecting services, the Civil Air boss says. (ABC News)

It was the second near-miss at the airport in recent weeks, with two Qantas planes narrowly avoiding crashing late last month.

Commissioner Mitchell said in both instances the pilots were able to act quickly to avoid a collision.

He said the probe would be wide-ranging and also scrutinise whether the understaffing issues within the airport's air traffic control fleet had any role to play.

Commissioner Mitchell says the investigation will look into whether any individual errors were made. (Supplied: ATSB)

Commissioner Mitchell said the investigation needed to uncover whether systemic changes were needed to ensure that if individual errors are made, that there are other mechanisms in place to avoid serious problems.

'There aren't enough controllers'

The government confirmed the air traffic control ground worker and the tug operator involved in yesterday's near collision have both been stood down, pending the outcome of the investigation.

A Jetstar spokesperson said the aircraft had been following air traffic control instructions during the incident and its captain acted "quickly and decisively".

The crew member sustained a minor injury after falling when the pilot hit the brakes.

The boss of the union representing air traffic controllers declined to publicly comment what he believed was the cause of the two near collisions, saying it was "premature" while investigations were underway.

Mr Nugent said resourcing for air traffic controllers has been a long-running issue. (Supplied)

But Civil Air president Scott Nugent, who is a trained air traffic controller, said staffing shortages took a heavy toll on those working on the frontline.

"What I can say is that air traffic controllers in Australia are working very hard, and for a long time they have not necessarily had the resources they need to do their jobs properly," he told the ABC.

"There aren't enough controllers in Australia."

He said the air traffic control system at Sydney Airport relies on workers doing excessive overtime, with some potentially doing more than 20 extra hours a week.

"We've seen in the past few days what happened when you don't have enough air traffic controllers, the impact on industry," he said.

"Civil Air has been saying to Airservices over the past four or five years you don't have enough air traffic controllers in Sydney airport tower.

"No matter why they occurred, people no longer want to work the overtime because they're very stressed and upset, and the whole system is propped up on overtime."

Mr Nugent said he would also be meeting with Mr Sharp later today to discuss his concerns in the wake of the weekend disruption.

World.title: How Elliot won Race Around the World in 'opportunity of a lifetime'
World.content:
Elliot Constable was wandering through a park in Chisinau, Moldova, when he met Tatiana.

A Race Around the World contestant tasked with making short documentaries on tight deadlines, he was looking for a story.

He had only 10 days to shoot and edit a film, but he spent two of those just listening to her.

Tatiana had fled Ukraine when Russia attacked her home in 2022, but when she met Constable, she was trying to get back into the war-torn country for cancer treatment.

Since then, Constable has been crowned the winner of ABC iview's Race Around the World, a reboot of the 1990s classic TV competition.

Now back home in Sydney, Constable tells me Tatiana's back in Kyiv, and their families remain in touch.

Loading...

The filmmaker credits his success on the show to his character-driven approach.

"It's those people that have stories where you think, 'Where are they going to end up?' that, I think, really hit home," Constable says.

When I catch him on the phone the day after filming the finale (and the subsequent celebrations), he hasn't even had the chance to return to his apartment yet.

Constable's journey took him across South Africa, Norway, Azerbaijan, the Bahamas and eventually Brazil. He's battling the whirr of jet lag as he admits his success is yet to sink in.

In week four, Elliot travelled to Svalbard, Norway, where he was guided through polar bear territory in the Arctic mountains. (ABC iview/Race Around The World: Elliot Constable)

Winning means Constable receives funding to produce his own project produced by the ABC.

Elliot's race around the world: Moldova

South Africa

California, USA

Norway

Japan

Nepal

Azerbaijan

The Bahamas

Monaco

Brazil

"I thought I'd won already because I was on the show, and I think that's the consensus with all the other racers. It's an opportunity of a lifetime; we all won, right?" he says.

"But the fact that I now have an opportunity to tell another story or maybe go back and do something a bit bigger… maybe it is going back to Moldova, maybe it's going back to Brazil, I don't know, maybe it's doing something in Australia."

It was Brazil, the destination he was allowed to select for the show's finale, where he entered the favelas in Rio de Janeiro and met a father determined to shield his son from a future of crime.

"I didn't want to do a story about the gangs, but I wanted the film to be more about hope and this boy who is going to have a challenging decision to make one day," he says.

"Do you take an honest path? Often in places like Brazil in the favelas, it's going to mean a tough life.

"Or you take this path that is more of the gang route. You see them walking around with gold chains and weapons; they look like action stars, and they're feared and respected, and young boys see that and think, 'I want that life.'"

Loading...

Constable's main hope is that people watch his films and care for the people and their complex situations.

This sentiment is shared by the competition's People's Choice Award winner, Jayden O'Neill, who took out the top spot in the ABC's audience poll.

"The reason you make content is because you want the audience to take it in," O'Neill says.

Jayden spent time in India, Jordan, Timor-Leste and the Philippines. (ABC iview/Race Around The World: Jayden O'Neill)

On the show, the six contestants were judged each week by a panel of industry experts.

"The judging panel is only made up of three people, and they'll all have their own views," he says.

"If you can get the popular vote, I think it's really cool that it resonates with so many people, and that's what we're here for."

Jayden's favourite films to make were the same ones the audience loved, including his week one entry from the Philippines, which detailed fishers using illegal methods to feed their families.

"The connection I made with the people there is what made the film what it was, and you don't have that connection with every single film," O'Neill says.

'A completely solo venture'

If you're wondering whether the six contestants were really showing up to a new country every 10 days and making a film on their own, host Zan Rowe confirms as much.

"They have to find the story, shoot it, edit it, record the sound and deliver it. It's all a completely solo venture," she says.

Zan Rowe says the show took a new approach. (ABC)

The show is a reboot of the original series broadcast in 1997 and 1998, but with all of the technological advancements, Rowe says it's barely recognisable.

"It is basically launching a new show, and the beauty of that is you can try new things," she says.

"In week three we noticed [the contestants] were doing these character pieces that were a bit slow and reflective; we needed to get them more in the field to see them immerse themselves in the country. So we threw them a challenge in that regard and really shook it up."

Destinations were also changed at the last minute.

"Things were changed, both for safety reasons, geopolitical reasons, but also just to see variety, how the filmmakers were reacting to certain places, what sort of ways the producers could challenge them or take them somewhere where they thought they'd probably do something interesting," Rowe says.

In week five, all of the contestants were sent to Japan. (ABC iview/Race Around The World)

In the original series, there was no feedback on the road and no way for the contestants to communicate with each other.

Constable says having access to feedback early on helped him refine his approach.

"Ultimately, they're looking for a narrative that makes sense. And I think I really took on the feedback. I struggled at the start with having too much going on," he says.

"You don't have the luxury of being able to step away from it or have a day off from it, which I think always helps in the real world."

In the Bahamas, Elliot prepared a meal with a local family's catch of the day. (ABC iview/Race Around The World: Elliot Constable)

For Constable, the clock was always the biggest challenge.

"You're constantly up against it with time; you turn up to a country, and you don't know what you're doing. Things fall through, and ideas don't come together, and you sometimes have to pivot," he says.

Race Around the World's week 10 films Catch up on every week 10 film from Race Around the World.

"And then at the end of the episode, they're like, all right, you're going to this place and two hours later you're on a flight."

Constable is still very much running on "autopilot", having come back from Brazil only one day before the finale.

So, after 100 days across the globe, 10 new films and a shiny prize of an ABC-funded project up his sleeve, he's got one thing on his mind: sleep.

World.title: Flights cancelled, evacuations as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
World.content:
Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in densely populated eastern China on Sunday, meteorological authorities said, after the storm triggered more than 1,000 flight cancellations, evacuations and a top-level alert.

China's east coast has been preparing for the storm's arrival in recent days, with work and transport services suspended in some areas along its predicted path.

The centre of the typhoon moved over the coastline near Yuhuan City in Zhejiang Province at about 5:30 pm (7:30pm AEST), China's National Meteorological Centre said in an online post.

Heavy rains have created a risk of severe flooding in Zhejiang, and authorities have warned of severe landslide risks.

Forecasters predict between 200 and 400 millimetres of rainfall in some areas over the next few days. (Reuters: cnsphoto)

Forecasters in China predicted that areas could see 200–400 millimetres of rainfall over the next few days.

Maximum wind speeds near the centre were more than 150 kilometres per hour at the time it made landfall, the NMC said.

Nearly 1,400 flights in and out of Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Hangzhou's airport in nearby Zhejiang province saw 270 inbound and outbound flights cancelled, the report said.

On Saturday evening, authorities in Zhejiang evacuated 390,000 people in the city of Taizhou. Authorities in Shanghai evacuated more than 30,000 people from riskier areas.

The effects were felt as far away as Hong Kong on China's southern coast, where the weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9 Celsius, caused by warm air pushed over the city by Typhoon Dolphin.

With the storm "moving towards the vicinity of Zhejiang and moving inland, its outer subsiding air will persistently bring extremely hot weather to the territory today to Tuesday", the Hong Kong Observatory said.

Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain and strong winds to Japan's Okinawa before reaching China.

Seven people in Okinawa suffered minor injuries, including a man aged over 100 who was blown over by gusts, fell on the ground and hit his head, according to the island's government.

Strong winds and rain led to thousands of flight cancellations. (AP: Wang Xiang/Xinhua)

By Sunday afternoon, 5,290 households in Okinawa were without electricity, according to regional utility Okinawa Electric Power.

In Taiwan, dozens of ferry services were suspended and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds to the island's north on Sunday.

In the Philippines, five people were rescued and seven remained missing after a landslide that hit three houses in the northern mountain resort city of Baguio on Sunday.

Red alert

China's NMC issued a red typhoon alert — its most severe warning — on Sunday morning, forecasting "extraordinary torrential rain" in some areas of central and eastern Zhejiang.

Heavy precipitation is also expected to fall in Shanghai and parts of Fujian, Anhui and Jiangsu provinces through Monday afternoon, it said.

Typhoon Dolphin was expected to weaken after making landfall while moving in a north-westerly direction over eastern China.

Residents struggled against the strong wind gusts. (AP: Wang Xiang/Xinhua)

In Fujian, nearly 99,000 people were relocated from "risky areas" on Saturday evening ahead of the storm's arrival, state news agency Xinhua reported.

Services on more than 200 ferry routes were suspended in Zhejiang and Fujian, Xinhua said, while work at offshore projects was halted and 474 construction vessels had been called to port by Friday morning.

Some train services in affected areas were also suspended on Sunday to ensure passenger safety, state media reported.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme heat events more frequent and more intense worldwide.

Typhoon Dolphin's arrival in China comes two weeks after Typhoon Noul lashed southern Guangdong province, declared by authorities at the time as the strongest storm to hit China this year.

Three people were killed and hundreds of homes were damaged by Typhoon Noul in the Philippines before it reached China.

AP/AFP

World.title: Police working to determine how long body in suitcase lay by road
World.content:
Police are still working to determine how long a body found in a suitcase by the side of a road in southern NSW had gone undiscovered.

Two members of the public alerted authorities just before 1pm on Sunday after making the grim discovery near Wolgon Road at Oallen, about 60 kilometres south-east of Goulburn.

Commander of the Hume Police District, Superintendent Linda Bradbury, told ABC 702 Sydney they believed the body was that of an adult female.

"We're still conducting efforts to identify the remains," she said.

"That is still underway as they are in a state of decomposition so that will take some time.

"Forensic examination is underway to assist us in identifying how long that suitcase has been there."

Police have confirmed the death is being treated as suspicious.

Police at the scene where a body was found in a suitcase by a road at Oallen in southern NSW. (ABC News.)

Investigating links to missing people

Authorities confirmed that police were investigating potential links between the body and other missing people, after the suitcase was seized for forensic examination.

"We will be conducting a number of inquiries about what may have happened," Superintendent Bradbury told ABC 702.

Oallen is a small village on the Shoalhaven River in the Southern Tablelands, 109km north-east of Canberra and 254km south-west of Sydney.

Superintendent Bradbury said the suitcase was located by Wolgon Road and Oallen Ford Road, which was "not a heavy route for traffic".

"It is a road that is travelled frequently, but it is in a rural-residential area," she said.

Police told the ABC that forensic testing "will take some time" and the homicide squad was involved in the ongoing investigations.

World.title: Big changes for NSW renters as portable bond scheme begins
World.content:
From today, renters moving into selected New South Wales suburbs can transfer their existing bonds to their new rental properties, potentially saving thousands of dollars.

The government's Smart Rental Bonds scheme is now live, but currently it is only available in the Parramatta, Penrith and Central Coast local government areas.

The system is being introduced a year later than expected and it won't be free to use, but the government thinks it will be popular with renters.

What is the scheme?

Smart Rental Bonds is designed to remove one of the financial headaches many renters experience when they are moving from one property to another.

Having been accepted for a rental, they may be required to find thousands of dollars to pay a bond for the new property before their old bond is returned to them.

Shelter NSW CEO John Engeler said the stress of finding cash to cover another bond can be a major barrier to moving.

"It might seem like it's not a big deal, but for people on low and very low incomes, this is a game changer," he said.

John Engeler calls the scheme a "game changer". (Supplied: Homes NSW)

Some tenants have to borrow money, he added, or go without food in order to scrape together another deposit.

To overcome this, Smart Rental Bonds allows renters to transfer their existing bond to their new property via an online portal.

How does it work？

Renters will have to pay a $25 application fee to use the online service, overseen by NSW Fair Trading.

They will have to nominate which bond they would like to transfer, choose where they want it sent, then pay the difference if the new bond is higher.

For example, if the existing bond is $2,400 but the new bond is $2,700, the tenant will need to make a $300 top-up payment in order to transfer it.

If the new bond is cheaper than the existing one, the tenant will be refunded as long as no claim is made against the existing bond.

How do landlords make claims against the bond？

The process of deducting money from a bond will not fundamentally change for the landlord.

If a landlord believes they are owed money due to unpaid rent or damage, they can make a claim against the bond.

If the tenant agrees to the claim, the government will pay the landlord directly and the renter will have to pay the government back within 28 days.

The process for landlords for deducting money from a bond will not change. (ABC News: Jack Ailwood)

If the tenant disputes the claim, the matter can be determined by the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT).

The government will only pay a landlord's claim once there is an agreement with the tenant or an order from NCAT.

Who can use it？

For now, only renters moving into properties in the Parramatta, Penrith and Central Coast local government areas can use Smart Rental Bonds.

Fair Trading Minister Anoulack Chanthivong said the scheme needed to be scaled up gradually.

"You're talking close to a million bonds and $2.3 billion worth of renters' money," he said.

" Having a planned, phased process ensures that the system works smoothly and actually instils trust and confidence. "

Anoulack Chanthivong says there are about a million bonds in NSW worth $2.3 billion. (AAP: Dan Himbrechts)

The government had hoped to deliver the scheme by late 2025, but delayed its launch until mid-2026 to ensure it could roll out smoothly.

Mr Chanthivong said more locations would be added in the coming months.

"If things go well, every renter across New South Wales will have access to Smart Rental Bonds by the end of the year."

Why the fee？

The $25 fee is payable every time a renter wants to transfer their bond.

While the scheme has been welcomed by the Tenants' Union of NSW, the fee has not.

When the government announced the details earlier this year, the Tenants' Union said the $25 charge would disproportionately affect renters on low incomes.

The online rental bond service will cost renters $25. (ABC News)

Mr Chanthivong said the fee would help cover the scheme's administration costs and insisted the government wasn't trying to profit.

"It's a very small investment from renters of $25, which potentially saves them up to $4,000," he said.

Mr Engeler said while he would prefer the scheme to be free, he believed the application fee would be worth it.

"At $25, I think most reasonable people would say that's a lot less of an impediment than $2,500 or what an average four-week bond would be," he said.

"Let's not worry about the cents. We're talking about big dollars."

World.title: Australia news LIVE: Frydenberg reveals he will not appear before royal commission; Coalition accuses Labor of funding ‘ghettoisation’ of migrant communities
World.content:
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has blamed rising rents and low wages on Labor’s migration policies in a sweeping attack on Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, as she accuses the government of planning to bring in an additional million migrants over the next four years.

“Tony Burke isn’t cutting migration ... Labor is lying again. And here’s the worst part. You can’t even trust them to stop at a million. This weak government has never once hit a migration target it set. Not once, in four years,” Hanson wrote in a post to X this morning.

The sledge comes a week after Burke delayed a speech outlining the government’s migration overhaul amid a dispute in cabinet. Hanson said the minister was planning to announce “another million people” migrating to the country.

“They already brought in 1.5 million in four years. That’s why your rent exploded, your pay went backwards, and your kids can’t buy a home. It’s why hospitals are turning away sick people.”

After abruptly delaying the announcement of a migration overhaul last week, Burke is expected to provide more detail in coming days, on a package of new measures to cut the net overseas migration intake to its budget forecast of 225,000 per year.

Nine months after the Bondi massacre enlivened debate over social cohesion, Labor is toying with proposals to rework the skills program to better serve the economy, put stricter rules on working holidaymakers and family reunion visas, and cut work rights from visa overstayers. Polls suggest there is support among voters for tighter controls on migration.

World.title: ‘Shocking’: Body of woman stuffed in suitcase found after ‘weekend drive’, police say
World.content:
A body, believed to be that of a woman, has been found in a “state of decomposition” inside a suitcase near Goulburn in NSW’s Southern Tablelands, police say. Two men on a weekend drive had stopped on the side of Wolgon Road at Oallen, about 60 kilometres south of Goulburn, when they made the “shocking discovery” on Sunday afternoon, according to Hume District Commander Linda Bradbury. The body was found in a suitcase under a pine tree on the fringes of dense bushland, metres from the road, triggering the call to emergency services just before 1pm on Sunday. The body was found on Wolgon Road, south of Goulburn. Google StreetView The body is yet to be formally identified, and it is unclear how long the body had been there.



Officers have established a crime scene under Strike Force Bryton and have seized the suitcase for further examination. The State Crime Command’s Homicide Squad has been sent to Goulburn to assist the investigation. Forensic teams placed evidence markers and photographed the crime scene on Sunday night. Detectives conducted preliminary investigations at the scene, including an initial review of the body, aided by forensics officers. The body was removed from the scene late on Sunday. Bradbury said Wolgon Road was not a heavy route for traffic but was “travelled frequently”. She said the body was in a “state of decomposition”. “Forensic examination is under way to assist us in identifying how long that suitcase has been there,” Bradbury told ABC 702 radio on Monday morning.



“There’s very little we know at this point in time. The investigation is in the early stages, and we really are relying on forensic evidence to tell us a bit more.” Detectives will return to the crime scene on Monday, where they will canvass the road and surrounding bushland for any further evidence or information to assist with the investigation. Police are working to match the remains with any outstanding missing persons on record. Goulburn is 194 kilometres south-west of Sydney via the Hume Highway.

World.title: ‘We’re off to a clunky start’: Kyle Sandilands’ new show begins … with tech issues
World.content:
CultureTV & radioRadio ‘We’re off to a clunky start’: Kyle Sandilands’ new show begins … with tech issues Kayla Olaya August 10, 2026 — 6:39am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Despite a “clunky start”, Kyle Sandilands’ new digital radio show, Kyle Sandilands Live made its debut on Monday morning, with guests including NSW Premier Chris Minns and celebrity psychic John Edwards. “It is live. We’re all here, and it’s a digital mess behind the scenes,” Sandilands said at the start of the show, after cutting in and out through his microphone. “We’re off to a clunky start.” Kyle Sandilands on his new digital radio show. About an hour in, longtime manager and close friend Bruno Bouchet had to reset the entire show due to compounding technological lag. “Bruno now wants to turn the entire system off and reset,” Sandilands said just after 7am, with Bouchet adding: “Everything’s going to go black here. We’re going to lose all audio, all lights. Screens are going to shut down.”



But it wasn’t just tech causing problems. Within the first five minutes of the show, Sandilands introduced Jaimee “Mayo” Blazquez as his executive director, prompting Bouchet to refer to her using an expletive. Sandilands replied jokingly: “Bruno, I made it quite clear to the ensemble cast. This isn’t some potty-mouth all-boys’ club filth nest”. Celebrity psychic John Edwards joined via Zoom during the first 30 minutes of the show, though his feed was impeded by technical issues and different presenters’ microphones talking over him. Sandilands was able to, however, squeeze in a question about whether Edwards had witnessed “anyone giving themselves a fiddle” while travelling through the spirit world. NSW Premier Chris Minns was the show’s first live in-studio guest, with Sandilands recalling recently running into Minns in the Blue Mountains and mistaking him for a “meth head”.



“You know what I like about you?” Sandilands said, after the pair shared a laugh. “People on all sides of politics – Labor, Liberals, One Nation types, the Nationals … you don’t seem very Labor.” Minns replied: “Well, we try and be common sense”. Sandilands’ only political question to the premier was whether he would get rid of e-bikes, or Lime bikes, after he revealed he had gifted one to his 11-year-old son, which had made him start “behaving” by getting him out of the house. Six months ago, the Minns Government announced a crackdown on e-bikes allowing police to seize and crush illegally modified e-bikes.



“When there’s a new technology, like anything, there are people that take it too far,” Minns replied, talking about how rules evolved with use of the technology. Minns then cut a golden ribbon to commemorate the occasion before leaving. Earlier in the show, Sandilands said there would also be a potential call-in from One Nation leader Pauline Hanson, and joked about having Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on as well. Despite costing $99.99 a year – with an upfront payment being the only payment method available – Sandilands said the show is not running s “because of the female militant activist group, the Mad F------ Witches”. “They tried to threaten all the clients. Then apparently, clients pretended to be too scared to advertise to their people, so they stopped paying. They stopped putting ads in the show, and I said, ‘Oh well, screw them.
